children.text: Chapter 1

buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho rājagṛham upaniśritya viharati veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe
children.translated_text: The Blessed Buddha, honored, treated as teacher, respected, and worshiped by kings, royal ministers, wealthy men, townspeople, guild-leaders, caravan-leaders, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, thus venerated by gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, was renowned, of great merit, and a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicines and requisites for sickness. Together with the community of disciples he was dwelling near <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the Bamboo Grove at the Squirrels' Feeding-place.

children.text: tatra bhagavato 'cirābhisaṃbuddhabodher yaśasā ca sarvaloka āpūrṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, the whole world was filled with the fame of the Blessed One, whose awakening to bodhi had only recently taken place.

children.text: atha dakṣiṇāgiriṣu janapade saṃpūrṇo nāma brāhmaṇamahāśālaḥ prativasati āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī
children.translated_text: Now in the country of <s>Dakṣiṇāgiri</s> there lived a very eminent brahmin named <s>Saṃpūrṇa</s>, rich, possessed of great wealth and great enjoyments, with broad and extensive possessions, equal to <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth and rivaling the wealth of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>.

children.text: sa ca śrāddho bhadraḥ kalyāṇāśaya ātmahitaparahitapratipannaḥ kāruṇiko mahātmā dharmakāmaḥ prajāvatsalas tyāgaruciḥ pradānaruciḥ pradānābhirato mahati tyāge vartate ||
children.translated_text: He was faithful, good, of noble intention, devoted to his own welfare and the welfare of others, compassionate, magnanimous, desirous of dharma, affectionate toward his people, fond of giving, fond of gifts, delighting in gifts, and engaged in great liberality.

children.text: yāvad asau sarvapāṣaṇḍikaṃ yajñam ārabdho yaṣṭum yatrānekāni tīrthikaśatasahasrāṇi bhuñjate sma
children.translated_text: At one time he had begun to perform a sacrifice for all sectarians, where many hundreds of thousands of tīrthikas were eating.

children.text: yadā bhagavatā rājā bimbisāraḥ saparivāro vinītaḥ tasya ca vinayād bahūni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi vinayam upagatāni tadā rājagṛhāt pūrṇasya jñātayo 'bhyāgatya pūrṇasya purastād buddhasya varṇaṃ bhāṣayituṃ pravṛttā dharmasya saṃghasya ca
children.translated_text: When King <s>Bimbisāra</s>, together with his retinue, had been disciplined by the Blessed One, and through his discipline many hundreds of thousands of living beings had come under discipline, then <s>Pūrṇa</s>'s relatives came from <s>Rājagṛha</s> and began, in <s>Pūrṇa</s>'s presence, to speak praise of the Buddha, the dharma, and the saṃgha.

children.text: atha pūrṇo brāhmaṇamahāśālo bhagavato guṇasaṃkīrtanaṃ pratiśrutya mahāntaṃ prasādaṃ pratilabdhavān
children.translated_text: Then the great brahmin <s>Pūrṇa</s>, hearing the proclamation of the Blessed One's qualities, obtained great faith.

children.text: tataḥ śaraṇam abhiruhya rājagṛhābhimukhaḥ sthitvā ubhau jānumaṇḍale pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya puṣpāṇi kṣipan dhūpam udakaṃ ca bhagavantam āyācituṃ pravṛttaḥ āgacchatu bhagavān yajñaṃ me anubhavituṃ yajñavāṭam iti
children.translated_text: Then, having gone for refuge, he stood facing <s>Rājagṛha</s>, placed both knees on the ground, scattered flowers, incense, and water, and began to invite the Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One come to enjoy my sacrifice, to the sacrificial enclosure.'

children.text: atha tāni puṣpāṇi buddhānāṃ buddhānubhāvena devatānāṃ ca devatānubhāvenopari bhagavataḥ puṣpamaṇḍapaṃ kṣiptvā tasthuḥ dhūpo 'bhrakūṭavad udakaṃ vaiḍūryaśalākavat ||
children.translated_text: Then those flowers, by the power of the Buddhas and by the power of the deities, rose above the Blessed One and remained there, forming a pavilion of flowers; the incense was like a mass of cloud, and the water like a rod of beryl.

children.text: athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha kuta idaṃ bhadanta nimantraṇam āyātam iti
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with joined palms, asked the Blessed One, 'Venerable sir, from where has this invitation come?'

children.text: bhagavān āha dakṣiṇāgiriṣv ānanda janapade saṃpūrṇo nāma brāhmaṇamahāśālaḥ prativasati tatrāsmābhir gantavyam sajjībhavantu bhikṣava iti
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, 'Ānanda, in the country of <s>Dakṣiṇāgiri</s> there lives a very eminent brahmin named <s>Saṃpūrṇa</s>. We must go there. Let the monks prepare themselves.'

children.text: bhagavān bhikṣusahasraparivṛtto dakṣiṇāgiriṣu janapade cārikāṃ caritvā pūrṇasya brāhmaṇamahāśālasya yajñavāṭasamīpe sthitvā cintām āpede yannvahaṃ pūrṇabrāhmaṇam ṛddhiprātihāryeṇāvarjayeyam iti
children.translated_text: The Blessed One, surrounded by a thousand monks, traveled on alms-tour in the country of <s>Dakṣiṇāgiri</s>; standing near the sacrificial enclosure of the great brahmin <s>Pūrṇa</s>, he thought, 'Suppose I were to win over the brahmin <s>Pūrṇa</s> by a miraculous display of supernormal power.'

children.text: atha bhagavāṃs taṃ bhikṣusahasram antardhāpya ekaḥ pātracarakavyagrahastaḥ pūrṇasamīpe sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One made that thousand monks disappear and stood alone near <s>Pūrṇa</s>, holding his bowl and wandering-staff in his occupied hands.

children.text: atha pūrṇo brāhmaṇamahāśālo bhagavantaṃ dadarśa dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam
children.translated_text: Then the great brahmin <s>Pūrṇa</s> saw the Blessed One adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man, his body shining with the eighty minor characteristics, adorned with a fathom-wide radiance, brighter than a thousand suns, like a moving mountain of jewels, auspicious on every side.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punas tvaritatvaritaṃ bhagavataḥ samīpam upasaṃkramya bhagavantam uvāca svāgataṃ bhagavan niṣīdatu bhagavān kriyatāṃ āsanaparigraho mamānugrahārtham iti
children.translated_text: Having seen him, he quickly and eagerly approached the Blessed One and said to him, 'Welcome, Blessed One. Let the Blessed One sit down; let him accept a seat, out of favor for me.'

children.text: bhagavān āha yadi te parityaktaṃ dīyatām asmin pātra iti
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, 'If it has been given up by you, let it be placed in this bowl.'

children.text: atha pūrṇo brāhmaṇamahāśālaḥ pañcamāṇavakaśataparivṛto bhagavato vividhabhakṣyabhojyakhādyalehyapeyacoṣyādibhir āhārair ārabdhaḥ pātraṃ paripūrayitum
children.translated_text: Then the great brahmin <s>Pūrṇa</s>, surrounded by five hundred young brahmins, began to fill the Blessed One's bowl with various foods: things to chew, eat, bite, lick, drink, and suck, and the like.

children.text: bhagavān api svakāt pātrād bhikṣupātreṣv āhāraṃ saṃkramayati
children.translated_text: The Blessed One, from his own bowl, transferred the food into the bowls of the monks.

children.text: yadā bhagavato viditaṃ pūrṇāni bhikṣusahasrasya pātrāṇīti tadā svapātraṃ pūrṇam ādarśitam
children.translated_text: When the Blessed One knew that the bowls of the thousand monks were full, then he showed his own bowl as full.

children.text: tato bhikṣusahasraṃ pūrṇapātram ardhacandrākāreṇa darśitavān
children.translated_text: Then he displayed the thousand monks with their full bowls in the shape of a half-moon.

children.text: devatābhir apy ākāśasthābhiḥ śabdam udīritam pūrṇāni bhagavato bhikṣusahasrasya ca pātrāṇīti
children.translated_text: The deities standing in the sky also uttered a sound: 'The bowls of the Blessed One and of the thousand monks are full.'

children.text: tataḥ prātihāryadarśanāt pūrṇaḥ prasādajāto mūlanikṛtta iva drumo hṛṣṭatuṣṭapramuditaḥ udagraprītisaumanasyajāto bhagavataḥ pādayor nipatya praṇidhiṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca andhe loke anāyake apariṇāyake buddho bhūyāsam atīrṇānāṃ sattvānāṃ tārayitā amuktānāṃ mocayitā anāśvastānām āśvāsayitā aparinirvṛtānāṃ parinirvāpayiteti ||
children.translated_text: Then, from seeing the miracle, <s>Pūrṇa</s> became filled with faith; like a tree cut at the root, joyful, satisfied, delighted, filled with high joy, gladness, and happiness, he fell at the Blessed One's feet and began to make a vow: 'By this root of good, by this arising of thought, and by this relinquishing of a gift of dharma, may I become a Buddha in the blind world, without guide and without leader, a ferrier of beings who have not crossed, a liberator of those not freed, a comforter of those without comfort, and one who brings to final nirvāṇa those not yet finally nirvāṇized.'

children.text: atha bhagavān pūrṇasya brāhmaṇamahāśālasya hetuparaṃparāṃ karmaparaṃparāṃ ca jñātvā smitaṃ prāvirakārṣīt
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, knowing the succession of causes and the succession of karma of the great brahmin <s>Pūrṇa</s>, made a smile appear.

children.text: dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhān niścārya kāścid adhastād gacchanti kāścid upariṣṭād gacchanti
children.translated_text: It is a rule of things that, at the time when the blessed Buddhas reveal a smile, blue, yellow, red, and white rays issue from their mouth; some go downward and some go upward.

children.text: yā adhastād gacchanti tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanam avīcim arbudaṃ nirarbudaṃ aṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvam utpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaṃ narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakās teṣu śītībhūtā nipatanti ye śītanarakās teṣu uṣṇībhūtā nipatanti
children.translated_text: Those that go downward, having gone to the hells <s>Samjiva</s>, <s>Kalasutra</s>, <s>Samghata</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Maharaurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratapana</s>, <s>Avici</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Atata</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahapadma</s>, fall into the hot hells after becoming cool, and into the cold hells after becoming warm.

children.text: tena teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante
children.translated_text: By that, the special torments of those beings subside.

children.text: teṣām evaṃ bhavati kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ āhosvid anyatropapannā iti
children.translated_text: They think, 'Have we, sirs, died from here, or have we been reborn somewhere else?'

children.text: teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati
children.translated_text: In order to produce faith in them, the Blessed One sends out an apparition.

children.text: teṣāṃ nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavati na hyeva vayaṃ bhavantaḥ itaś cyutāḥ nāpy anyatropapannāḥ api tv ayam apūrvadarśanaḥ sattvaḥ asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti
children.translated_text: Seeing the apparition, they think, 'Indeed, sirs, we have not died from here, nor have we been reborn elsewhere. Rather, this is a being never seen before; through his power our special torments have subsided.'

children.text: te nirmite cittam abhiprasādya tan narakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇanti yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti
children.translated_text: Having made their minds serene toward the apparition, they exhaust the karma that was to be experienced in hell and take rebirth among gods and humans, where they become vessels fit for the truths.

children.text: yā upariṣṭād gacchanti tāś cāturmahārājikāṃs trayastriṃśān yāmāṃs tuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhān apramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān abṛhān atapān sudṛśān sudarśanān akaniṣṭhān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmety udghoṣayanti gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante
children.translated_text: Those rays that go upward, having gone to the gods of the <s>Caturmaharajika</s>, <s>Trayastrimsa</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Tusita</s>, <s>Nirmanarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavasavartin</s>, <s>Brahmakayika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Mahabrahma</s>, <s>Parittabha</s>, <s>Apramanabha</s>, <s>Abhasvara</s>, <s>Parittasubha</s>, <s>Apramanasubha</s>, <s>Subhakrtsna</s>, <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Punyaprasava</s>, <s>Brhatphala</s>, <s>Abrha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudrsa</s>, <s>Sudarsana</s>, and <s>Akanistha</s> realms, proclaim, 'Impermanent, suffering, empty, without self,' and speak two verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane
children.translated_text: 'Begin! Go forth! Apply yourselves in the teaching of the Buddha.

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāram iva kuñjaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Shake off the army of death as an elephant shakes a house of reeds.

children.text: yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati
children.translated_text: For whoever lives heedfully in this dharma and discipline

children.text: prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: will abandon the cycle of birth and bring about the end of suffering.'

children.text: atha tā arciṣas trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātum anvāhiṇḍya bhagavantam eva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti
children.translated_text: Then those rays, having wandered through the great trichiliocosm, follow the Blessed One from behind, exactly behind him.

children.text: tad yadi bhagavān atītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If the Blessed One wishes to predict past karma, they disappear behind the Blessed One.

children.text: anāgataṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati purastād antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the future, they disappear in front of him.

children.text: narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pādatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth in hell, they disappear in the soles of his feet.

children.text: tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pārṣṇyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as an animal, they disappear at his heels.

children.text: pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as a preta, they disappear in his big toe.

children.text: manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati jānunor antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as a human, they disappear at his knees.

children.text: balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the kingship of a mighty wheel-turning king, they disappear in his left palm.

children.text: cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the kingship of a wheel-turning king, they disappear in his right palm.

children.text: devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati nābhyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth among the gods, they disappear at his navel.

children.text: śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati āsye 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the awakening of a disciple, they disappear in his mouth.

children.text: pratyekabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati ūrṇāyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the awakening of a solitary Buddha, they disappear in his urna.

children.text: anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati uṣṇīṣe antardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict unsurpassed perfect awakening, they disappear in his usnisa.

children.text: atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata uṣṇīṣe 'ntarhitāḥ
children.translated_text: Then those rays circumambulated the Blessed One three times to the right and vanished into the Blessed One's usnisa.

children.text: athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ananda</s>, with folded hands, asked the Blessed One:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro vaktrāntarān niṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ
children.translated_text: 'A cluster, varied and painted with a thousand colors, has issued from within your mouth,

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantād divākareṇodayatā yathaiva ||
children.translated_text: by which the quarters all around have been illuminated, just as by the rising sun.'

children.text: gāthāś ca bhāṣate
children.translated_text: And he speaks verses:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā buddhā jagaty uttamahetubhūtāḥ
children.translated_text: 'Buddhas, free from arising, having abandoned wretchedness and pride, the supreme causes in the world,

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ smitam upadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the Conquerors who have conquered their enemies do not show a smile, white as a conch and lotus fiber, without a reason.

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayam adhigamya vīra buddhyā śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām
children.translated_text: At this moment, O hero, having yourself understood by your wisdom the wishes of the listeners, O ascetic, lord of conquerors,

children.text: dhīrābhir munivṛṣa vāgbhir uttamābhir utpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: O bull among sages, dispel with steadfast and excellent words, with auspicious utterances, the doubt that has arisen.

children.text: nākasmāllavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ saṃbuddhāḥ smitam upadarśayanti nāthāḥ
children.translated_text: The perfectly awakened protectors, firm as the lord of mountains in the salt ocean, do not show a smile without cause.

children.text: yasyārthe smitam upadarśayanti dhīrāḥ taṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The crowds of people desire to hear the matter for which the steadfast ones show a smile.'

children.text: bhagavān āha evam etad ānanda evam etat
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, 'So it is, <s>Ananda</s>, so it is.

children.text: nāhetvapratyayam ānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti
children.translated_text: Not without cause and condition, <s>Ananda</s>, do the Tathagatas, Arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas reveal a smile.

children.text: eṣa ānanda pūrṇo brāhmaṇamahāśālaḥ
children.translated_text: This, <s>Ananda</s>, is <s>Purna</s>, a great Brahmin householder.'

children.text: anena kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca trikalpāsaṃkhyeyasamudānītāṃ bodhiṃ samudānīya mahākaruṇāparibhāvitāḥ ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ paripūrya pūrṇabhadro nāma samyaksaṃbuddho bhaviṣyati daśabhir balaiś caturbhir vaiśāradyais tribhir āveṇikaiḥ smṛtyupasthānair mahākaruṇayā ca
children.translated_text: By this root of good, by this arising of thought, and by this relinquishing of a gift of dharma, after accumulating the bodhi amassed through three incalculable kalpas, and after fulfilling the six pāramitās, matured by great compassion, he will become a perfectly awakened Buddha named <s>Pūrṇabhadra</s>, endowed with the ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the three special establishments of mindfulness, and great compassion.

children.text: ayam asya deyadharmo yo mamāntike cittaprasāda iti ||
children.translated_text: This is his gift of dharma: the serene faith of mind that he has toward me.

children.text: bhūyaś cānena citrāṇi kuśalamūlāni samavaropitāni ||
children.translated_text: And by this he has planted many various roots of good.

children.text: tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyaṃ yacchāstāraṃ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāmaḥ śāstāraṃ satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvopaniśritya vihariṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, monks, you should train yourselves thus: 'We shall honor the Teacher, treat him as teacher, respect him, and worship him. Having honored, treated as teacher, respected, worshiped, and relied upon the Teacher, we shall dwell.'

children.text: ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, you should train yourselves.

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced in the Blessed One's speech.

children.text: Chapter 2

buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho vaiśālīm upaniśritya viharati markaṭahradatīre kūṭāgāraśālāyām
children.translated_text: The Blessed Buddha, honored, treated as teacher, respected, and worshiped by kings, royal ministers, wealthy men, townspeople, guild-leaders, caravan-leaders, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, thus venerated by gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, renowned, of great merit, and a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicines and requisites for sickness, was dwelling with the community of disciples near <s>Vaiśālī</s>, in the Hall with the Peaked Roof on the bank of the Monkey Pond.

children.text: atha pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto vaiśālīṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat
children.translated_text: Then, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken bowl and robe, surrounded by a group of monks and preceded by the community of monks, he entered <s>Vaiśālī</s> for alms.

children.text: sāvadānīṃ vaiśālīṃ piṇḍāya caritvā yena siṃhasya senāpater niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ
children.translated_text: Having walked through <s>Vaiśālī</s> for alms with attentive care, he approached the residence of the general <s>Siṃha</s>.

children.text: upasaṃkramya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having approached, he sat down on the seat that had been prepared.

children.text: atha siṃhasya senāpateḥ snuṣā yaśomatī nāma abhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā
children.translated_text: Now the daughter-in-law of the general <s>Siṃha</s>, named <s>Yaśomatī</s>, was beautiful, lovely to behold, and gracious in appearance.

children.text: sā bhagavato vicitralakṣaṇojjvalakāyaṃ dṛṣṭvā atyarthaṃ prasādaṃ labdhavatī
children.translated_text: When she saw the Blessed One's body, radiant with its wondrous marks, she gained exceedingly great serene faith.

children.text: sā śvaśuraṃ papraccha asti kaścid upāyo yenāham apy evaṃguṇayuktā syām iti
children.translated_text: She asked her father-in-law, 'Is there some means by which I too might become endowed with such qualities?'

children.text: atha siṃhasya senāpater etad abhavat udārādhimuktā bateyaṃ dārikā
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to the general <s>Siṃha</s>: 'This young woman is surely of noble aspiration.'

children.text: yadi punar iyaṃ pratyayam āsādayet kuryād anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau praṇidhānam iti viditvoktavān dārike yadi hetuṃ samādāya vartiṣyasi tvam apy evaṃvidhā bhaviṣyasi yādṛśo bhagavān iti ||
children.translated_text: Knowing, 'If she should obtain the supporting condition, she would make a vow for unsurpassed perfect awakening,' he said, 'Girl, if you undertake and follow the cause, you too will become of such a kind as the Blessed One is.'

children.text: tataḥ siṃhena senāpatinā yaśomatyāḥ prasādābhivṛddhyarthaṃ prabhūtaṃ hiraṇyasuvarṇaṃ ratnāni ca dattāni
children.translated_text: Then the general <s>Siṃha</s>, in order to increase <s>Yaśomatī</s>'s serene faith, gave her abundant coined gold, refined gold, and jewels.

children.text: tato yaśomatyā dārikayā bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śvo 'ntargṛhe bhaktenopanimantritaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the girl <s>Yaśomatī</s> invited the Blessed One, together with the community of disciples, to a meal inside the house on the following day.

children.text: adhivāsitaṃ ca bhagavatā tasyā anugrahārtham ||
children.translated_text: And the Blessed One accepted, out of favor for her.

children.text: atha yaśomatī dārikā suvarṇamayāni puṣpāṇi kārayitvā rūpyamayāṇi ratnamayāni prabhūtagandhamālyavilepanasaṃgrahaṃ kṛtvā śatarasam āhāraṃ sajjīkṛtya bhagavato dūtena kālam ārocayati samayo bhadanta sajjaṃ bhaktaṃ yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālaṃ manyata iti
children.translated_text: Then the girl <s>Yaśomatī</s> had flowers made of gold, silver, and jewels prepared, gathered abundant perfumes, garlands, and ointments, made ready food of a hundred flavors, and informed the Blessed One of the time by messenger: 'It is time, venerable sir; the meal is ready, if the Blessed One now thinks it the proper time.'

children.text: atha bhagavān bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto yena siṃhasya senāpater niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, surrounded by a group of monks and preceded by the community of monks, approached the residence of the general <s>Siṃha</s>.

children.text: upasaṃkramya purastād bhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Having approached, he sat down before the community of monks on the seat that had been prepared.

children.text: atha yaśomatī dārikā sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ viditvā śatarasenāhāreṇa svahastaṃ saṃtarpya puṣpāṇi bhagavati kṣeptum ārabdhā
children.translated_text: Then the girl <s>Yaśomatī</s>, knowing that the community of monks headed by the Buddha was comfortably seated, satisfied them with food of a hundred flavors with her own hand and began to cast flowers upon the Blessed One.

children.text: atha tāni puṣpāṇi upari bhagavato ratnakūṭāgāro ratnacchatraṃ ratnamaṇḍapa ivāvasthitam yanna śakyaṃ suśikṣitena karmakāreṇa karmāntevāsinā vā kartum yathāpi tad buddhānāṃ buddhānubhāvena devatānāṃ ca devānubhāvena ||
children.translated_text: Then those flowers remained above the Blessed One as a jeweled peaked pavilion, a jeweled parasol, like a jeweled maṇḍapa, such as could not be made by a well-trained craftsman or by a craftsman's apprentice; for such is the Buddha-power of the Buddhas and the divine power of the deities.

children.text: atha yaśomatī dārikā tad atyadbhutaṃ devamanuṣyāvarjanakaraṃ prātihāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā mūlanikṛtta iva drumaḥ sarvaśarīreṇa bhagavataḥ pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ kartum ārabdhā anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca andhe loke anāyake apariṇāyake buddho bhūyāsam atīrṇānāṃ sattvānāṃ tārayitā amuktānāṃ mocayitā anāśvastānām āśvāsayitā aparinirvṛtānāṃ parinirvāpayiteti ||
children.translated_text: Then the girl <s>Yaśomatī</s>, seeing that utterly marvelous miracle that won over gods and humans, fell with her whole body at the Blessed One's feet like a tree cut at the root and began to make a vow: 'By this root of good, by this arising of thought, and by this relinquishing of a gift of dharma, may I become a Buddha in the blind world, without guide and without leader, a ferrier of beings who have not crossed, a liberator of those not freed, a comforter of those without comfort, and one who brings to final nirvāṇa those not yet finally nirvāṇized.'

children.text: atha bhagavān yaśomatyā dārikāyā hetuparaṃparāṃ karmaparaṃparāṃ ca jñātvā smitaṃ prāvirakārṣīt
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, knowing the succession of causes and the succession of karma of the girl <s>Yaśomatī</s>, made a smile appear.

children.text: dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhān niścārya kāścid adhastād gacchanti kāścid upariṣṭād gacchanti
children.translated_text: Now it is the nature of things that, at the time when the blessed Buddhas make a smile appear, blue, yellow, red, and white rays issue from their mouths; some go downward and some go upward.

children.text: yā adhastād gacchanti tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanam avīcim arbudaṃ nirarbudaṃ aṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvam utpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaṃ narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakāsteṣu śītībhūtā nipatanti ye śītanarakās teṣu uṣṇībhūtā nipatanti
children.translated_text: Those that go downward, having gone to the hells <s>Samjiva</s>, <s>Kalasutra</s>, <s>Samghata</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Maharaurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratapana</s>, <s>Avici</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Atata</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahapadma</s>, fall into the hot hells after becoming cool, and into the cold hells after becoming warm.

children.text: tena teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante
children.translated_text: By that, the special torments of those beings subside.

children.text: teṣām evaṃ bhavati kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ āhosvid anyatropapannā iti
children.translated_text: They think, 'Have we, sirs, died from here, or have we been reborn somewhere else?'

children.text: teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati
children.translated_text: In order to produce faith in them, the Blessed One sends out an apparition.

children.text: teṣāṃ nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavati na hy eva vayaṃ bhavantaḥ itaś cyutāḥ nāpy anyatropapannāḥ api tv ayam apūrvadarśanaḥ sattvaḥ asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti
children.translated_text: Seeing the apparition, they think, 'Indeed, sirs, we have not died from here, nor have we been reborn elsewhere. Rather, this is a being never seen before; through his power our special torments have subsided.'

children.text: te nirmite cittam abhiprasādya tan narakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇanti yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti
children.translated_text: Having made their minds serene toward the apparition, they exhaust the karma that was to be experienced in hell and take rebirth among gods and humans, where they become vessels fit for the truths.

children.text: yā upariṣṭād gacchanti tāś cāturmahārājikāṃs trayastriṃśān yāmāṃs tuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhān apramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān abṛhān atapān sudṛśān sudarśanān akaniṣṭhān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmety udghoṣayanti gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante
children.translated_text: Those rays that go upward, having gone to the gods of the <s>Caturmaharajika</s>, <s>Trayastrimsa</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Tusita</s>, <s>Nirmanarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavasavartin</s>, <s>Brahmakayika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Mahabrahma</s>, <s>Parittabha</s>, <s>Apramanabha</s>, <s>Abhasvara</s>, <s>Parittasubha</s>, <s>Apramanasubha</s>, <s>Subhakrtsna</s>, <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Punyaprasava</s>, <s>Brhatphala</s>, <s>Abrha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudrsa</s>, <s>Sudarsana</s>, and <s>Akanistha</s> realms, proclaim, 'Impermanent, suffering, empty, without self,' and speak two verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane
children.translated_text: 'Begin! Go forth! Apply yourselves in the teaching of the Buddha.

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāram iva kuñjaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Shake off the army of death as an elephant shakes a house of reeds.

children.text: yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati
children.translated_text: For whoever lives heedfully in this dharma and discipline

children.text: prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati
children.translated_text: will abandon the cycle of birth and bring about the end of suffering.'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: atha tā arciṣas trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātum anvāhiṇḍya bhagavantam eva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti
children.translated_text: Then those flames, having wandered through the great trichiliocosm, follow the Blessed One from behind, exactly behind him.

children.text: tad yadi bhagavān atītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If the Blessed One wishes to predict past karma, they disappear behind the Blessed One.

children.text: anāgataṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati purastād antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the future, they disappear in front of him.

children.text: narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pādatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth in hell, they disappear in the soles of his feet.

children.text: tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pārṣṇyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as an animal, they disappear at his heels.

children.text: pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as a preta, they disappear in his big toe.

children.text: manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati jānunor antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as a human, they disappear at his knees.

children.text: balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the kingship of a mighty wheel-turning king, they disappear in his left palm.

children.text: cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the kingship of a wheel-turning king, they disappear in his right palm.

children.text: devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati nābhyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth among the gods, they disappear at his navel.

children.text: śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati āsye 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the awakening of a disciple, they disappear in his mouth.

children.text: pratyekabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati ūrṇāyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the awakening of a solitary Buddha, they disappear in his urna.

children.text: anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati uṣṇīṣe antardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict unsurpassed perfect awakening, they disappear in his usnisa.

children.text: atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata uṣṇīṣe 'ntarhitāḥ
children.translated_text: Then those flames circumambulated the Blessed One three times to the right and vanished into the Blessed One's usnisa.

children.text: athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ananda</s>, with folded hands, asked the Blessed One:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro vaktrāntarān niṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ
children.translated_text: 'A cluster, varied and painted with a thousand colors, has issued from within your mouth,

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantād divākareṇodayatā yathaiva ||
children.translated_text: by which the quarters all around have been illuminated, just as by the rising sun.'

children.text: gāthāś ca bhāṣate
children.translated_text: And he speaks verses:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā buddhā jagaty uttamahetubhūtāḥ
children.translated_text: 'Buddhas, free from arising, having abandoned wretchedness and pride, the supreme causes in the world,

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ smitam upadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the Conquerors who have conquered their enemies do not show a smile, white as a conch and lotus fiber, without a reason.

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayam adhigamya vīra buddhyā śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām
children.translated_text: At this moment, O hero, having yourself understood by your wisdom the wishes of the listeners, O ascetic, lord of conquerors,

children.text: dhīrābhir munivṛṣa vāgbhir uttamābhir utpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: O bull among sages, dispel with steadfast and excellent words, with auspicious utterances, the doubt that has arisen.

children.text: nākasmāl lavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ saṃbuddhāḥ smitam upadarśayanti nāthāḥ
children.translated_text: The perfectly awakened protectors, firm as the lord of mountains in the salt ocean, do not show a smile without cause.

children.text: yasyārthe smitam upadarśayanti dhīrāḥ taṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ
children.translated_text: The crowds of people desire to hear the matter for which the steadfast ones show a smile.'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: bhagavān āha evam etad ānanda evam etat
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, 'So it is, <s>Ananda</s>, so it is.

children.text: nāhetvapratyayam ānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti
children.translated_text: Not without cause and condition, <s>Ananda</s>, do the Tathagatas, Arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas reveal a smile.

children.text: paśyasy ānanda anayā yaśomatyā dārikayā mamaivaṃvidhaṃ satkāraṃ kṛtam
children.translated_text: Do you see, <s>Ananda</s>, the honor of this kind done to me by this girl <s>Yasomati</s>?'

children.text: evaṃ bhadanta
children.translated_text: 'Yes, venerable sir.'

children.text: eṣā ānanda yaśomatī dārikā anena kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca trikalpāsaṃkhyeyasamudānītāṃ bodhiṃ samudānīya mahākaruṇāparibhāvitāḥ ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ paripūrya ratnamatir nāma samyaksaṃbuddho bhaviṣyati daśabhir balaiś caturbhir vaiśāradyais tribhir āveṇikaiḥ smṛtyupasthānair mahākaruṇayā ca
children.translated_text: 'This girl <s>Yasomati</s>, <s>Ananda</s>, by this root of good, by this arising of thought, and by the relinquishing of a gift of dharma, will bring together the awakening accumulated over three incalculable eons; having fulfilled the six perfections suffused with great compassion, she will become a perfectly awakened Buddha named <s>Ratnamati</s>, endowed with the ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the three exclusive foundations of mindfulness, and great compassion.

children.text: ayam asya deyadharmo yo mamāntike cittasyābhiprasāda iti ||
children.translated_text: This is her gift of dharma: the serene faith of her mind in my presence.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: With minds delighted, those monks rejoiced in the Blessed One's speech.

children.text: Chapter 3

buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme ||
children.translated_text: The blessed Buddha, honored, esteemed, respected, and worshiped by kings, royal ministers, wealthy men, townsmen, guild leaders, caravan merchants, gods, <s>nagas</s>, <s>yaksas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garudas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s>, thus revered by gods, <s>nagas</s>, <s>yaksas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garudas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s>, known, possessed of great merit, and receiving robes, alms food, beds, seats, medicines for the sick, and requisites, was dwelling with the community of disciples at <s>Sravasti</s>, in <s>Jeta</s> Grove, in <s>Anathapindada</s>'s park.

children.text: śrāvastyām anyatamaḥ śreṣṭhī prativasati āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī
children.translated_text: In <s>Sravasti</s> there lived a certain guild leader, rich, possessing great wealth and great enjoyments, with extensive and broad possessions, endowed with wealth like <s>Vaisravana</s>'s and rivaling <s>Vaisravana</s>'s wealth.

children.text: tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam
children.translated_text: He took a wife from a family equal to his own.

children.text: sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati
children.translated_text: Together with her he sported, delighted himself, and enjoyed pleasure.

children.text: tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayato na putro na duhitā
children.translated_text: As he sported, delighted himself, and enjoyed pleasure, he had neither a son nor a daughter.

children.text: sa kare kapolaṃ dattvā cintāparo vyavasthitaḥ anekadhanasamuditaṃ me gṛham
children.translated_text: Placing his hand on his cheek, he remained absorbed in thought: 'My house is endowed with abundant wealth,

children.text: na me putro na duhitā
children.translated_text: but I have neither a son nor a daughter.

children.text: mamātyayāt sarvasvāpateyam aputrakam iti kṛtvā rājavidheyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti
children.translated_text: After my death, all this property, being without an heir, will come under the authority of the king.'

children.text: sa śramaṇabrāhmaṇanaimittikasuhṛtsaṃbandhibāndhavair ucyate devatāyācanaṃ kuruṣveti ||
children.translated_text: He was told by ascetics, brahmins, omen-readers, friends, relations, and kinsmen, 'Make supplication to deities.'

children.text: asti caiṣa loke pravādo yadāyācanahetoḥ putrā jāyante duhitaraś ceti
children.translated_text: And there is this saying in the world, that because of supplication sons are born and daughters too.

children.text: tacca naivam
children.translated_text: But that is not so.

children.text: yady evam abhaviṣyat ekaikasya putrasahasram abhaviṣyat tadyathā rājñaś cakravartinaḥ
children.translated_text: If it were so, each person would have a thousand sons, just like a wheel-turning king.

children.text: api tu trayāṇāṃ sthānānāṃ saṃmukhībhāvāt putrā jāyante duhitaraś ca
children.translated_text: Rather, sons and daughters are born from the coming together of three conditions.

children.text: katameṣāṃ trayāṇām
children.translated_text: Which three?

children.text: mātāpitarau raktau bhavataḥ saṃnipatitau
children.translated_text: The mother and father are impassioned and have come together.

children.text: mātā kalyā bhavati ṛtumatī
children.translated_text: The mother is healthy and in her fertile season.

children.text: gandharvaś ca pratyupasthito bhavati
children.translated_text: And a <s>gandharva</s> is present.

children.text: eṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ sthānānāṃ saṃmukhībhāvāt putrā jāyante duhitaraś ca
children.translated_text: From the coming together of these three conditions sons and daughters are born.

children.text: tathā hy asau śramaṇabrāhmaṇanaimittikasuhṛtsaṃbandhibāndhavavipralabdho 'putraḥ putrābhinandī śivavaruṇakuberaśakrabrahmādīn anyāṃś ca devatāviśeṣān āyācate sma
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, deceived by ascetics, brahmins, omen-readers, friends, relations, and kinsmen, that childless man, longing for a son, made supplication to <s>Siva</s>, <s>Varuna</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Sakra</s>, <s>Brahma</s>, and other particular deities.

children.text: tadyathā ārāmadevatā vanadevatāś catvaradevatāḥ śṛṅgāṭakadevatā balipratigrāhikā devatāḥ
children.translated_text: That is, to park deities, forest deities, deities of crossroads, deities of street-corners, and deities who receive offerings.

children.text: sahajāḥ sahadharmikā nityānubandhā api devatā āyācate sma
children.translated_text: He also made supplication to deities who were born together with him, shared his dharma, and constantly accompanied him.

children.text: sa caivam āyācanaparas tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: And he remained intent on supplication in this way.

children.text: anyatamaś ca sattvo 'nyatamasmāt sattvanikāyāc cyutvā tasyāḥ prajāpatyāḥ kukṣim avakrāntaḥ
children.translated_text: Then a certain being, having fallen from a certain class of beings, entered the womb of his wife.

children.text: pañcāveṇikā dharmā ekatye paṇḍitajātīye mātṛgrāme
children.translated_text: There are five special qualities in some women of wise disposition.

children.text: katame pañca
children.translated_text: What are the five?

children.text: raktaṃ puruṣaṃ jānāti viraktaṃ puruṣaṃ jānāti
children.translated_text: She knows a man who is impassioned, and she knows a man who is free from passion.

children.text: kālaṃ jānāti ṛtuṃ jānāti
children.translated_text: She knows the proper time; she knows the fertile season.

children.text: garbham avakrāntaṃ jānāti
children.translated_text: She knows that an embryo has entered the womb.

children.text: yasya sakāśād garbho 'vakrāmati taṃ jānāti
children.translated_text: She knows from whom the embryo has entered.

children.text: dārakaṃ jānāti
children.translated_text: She knows a boy,

children.text: dārikāṃ jānāti
children.translated_text: and she knows a girl.

children.text: saced dārako bhavati dakṣiṇaṃ kukṣiṃ niśritya tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: If it is a boy, he remains resting against the right side of the womb.

children.text: saced dārikā bhavati vāmaṃ kukṣiṃ niśritya tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: If it is a girl, she remains resting against the left side of the womb.

children.text: sā āttamanāttamanāḥ svāmina ārocayati diṣṭyā āryaputra vardhase
children.translated_text: Delighted and joyful, she informed her husband, 'Fortunately, noble son, you are increasing.

children.text: āpannasattvāsmi saṃvṛttā
children.translated_text: I have become pregnant.

children.text: yathā ca me dakṣiṇaṃ kukṣiṃ niśritya tiṣṭhati niyataṃ dārako bhaviṣyatīti
children.translated_text: And since it rests against my right side, it will certainly be a boy.'

children.text: so 'py āttamanāttamanāḥ pūrvakāyam atyunnamayya dakṣiṇaṃ bāhum abhiprasārya udānam udānayati apy evāhaṃ cirakālābhilaṣitaṃ putramukhaṃ paśyeyam
children.translated_text: He too, delighted and joyful, raised the front of his body very high, stretched out his right arm, and uttered this exclamation: 'May I indeed see the face of the son I have long desired!

children.text: jāto me syān nāvajātaḥ
children.translated_text: May he be born to me, and may he not be ill-born.

children.text: kṛtyāni me kurvīta
children.translated_text: May he perform my duties.

children.text: bhṛtaḥ pratibibhṛyāt
children.translated_text: May he support me, having been supported by me.

children.text: dāyād yaṃ pratipadyeta
children.translated_text: May he receive the inheritance.

children.text: kulavaṃśo me cirasthitikaḥ syāt
children.translated_text: May my family line endure for a long time.

children.text: asmākaṃ cāpy atītakālagatānām alpaṃ vā prabhūtaṃ vā dānāni dattvā kṛtyāni kṛtvā asmākaṃ nāmnā dakṣiṇām ādekṣyati idaṃ tayor yatratatropapannayor gacchator anugacchatviti
children.translated_text: And when we too have passed into the past, after giving gifts, whether small or abundant, and performing rites, may he dedicate the offering in our name, saying, "May this follow those two, wherever they have been reborn and wherever they are going."'

children.text: āpannasattvāṃ caināṃ viditvopariprāsādatalagatām ayantritāṃ dhārayati
children.translated_text: Knowing that she was pregnant, he kept her on the upper story of the palace, free from constraint.

children.text: śīte śītopakaraṇair uṣṇe uṣṇopakaraṇair vaidyaprajñaptair āhārair nātitiktair nātyamlair nātilavaṇair nātimadhurair nātikaṭukair nātikaṣāyais tiktāmlalavaṇamadhurakaṭukakaṣāyavivarjitair āhārair hārārdhahāravibhūṣitagātrīm apsarasam iva nandanavanavicāriṇīṃ mañcān mañcaṃ pīṭhāt pīṭham anavatarantīmadharimāṃ bhūmim
children.translated_text: In the cold he provided things suitable for cold, in the heat things suitable for heat, and foods prescribed by physicians, not too bitter, not too sour, not too salty, not too sweet, not too pungent, not too astringent, foods free from excess bitterness, sourness, saltiness, sweetness, pungency, and astringency; with her limbs adorned with necklaces and half-necklaces, like an apsaras wandering in <s>Nandana</s> Grove, not descending from couch to couch or seat to seat to the lower ground,

children.text: na cāsyāḥ kiṃcid amanojñaśabdaśravaṇaṃ yāvad eva garbhasya paripākāya
children.translated_text: and he allowed her to hear no disagreeable sound at all, solely for the maturation of the embryo.

children.text: sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā
children.translated_text: After eight or nine months had passed, she gave birth.

children.text: dārako jātaḥ
children.translated_text: A boy was born,

children.text: abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ
children.translated_text: handsome, lovely to behold, and pleasing.

children.text: janmani cāsya tat kulaṃ nanditam
children.translated_text: At his birth that family was made joyful.

children.text: tasya jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāmeti
children.translated_text: When, at his birth, they had held the birth festival, they set about establishing a name: 'What should the boy's name be?'

children.text: jñātayaḥ ūcuḥ yasmād asya janmani sarvakulaṃ nanditam tasmād bhavatu dārakasya nanda iti nāmeti
children.translated_text: The relatives said, "Since at his birth the whole family has been delighted, let the boy's name be <s>Nanda</s>."

children.text: tasya nanda iti nāma vyavasthāpitam ||
children.translated_text: His name was fixed as <s>Nanda</s>.

children.text: so 'ṣṭābhir dhātrībhir unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍenānyaiś cottaptottaptair upakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ
children.translated_text: He was raised and brought up by eight nurses, with milk, curds, fresh butter, ghee, clarified butter-oil, and other especially warmed requisites.

children.text: āśu vardhate hradastham iva paṅkajam
children.translated_text: He grew quickly, like a lotus standing in a lake.

children.text: yadā mahān saṃvṛttaḥ pañcavarṣaḥ ṣaḍvarṣo vā tadā kusīdaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ paramakusīdaḥ
children.translated_text: When he had grown large, five or six years old, he became indolent, extremely indolent.

children.text: necchati śayanāsanād apy utthātum
children.translated_text: He did not wish to get up even from his bed or seat.

children.text: tena tīkṣṇaniśitabuddhitayā antargṛhasthenaiva śāstrāṇy adhītāni ||
children.translated_text: Because his intellect was sharp and keen, he studied the treatises while remaining inside the house.

children.text: atha śreṣṭhina etad abhavat so 'pi me kadācit karhicid devatārādhanayā putro jātaḥ so 'pi kusīdaḥ paramakusīdaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the merchant thought, "This son of mine too was born at some time, somehow, through propitiating a deity; yet he too is indolent, extremely indolent.

children.text: śayanāsanād api nottiṣṭhate
children.translated_text: He does not rise even from his bed or seat.

children.text: tat kiṃ mamānenedṛgjātīyena putreṇa yo nāma svasthaśarīro bhūtvā paśur iva saṃtiṣṭhatīti ||
children.translated_text: What use have I for such a son, who, though his body is healthy, simply remains like an animal?"

children.text: sa ca śreṣṭhī pūraṇābhiprasannaḥ
children.translated_text: And that merchant was favorably disposed toward <s>Pūraṇa</s>.

children.text: tena ṣaṭ tīrthikāḥ śāstāraḥ svagṛham āhūtāḥ api nāmāyaṃ dārakas teṣāṃ darśanād gauravajātaḥ śayanāsanād api tāvad uttiṣṭhet
children.translated_text: He invited the six sectarian teachers to his house, thinking, "Perhaps, from seeing them, this boy will feel respect and at least rise from his bed or seat."

children.text: atha kusīdo dārakas tāñśāstṝn dṛṣṭvā cakṣuḥsaṃprekṣaṇām api na kṛtavān kaḥ punar vāda utthāsyati vā abhivādayiṣyati vā āsanena vā upanimantrayiṣyati
children.translated_text: But when the indolent boy saw those teachers, he did not even look at them with his eyes; what need to say that he would rise, salute them, or invite them to a seat?

children.text: atha sa gṛhapatis tām evāvasthāṃ dṛṣṭvā suṣṭhutaram utkaṇṭhitaḥ kare kapolaṃ dattvā cintāparo vyavasthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, seeing that very state of affairs, the householder became still more distressed; putting his hand to his cheek, he remained absorbed in thought.

children.text: atrāntare nāsti kiṃcid buddhānāṃ bhagavatām ajñātam adṛṣṭam aviditam avijñātam
children.translated_text: At that moment there is nothing unknown, unseen, unrecognized, or unperceived by the blessed Buddhas.

children.text: dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahākāruṇikānāṃ lokānugrahapravṛttakānām ekārakṣāṇāṃ śamathavipaśyanāvihāriṇāṃ tridamathavastukuśalānāṃ caturoghottīrṇānāṃ caturṛddhipādacaraṇatalasupratiṣṭhitānāṃ caturṣu saṃgrahavastuṣu dīrgharātrakṛtaparicayānāṃ pañcāṅgaviprahīṇānāṃ pañcagatisamatikrāntānāṃ ṣaḍaṅgasamanvāgatānāṃ ṣaṭpāramitāparipūrṇānāṃ saptabodhyaṅgakusumāḍhyānām aṣṭāṅgamārgadeśikānāṃ navānupūrvavihārasamāpattikuśalānāṃ daśabalabalināṃ daśadiksamāpūrṇayaśasāṃ daśaśatavaśavartiprativiśiṣṭānāṃ trī rātres trir divasasya ca buddhacakṣuṣā lokaṃ vyavalokya jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate ko hīyate ko vardhate kaḥ kṛcchraprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃkaṭaprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃbādhaprāptaḥ kaḥ kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasaṃbādhaprāptaḥ ko 'pāyanimnaḥ ko 'pāyapravaṇaḥ ko 'pāyaprāgbhāraḥ kam aham apāyād uddhṛtya svarge mokṣe ca pratiṣṭhāpayeyam
children.translated_text: Indeed, it is the nature of the blessed Buddhas, the greatly compassionate ones who act for the welfare of the world, who have a single protection, who dwell in tranquility and insight, who are skilled in the three means of taming, who have crossed the four floods, whose feet are firmly planted on the four bases of miraculous power, who over a long night have become familiar with the four means of attraction, who have abandoned the five factors, passed beyond the five destinies, are endowed with the six limbs, have fulfilled the six perfections, are rich with the flowers of the seven factors of awakening, teach the eightfold path, are skilled in the attainments of the nine successive abidings, are mighty with the strength of the ten powers, whose fame fills the ten directions, and who are superior to hundreds of tenfold masters: three times by night and three times by day, having surveyed the world with the Buddha-eye, knowledge and vision arise in them: "Who is declining? Who is prospering? Who has fallen into hardship? Who has fallen into danger? Who has fallen into distress? Who has fallen into hardship, danger, and distress? Who is inclined toward the lower realms? Who leans toward the lower realms? Who is sloping toward the lower realms? Whom shall I lift out of the lower realms and establish in heaven and liberation?

children.text: kasya kāmapaṅkanimagnasya hastoddhāram anupradadyām
children.translated_text: "To whom, sunk in the mire of desire, shall I extend a hand to pull him out?

children.text: kam āryadhanavirahitam āryadhanaiśvaryādhipatye pratiṣṭhāpayeyam
children.translated_text: "Whom, bereft of noble wealth, shall I establish in lordship over the sovereignty of noble wealth?

children.text: kasyājñānatimirapaṭalaparyavanaddhanetrasya jñānāñjanaśalākayā cakṣur viśodhayāmi
children.translated_text: "Whose eye, covered by the mass of the darkness of ignorance, shall I clear with the collyrium-stick of knowledge?

children.text: kasyānavaropitāni kuśalamūlānyavaropayeyam
children.translated_text: "Whose unplanted roots of good shall I plant?

children.text: kasyāvaropitāni paripācayeyam
children.translated_text: "Whose planted roots shall I bring to maturity?

children.text: kasya paripakvāni vimocayeyam
children.translated_text: "Whose matured roots shall I liberate?"

children.text: āha ca
children.translated_text: And it is said:

children.text: apyevātikramed velāṃ sāgaro makarālayaḥ
children.translated_text: The ocean, abode of sea-monsters, might perhaps transgress its shore,

children.text: na tu vaineyavatsānāṃ buddho velām atikramet ||
children.translated_text: but the Buddha does not miss the time for the calves who are to be trained.

children.text: paśyati bhagavān ayaṃ dārakaḥ kusīdo maddarśanād vīryam ārapsyate yāvad anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittaṃ pariṇāmayiṣyatīti
children.translated_text: The Blessed One saw, "This indolent boy, from seeing me, will undertake energy, until he turns his mind toward unsurpassed perfect awakening."

children.text: tato bhagavatā tīrthyānāṃ madadarpacchittyarthaṃ dārakasya ca kuśalamūlasaṃjananārthaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhāḥ kanakavarṇamarīcaya utsṛṣṭāḥ yais tad gṛhaṃ samantād avabhāsitam
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, in order to cut off the intoxication and pride of the sectarians and to generate roots of good in the boy, emitted golden-colored rays whose brilliance exceeded that of a thousand suns, and by them that house was illuminated on every side.

children.text: kalpasahasraparibhāvitāś ca maitryaṃśava utsṛṣṭāḥ yair asya spṛṣṭamātraṃ śarīraṃ prahlāditam
children.translated_text: And he emitted rays of loving-kindness cultivated over a thousand eons, by which the boy's body was gladdened as soon as it was touched.

children.text: sa itaś cāmutaś ca prekṣitum ārabdhaḥ kasya prabhāvān mama śarīraṃ prahlāditam iti
children.translated_text: He began to look here and there, thinking, "By whose power has my body been gladdened?"

children.text: tato bhagavān bhikṣugaṇaparivṛtas tad gṛhaṃ praviveśa
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, surrounded by the community of monks, entered that house.

children.text: dadarśa kusīdo buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtamaśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam
children.translated_text: The indolent boy saw the Buddha, the Blessed One, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man, his limbs radiant with the eighty minor marks, adorned with a fathom-wide halo, brighter than a thousand suns, like a moving mountain of jewels, auspicious on every side.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ paraṃ prasādam āpannaḥ
children.translated_text: Having seen him, he became filled with supreme faith.

children.text: sahasā svayam evotthāya bhagavato 'rthe āsanaṃ prajñapayati
children.translated_text: Suddenly he himself rose and prepared a seat for the Blessed One.

children.text: evaṃ cāha etu bhagavān svāgataṃ bhagavataḥ niṣīdatu bhagavān prajñapta evāsana iti
children.translated_text: And he said this: "Let the Blessed One come. Welcome to the Blessed One. Let the Blessed One sit; the seat has indeed been prepared."

children.text: athāsya mātāpitarāv antarjanaś cādṛṣṭapūrvaprabhāvaṃ dṛṣṭvā paramaṃ vismayam āpannāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then his mother and father and the people of the household, seeing a power never seen before, were filled with the highest amazement.

children.text: tataḥ kusīdo dārako harṣavikasitābhyāṃ nayanābhyāṃ bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya
children.translated_text: Then the lazy boy, with eyes opened wide in joy, paid homage at the Blessed One's feet and sat down before him in order to hear the Dharma.

children.text: tasmai bhagavatā anekaprakāraṃ kausīdyasyāvarṇo bhāṣitaḥ vīryārambhasya cānuśaṃsaḥ
children.translated_text: To him the Blessed One spoke in many ways of the blame attaching to laziness and of the benefit of undertaking energetic effort.

children.text: candanamayīṃ cāsya yaṣṭim anuprayacchati imāṃ dāraka yaṣṭim ākoṭayeti
children.translated_text: And he handed him a staff made of sandalwood, saying, 'Boy, strike this staff.'

children.text: sa tām ākoṭayitum ārabdhaḥ
children.translated_text: He began to strike it.

children.text: athāsau yaṣṭir ākoṭyamānā manojñaśabdaśravaṇaṃ karoti vividhāni ca ratnanidhānāni paśyati
children.translated_text: Then, as that staff was being struck, it produced a delightful sound for him to hear, and he saw various stores of jewels.

children.text: tasyaitad abhavat mahān batāyaṃ vīryārambhe viśeṣo yannvahaṃ bhūyasyā mātrayā vīryam ārabheyeti
children.translated_text: It occurred to him, 'Great indeed is this distinction in undertaking energetic effort. What if I were to undertake effort in still greater measure?'

children.text: sa śrāvastyāṃ ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ sārthavāham ātmānam udghoṣya ṣaḍvārān mahāsamudram avatīrṇaḥ
children.translated_text: He had a proclamation made in <s>Sravasti</s>, announced himself as a caravan leader, and six times entered the great ocean.

children.text: tataḥ siddhayānapātreṇa mahāratnasaṃgrahaṃ kṛtvā bhagavān antarniveśane saśrāvakasaṃgho bhojitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after gathering a great collection of jewels with a vessel whose voyage was successful, he fed the Blessed One together with the community of disciples inside his residence.

children.text: anuttarāyāṃ ca samyaksaṃbodhau praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: And he made a vow for unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: atha bhagavān kusīdasya dārakasya hetuparaṃparāṃ karmaparaṃparāṃ ca jñātvā smitaṃ prāvirakārṣīt
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, knowing the succession of causes and the succession of karma for the lazy boy, revealed a smile.

children.text: dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhān niścārya kāścid adhastād gacchanti kāścid upariṣṭād gacchanti
children.translated_text: It is the nature of things that, when the blessed Buddhas reveal a smile, rays of blue, yellow, red, and white issue from their mouths; some go downward and some go upward.

children.text: yā adhastād gacchanti tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanam avīcim arbudaṃ nirarbudaṃ aṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvam utpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaṃ narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakās teṣu śītībhūtā nipatanti ye śītanarakās teṣu uṣṇībhūtā nipatanti tena teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante
children.translated_text: Those that go downward, having gone to the hells <s>Samjiva</s>, <s>Kalasutra</s>, <s>Samghata</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Maharaurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratapana</s>, <s>Avici</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Atata</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahapadma</s>, fall into the hot hells after becoming cool, and into the cold hells after becoming warm. By that, the particular torments of those beings subside.

children.text: teṣām evaṃ bhavati kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ āhosvid anyatropapannā iti
children.translated_text: They think, 'Have we, sirs, died from here, or have we been reborn somewhere else?'

children.text: teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati
children.translated_text: In order to generate serene faith in them, the Blessed One sends forth an apparition.

children.text: teṣāṃ nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavati na hy eva vayaṃ bhavantaḥ itaś cyutāḥ nāpyanyatropapannāḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing the apparition, they think, 'Indeed, sirs, we have not died from here, nor have we been reborn elsewhere.

children.text: api tv ayam apūrvadarśanaḥ sattvaḥ asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti
children.translated_text: Rather, this is a being never seen before; through his power our particular torments have subsided.'

children.text: te nirmite cittam abhiprasādya tan narakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇanti yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti
children.translated_text: Having made their minds serene toward the apparition, they exhaust the karma to be experienced in hell and take rebirth among gods and humans, where they become vessels fit for the truths.

children.text: yā upariṣṭād gacchanti tāś cāturmahārājikāṃs trayastriṃśān yāmāṃs tuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhān apramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān abṛhān atapān sudṛśān sudarśanān akaniṣṭhān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmety udghoṣayanti gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante
children.translated_text: Those rays that go upward, having gone to the gods of the <s>Caturmaharajika</s>, <s>Trayastrimsa</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Tusita</s>, <s>Nirmanarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavasavartin</s>, <s>Brahmakayika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Mahabrahma</s>, <s>Parittabha</s>, <s>Apramanabha</s>, <s>Abhasvara</s>, <s>Parittasubha</s>, <s>Apramanasubha</s>, <s>Subhakrtsna</s>, <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Punyaprasava</s>, <s>Brhatphala</s>, <s>Abrha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudrsa</s>, <s>Sudarsana</s>, and <s>Akanistha</s> realms, proclaim, 'Impermanent, suffering, empty, without self,' and speak two verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane
children.translated_text: 'Begin! Go forth! Apply yourselves in the teaching of the Buddha.

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāram iva kuñjaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Shake off the army of death as an elephant shakes a house of reeds.

children.text: yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati
children.translated_text: For whoever lives heedfully in this Dharma and discipline

children.text: prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati
children.translated_text: will abandon the cycle of birth and bring about the end of suffering.'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: atha tā arciṣas trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātum anvāhiṇḍya bhagavantam eva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti
children.translated_text: Then those rays, having wandered through the great trichiliocosm, follow the Blessed One from behind, exactly behind him.

children.text: tad yadi bhagavān atītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: Now if the Blessed One wishes to predict past karma, they disappear behind the Blessed One.

children.text: anāgataṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati purastād antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the future, they disappear in front of him.

children.text: narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pādatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth in hell, they disappear in the soles of his feet.

children.text: tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pārṣṇyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as an animal, they disappear at his heels.

children.text: pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as a preta, they disappear in his big toe.

children.text: manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati jānunor antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as a human, they disappear at his knees.

children.text: balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict kingship as a mighty wheel-turning king, they disappear in his left palm.

children.text: cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict kingship as a wheel-turning king, they disappear in his right palm.

children.text: devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati nābhyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth among the gods, they disappear at his navel.

children.text: śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati āsye 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the awakening of a disciple, they disappear in his mouth.

children.text: pratyekabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati ūrṇāyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the awakening of a solitary Buddha, they disappear in his urna.

children.text: anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati uṣṇīṣe antardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict unsurpassed perfect awakening, they disappear in his usnisa.

children.text: atha ca tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata uṣṇīṣe 'ntarhitāḥ
children.translated_text: And then those rays circumambulated the Blessed One three times to the right and vanished into the Blessed One's usnisa.

children.text: athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ananda</s>, with folded hands, asked the Blessed One:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro vaktrāntarān niṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ
children.translated_text: 'A cluster, varied and painted with a thousand colors, has issued from within your mouth,

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantād divākareṇodayatā yathaiva ||
children.translated_text: by which the quarters all around have been illuminated, just as by the rising sun.

children.text: gāthāś ca bhāṣate
children.translated_text: And he speaks verses:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā buddhā jagaty uttamahetubhūtāḥ
children.translated_text: Free from renewed becoming, having abandoned misery and pride, the Buddhas, who are the highest cause in the world,

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ smitam upadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Jinas</s>, conquerors of their enemies, do not show a smile, white as a conch or lotus-fiber, without a reason.

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayam adhigamya vīra buddhyā śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām
children.translated_text: Therefore, having yourself understood at once with your heroic wisdom, O hero, O ascetic, O lord of <s>Jinas</s>, for the hearers who desire to know,

children.text: dhīrābhir munivṛṣa vāgbhir uttamābhir utpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: O bull among sages, remove the arisen doubt with your firm, excellent, auspicious words.

children.text: nākasmāllavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ saṃbuddhāḥ smitam upadarśayanti nāthāḥ
children.translated_text: The perfectly awakened lords, firm as the king of mountains rising from the salt ocean, do not show a smile without cause.

children.text: yasyārthe smitam upadarśayanti dhīrāḥ taṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ
children.translated_text: The crowds of people desire to hear the matter for whose sake the steadfast ones show a smile.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: bhagavān āha evam etad ānanda evam etat
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "So it is, <s>Ananda</s>; so it is.

children.text: nāhetvapratyayam ānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti
children.translated_text: Not without cause and condition, <s>Ananda</s>, do <s>Tathagatas</s>, arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas, reveal a smile.

children.text: paśyasy ānanda anena kusīdena dārakeṇa mamaivaṃvidhaṃ satkāraṃ kṛtam
children.translated_text: Do you see, <s>Ananda</s>, that this indolent boy has shown me such honor?"

children.text: evaṃ bhadanta
children.translated_text: "Yes, venerable sir."

children.text: eṣa ānanda kusīdo dārako 'nena kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca trikalpāsaṃkhyeyasamudānītāṃ bodhiṃ samudānīya mahākaruṇāparibhāvitāḥ ṣaṭpāramitāḥ paripūrya atibalavīryaparākramo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho bhaviṣyati daśabhir balaiś caturbhir vaiśāradyais tribhir āveṇikaiḥ smṛtyupasthānair mahākaruṇayā ca
children.translated_text: "This indolent boy, <s>Ananda</s>, through this root of good, through this production of thought and this renunciation of a gift-offering, after gathering the awakening accumulated over three incalculable eons, and after fulfilling the six <s>paramitas</s> (perfections) suffused with great compassion, will become a perfectly awakened Buddha named <s>Atibalaviryaparakrama</s>, endowed with the ten powers, the four confidences, the three special applications of mindfulness, and great compassion.

children.text: ayam asya deyadharmo yo mamāntike cittaprasāda iti ||
children.translated_text: This is his gift-offering: the clarity of faith in his mind toward me."

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasas te ca bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: And those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.

children.text: Chapter 4

buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme ||
children.translated_text: The Buddha, the Blessed One, honored, respected, esteemed, and worshiped by kings, royal ministers, wealthy men, townspeople, guild leaders, caravan merchants, gods, <s>nagas</s>, <s>yakshas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garudas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s>, thus venerated by gods, <s>nagas</s>, <s>yakshas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garudas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s>, known, greatly meritorious, and receiving robes, almsfood, bedding and seats, and medicines and requisites for illness, was dwelling together with the community of disciples at <s>Sravasti</s>, in <s>Jeta</s> Grove, in <s>Anathapindada</s>'s park.

children.text: śrāvastyām anyatamo mahāsārthavāho mahāsamudrād bhagnayānapātra āgataḥ
children.translated_text: In <s>Sravasti</s> a certain great caravan merchant had returned from the great ocean with his ship broken.

children.text: sa dvir api trir api svadevatāyācanaṃ kṛtvā mahāsamudram avatīrṇo bhagnayānapātra evāgataḥ
children.translated_text: A second and even a third time, after making supplication to his own deity, he went down to the great ocean and returned with his ship broken again.

children.text: tato 'sya mahān kheda utpannaḥ
children.translated_text: Then great distress arose in him.

children.text: sa imāṃ cintām āpede ko me upāyaḥ syādyena dhanārjanaṃ kuryām iti
children.translated_text: He fell into this thought: "What means might there be for me by which I could acquire wealth?"

children.text: tasyaitad abhavat ayaṃ buddho bhagavān sarvadevaprativiśiṣṭataraḥ ātmahitaparahitapratipannaḥ kāruṇiko mahādharmakāmaḥ prajāvatsalaḥ yannvaham idānīm asya nāmnā punar api mahāsamudram avatareyam
children.translated_text: It occurred to him, "This Buddha, the Blessed One, is more eminent than all the gods, devoted to his own welfare and the welfare of others, compassionate, greatly desirous of <s>dharma</s> (teaching), and affectionate toward beings. What if I now went down once more into the great ocean in his name?

children.text: siddhayānapātras tv āgaccheyaṃ ced upārdhena dhanenāsya pūjāṃ kuryām iti ||
children.translated_text: And if I should return with my ship successful, I would perform worship for him with half of the wealth."

children.text: sa evaṃ kṛtavyavasāyaḥ punar api mahāsamudram avatīrṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Having formed this resolve, he went down once more into the great ocean.

children.text: buddhānubhāvena ca ratnadvīpaṃ samprāpya mahāratnasaṃgrahaṃ kṛtvā kuśalasvastinā svagṛham anuprāptaḥ
children.translated_text: And through the Buddha's power he reached the jewel-island, gathered a great collection of jewels, and returned safely and happily to his own house.

children.text: sa mārgaśramaṃ prativinodya bhāṇḍaṃ pratyavekṣitum ārabdhaḥ
children.translated_text: After dispelling the fatigue of the road, he began to inspect his goods.

children.text: tasya nānāvicitrāṇi ratnāni dṛṣṭvā mahāṃllābha utpannaḥ
children.translated_text: When he saw the many various and wondrous jewels, great gain arose for him.

children.text: cintayati ca mayā īdṛśānāṃ ratnānāṃ śramaṇasya gautamasya upārdhaṃ dātavyaṃ bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: And he thought, "I will have to give half of jewels such as these to the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>.

children.text: yannvaham etāni svasyāḥ patnyā āyaḥ
children.translated_text: What if I were to entrust these to my own wife?"

children.text: tena kārṣāpaṇadvayena vikrīya bhagavato gandhaṃ dadyām iti
children.translated_text: "Then, having sold enough for two <s>karshapanas</s>, I would give incense to the Blessed One."

children.text: sa kārṣāpaṇadvayenāgaruṃ krītvā jetavanaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: He bought aloe-wood for two <s>karshapanas</s> and went to <s>Jeta</s> Grove.

children.text: tato 'patrapamāṇarūpo dvārakoṣṭhake sthitvāgaruṃ dhūpitavān ||
children.translated_text: Then, being of a shamefaced disposition, he stood in the gateway and burned the aloe-wood incense.

children.text: atha bhagavāṃstad rūpam ṛddhyabhisaṃskāram abhisaṃskṛtavān yena sa dhūpa upari vihāyasam abhyudgamya sarvāṃ ca śrāvastīṃ sphuritvā mahadabhrakūṭavad avasthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One performed such a miraculous transformation that the smoke rose upward into the sky, pervaded all <s>Sravasti</s>, and remained there like a great mass of cloud.

children.text: tasya tad atyadbhutaṃ devamanuṣyāvarjanakaraṃ prātihāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā mahān prasāda utpannaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that extremely wonderful miracle, which attracted gods and humans, great faith arose in him.

children.text: sa svacittaṃ paribhāṣitavān naitan mama pratirūpaṃ syād yad ahaṃ bhagavantaṃ ratnair nābhyarcayeyam iti ||
children.translated_text: He reproached his own mind: "It would not be fitting for me not to honor the Blessed One with the jewels."

children.text: atha tena sārthavāhena bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃgho 'ntarniveśane bhaktenopanimantritaḥ
children.translated_text: Then that caravan merchant invited the Blessed One, together with the community of disciples, to a meal inside his residence.

children.text: tataḥ praṇītenāhāreṇa saṃtarpya mahāratnair avakīrṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after satisfying them with excellent food, he scattered great jewels over them.

children.text: tatas tāni ratnāni upari vihāyasam abhyudgamya mūrdhni bhagavato ratnakūṭāgāro ratnacchatraṃ ratnamaṇḍapaś cāvasthitaḥ yan na śakyaṃ suśikṣitena karmakāreṇa karmāntevāsinā vā kartum yathāpi tad buddhasya buddhānubhāvena devatānāṃ ca devatānubhāvena ||
children.translated_text: Then those jewels rose upward into the sky and remained above the Blessed One's head as a jeweled pavilion, a jeweled parasol, and a jeweled hall, such as could not be made by a well-trained artisan or by an artisan's apprentice, but only by the Buddha's Buddha-power and by the deities' deity-power.

children.text: atha sārthavāho dviguṇajātaprasādas tatpratihāryadarśanān mūlanikṛtta iva drumo bhagavataḥ pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca andhe loke anāyake apariṇāyake buddho bhūyāsam atīrṇānāṃ sattvānāṃ tārayitā amuktānāṃ mocayitā anāśvastānām āśvāsayitā aparinirvṛtānāṃ parinirvāpayiteti ||
children.translated_text: Then the caravan leader, his faith doubled by seeing that miracle, fell at the Blessed One's feet like a tree cut off at the root, and began to make a vow: 'By this root of good, by this arising of thought, and by this relinquishing of a gift of <s>dharma</s>, may I become a Buddha in a blind world, without guide and without leader; may I be the one who ferries beings not yet ferried, releases those not yet released, consoles those not yet consoled, and brings to final nirvāṇa those not yet finally nirvāṇized.'

children.text: atha bhagavāṃs tasya sārthavāhasya hetuparaṃparāṃ karmaparaṃparāṃ ca jñātvā smitaṃ prāviṣkārṣīt
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, knowing the succession of causes and the succession of karma of that caravan leader, displayed a smile.

children.text: dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhān niścārya kāścid adhastād gacchanti kāścid upariṣṭād gacchanti
