children.translated_text: It is indeed the regular nature of things that, at the time when the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, display a smile, rays blue, yellow, red, and white issue from their mouths; some go downward and some go upward.

children.text: yā adhastād gacchanti tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanam avīcim arbudaṃ nirarbudaṃ aṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvam utpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaṃ narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakās teṣu śītībhūtā nipatanti ye śītanarakās teṣūṣṇībhūtā nipatanti
children.translated_text: Those that go downward, having gone to the hells <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s>, fall cool in the hot hells and warm in the cold hells.

children.text: tena teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante
children.translated_text: Through that, the distinctive torments of those beings are calmed.

children.text: teṣām evaṃ bhavati kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ āhosvid anyatropapannā iti
children.translated_text: It occurs to them: 'Good sirs, have we fallen from here, or have we been reborn somewhere else?'

children.text: teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati
children.translated_text: In order to generate faith in them, the Blessed One sends forth an apparition.

children.text: teṣāṃ nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavati na hy eva vayaṃ bhavantaḥ itaś cyutā nāpy anyatropapannāḥ
children.translated_text: When they see the apparition, it occurs to them: 'No indeed, good sirs, we have not fallen from here, nor have we been reborn elsewhere.

children.text: api tv ayam apūrvadarśanaḥ sattvaḥ asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti
children.translated_text: Rather, this being, never seen before, has by his power calmed our distinctive torments.'

children.text: te nirmite cittam abhiprasādya tan narakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇanti yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti
children.translated_text: Having made their minds full of faith in the apparition, they exhaust the karma to be experienced in hell and take rebirth among gods and humans, where they become vessels fit for the truths.

children.text: yā upariṣṭād gacchanti tāś cāturmahārājikāṃs trayastriṃśān yāmāṃs tuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhān apramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān abṛhān atapān sudṛśān sudarśanān akaniṣṭhān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmety udghoṣayanti gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante
children.translated_text: Those rays that go upward, having gone to the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s>, <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, and <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> heavens, to the <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, <s>Parīttābha</s>, <s>Apramāṇābha</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, <s>Abṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods, proclaim, 'Impermanent, suffering, empty, without self,' and speak two verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane
children.translated_text: 'Set yourselves in motion, go forth, apply yourselves to the Buddha's teaching.

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāram iva kuñjaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Shake off the army of Death, as an elephant shakes a reed hut.

children.text: yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati
children.translated_text: For whoever will live heedfully in this <s>dharma-vinaya</s> (teaching and discipline),

children.text: prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati
children.translated_text: having abandoned the cycle of birth and rebirth, will make an end of suffering.'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: atha tā arciṣas trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātum anvāhiṇḍya bhagavantam eva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti
children.translated_text: Then those rays, after wandering through the three-thousand great-thousand world-system, follow behind the Blessed One, right behind him.

children.text: tad yadi bhagavān atītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If the Blessed One wishes to predict past karma, they disappear behind the Blessed One.

children.text: anāgataṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati purastād antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the future, they disappear in front of him.

children.text: narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pādatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth in hell, they disappear in the soles of his feet.

children.text: tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pārṣṇyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as an animal, they disappear in his heels.

children.text: pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as a preta, they disappear in his big toe.

children.text: manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati jānunor antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as a human, they disappear in his knees.

children.text: balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict sovereignty as a powerful wheel-turning king, they disappear in the palm of his left hand.

children.text: cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict sovereignty as a wheel-turning king, they disappear in the palm of his right hand.

children.text: devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati nābhyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth among gods, they disappear in his navel.

children.text: śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati āsye 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the awakening of a disciple, they disappear in his mouth.

children.text: pratyekabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati ūrṇāyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the awakening of a pratyekabuddha, they disappear in the tuft of hair between his brows.

children.text: anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati uṣṇīṣe antardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict unsurpassed perfect awakening, they disappear in his uṣṇīṣa.

children.text: atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata uṣṇīṣe 'ntarhitāḥ
children.translated_text: Then those rays circumambulated the Blessed One three times and disappeared into the Blessed One's uṣṇīṣa.

children.text: athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with his hands joined in reverence, asked the Blessed One:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro vaktrāntarān niṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ
children.translated_text: 'A cluster of many kinds, variegated with a thousand colors, has issued from within your mouth,

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantād divākareṇodayatā yathaiva ||
children.translated_text: by which the directions all around have been illuminated, just as by the sun when it rises.'

children.text: gāthāś ca bhāṣate
children.translated_text: And he speaks verses:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā buddhā jagaty uttamahetubhūtāḥ
children.translated_text: 'The Buddhas, free from arising, rid of wretchedness and pride, being the supreme cause in the world,

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ smitam upadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the Jinas, conquerors of enemies, do not without cause display a smile white as a conch shell or lotus fiber.

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayam adhigamya vīra buddhyā śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām
children.translated_text: At this moment, O hero, having yourself understood by your wisdom what is desired by your listeners, O ascetic, O lord of Jinas,

children.text: dhīrābhir munivṛṣa vāgbhir uttamābhir utpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: remove, O bull among sages, with steadfast, excellent, and auspicious words, the doubt that has arisen.

children.text: nākasmāl lavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ saṃbuddhāḥ smitam upadarśayanti nāthāḥ
children.translated_text: Not without cause do the protectors, the perfectly awakened ones, steadfast as the king of salt-water mountains, display a smile.'

children.text: yasyārthe smitam upadarśayanti dhīrāḥ taṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ
children.translated_text: The crowds of people desire to hear the matter for whose sake the steadfast ones show a smile.

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: bhagavān āha evam etad ānanda evam etat
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "So it is, <s>Ananda</s>; so it is.

children.text: nāhetvapratyayam ānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti
children.translated_text: Not without cause and condition, <s>Ananda</s>, do <s>Tathagatas</s>, arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas reveal a smile.

children.text: paśyasy ānanda anena sārthavāhena mamaivaṃvidhaṃ satkāraṃ kṛtam
children.translated_text: Do you see, <s>Ananda</s>, that this caravan merchant has shown me such honor?

children.text: evaṃ bhadanta
children.translated_text: "Yes, venerable sir."

children.text: eṣa ānanda sārthavāho 'nena kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca trikalpāsaṃkhyeyasamudānītāṃ bodhiṃ samudānīya mahākaruṇāparibhāvitāḥ ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ paripūrya ratnottamo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho bhaviṣyati daśabhir balaiś caturbhir vaiśāradyais tribhir āveṇikaiḥ smṛtyupasthānair mahākaruṇayā ca
children.translated_text: This caravan merchant, <s>Ananda</s>, through this root of good, through this arising of thought and this renunciation of a gift-offering, after gathering the awakening accumulated over three incalculable eons and fulfilling the six <s>paramitas</s> (perfections) suffused with great compassion, will become a perfectly awakened Buddha named <s>Ratnottama</s>, endowed with the ten powers, the four confidences, the three special applications of mindfulness, and great compassion.

children.text: ayam asya deyadharmo yo mamāntike cittasyābhiprasādaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is his gift-offering: the clarity of faith in his mind in my presence."

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: And those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.

children.text: Chapter 5

buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme ||
children.translated_text: The Buddha, the Blessed One, honored, respected, esteemed, and worshiped by kings, royal ministers, wealthy men, townspeople, guild leaders, caravan merchants, gods, <s>nagas</s>, <s>yakshas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garudas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s>, thus venerated by gods, <s>nagas</s>, <s>yakshas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garudas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s>, known, greatly meritorious, and receiving robes, almsfood, bedding and seats, and medicines and requisites for illness, was dwelling together with the community of disciples at <s>Sravasti</s>, in <s>Jeta</s> Grove, in <s>Anathapindada</s>'s park.

children.text: śrāvastyām anyatamo gṛhapatiḥ śreṣṭhī prativasati āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī
children.translated_text: In <s>Sravasti</s> there lived a certain householder and guild leader, rich, very wealthy, of great possessions, with extensive and broad holdings, possessed of <s>Vaisravana</s>'s wealth and rivaling <s>Vaisravana</s>'s wealth.

children.text: tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam
children.translated_text: He brought a wife from a family equal to his own.

children.text: sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati
children.translated_text: Together with her he played, enjoyed himself, and took pleasure.

children.text: tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ gṛhapateḥ patnī āpannasattvā saṃvṛttā
children.translated_text: As that householder played, enjoyed himself, and took pleasure, his wife became pregnant.

children.text: sā navānāṃ māsānām atyayāt prasūtā
children.translated_text: After nine months had passed, she gave birth.

children.text: dārako jāto abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A boy was born, handsome, good-looking, and pleasing.

children.text: tasya jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā vaḍika iti nāmadheyaṃ kṛtavān pitā
children.translated_text: At his birth, after holding a birth-festival, the father gave him the name <s>Vadika</s>.

children.text: vaḍiko dārako 'ṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo dattaḥ aṃsadhātrībhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dhātrībhyām
children.translated_text: The boy <s>Vadika</s> was given to eight nurses: two carrying nurses, two milk nurses, two cleaning nurses, and two play nurses.

children.text: so 'ṣṭābhir dhātrībhir unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍena anyaiś cottaptottaptair upakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ
children.translated_text: He was raised and nurtured by the eight nurses with milk, curds, fresh butter, ghee, the essence of ghee, and other especially heated requisites.

children.text: āśu vardhate hradastham iva paṅkajam
children.translated_text: He grew quickly, like a lotus in a pond.

children.text: yadā mahān saṃvṛttaḥ pañcavarṣaḥ ṣaḍvarṣo vā tadā gurau bhaktiṃ kṛtvā sarvaśāstrāṇi adhītāni
children.translated_text: When he had grown large, five or six years old, he showed devotion to his teacher and studied all the treatises.

children.text: tīkṣṇabuddhitayā śīghraṃ sarvaśāstrasya pāraṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because of his sharp intellect, he quickly reached the far shore of all learning.

children.text: tad anantaraṃ tasya vaḍikasya kiṃcit pūrvajanmakṛtakarmavipākena śarīre kāyikaṃ duḥkhaṃ patitam iti duḥkhī bhūtaś cintāparaḥ sthitaḥ kiṃ pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ mayā yad idaṃ kāyikaṃ duḥkhaṃ mama śarīre jātam
children.translated_text: After that, through the ripening of some deed done in a former birth, bodily pain fell upon <s>Vadika</s>'s body; he became miserable and remained absorbed in thought: "What evil have I done, that this bodily pain has arisen in my body?"

children.text: tataḥ sa vaidyas tasya rogacihnaṃ dṛṣṭvā cikitsāṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the physician, seeing the signs of his disease, began to undertake treatment.

children.text: tathāpi tasya rogaśāntir na bhavati punar vṛddhir bhavati
children.translated_text: Even so, the disease did not become calm; instead it increased again.

children.text: pitā putrasya rogaṃ vṛddhaṃ jātaṃ dṛṣṭvā avaśyaṃ putro mariṣyati yad vaidyenāpi cāsya rogasya cikitsituṃ na śakyate iti mūrcchayā bhūmau patitaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that his son's disease had become worse, the father thought, "Surely my son will die, since even the physician cannot treat this disease of his," and he fell unconscious to the ground.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhūyo 'pi putrasya cintā jātā
children.translated_text: Seeing him, anxiety for his father arose again in the son.

children.text: bhūyo 'pi cintayā mānasī vyathā jātā
children.translated_text: Again, through that anxiety, mental anguish arose in him.

children.text: sa dārako rogī bhūto 'śakyo 'pi vadituṃ kathaṃcit pitaraṃ babhāṣe mā tāta sāhasam
children.translated_text: That boy, being ill and scarcely able even to speak, somehow said to his father, "Father, do not act rashly.

children.text: dhairyam avalambyottiṣṭha
children.translated_text: Take hold of courage and get up.

children.text: mamātyayāśaṅkayā mā bhūs tvam api mādṛśaḥ
children.translated_text: Out of fear for my death, do not become like me yourself.

children.text: mama nāmnā devānāṃ pūjāṃ kuru dānaṃ dehi
children.translated_text: In my name perform worship of the gods and give gifts.

children.text: tato mama svasthā bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: Then I will become well."

children.text: sa gṛhapatir iti putrasya vaca ākarṇya sarvadevebhyaḥ pūjāṃ kṛtavān
children.translated_text: Hearing these words of his son, that householder performed worship for all the gods.

children.text: sarvabrāhmaṇatīrthikaparivrājakebhyo dānaṃ dattavān
children.translated_text: He gave gifts to all the brahmans, sectarian ascetics, and wandering mendicants.

children.text: tathāpi tasya rogaśāntir na bhavati
children.translated_text: Even so, his disease did not become calm.

children.text: tadā tasya mahān mānaso duḥkho 'bhūt
children.translated_text: Then great mental suffering arose in him.

children.text: sarvadeveṣu pūjā kṛtā dāno 'pi dattaḥ pitrā mama tathāpi svasthā na bhavati
children.translated_text: "Worship has been performed to all the gods, and gifts too have been given by my father, yet I do not become well."

children.text: tatas tathāgataguṇān anusmṛtya buddhaṃ namaskāraṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, recollecting the qualities of the <s>Tathagata</s>, he began to bow to the Buddha.

children.text: atrāntare nāsti kiṃcid buddhānāṃ bhagavatām ajñātam adṛṣṭam aviditam avijñātam
children.translated_text: Meanwhile there is nothing unknown, unseen, unrecognized, or unperceived by the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.

children.text: dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahākāruṇikānāṃ lokānugrahapravṛttakānām ekārakṣāṇāṃ śamathavipaśyanāvihāriṇāṃ tridamathavastukuśalānāṃ caturoghottīrṇānāṃ caturṛddhipādacaraṇatalasupratiṣṭhitānāṃ caturṣu saṃgrahavastuṣu dīrgharātrakṛtaparicayānāṃ pañcāṅgaviprahīṇānāṃ pañcagatisamatikrāntānāṃ ṣaḍaṅgasamanvāgatānāṃ ṣaṭpāramitāparipūrṇānāṃ saptabodhyaṅgakusumāḍhyānām aṣṭāṅgamārgadeśikānāṃ navānupūrvavihārasamāpattikuśalānāṃ daśabalabalināṃ daśadiksamāpūrṇayaśasāṃ daśaśatavaśavartiprativiśiṣṭānāṃ trī rātres trir divasasya ca buddhacakṣuṣā lokaṃ vyavalokya jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate ko hīyate ko vardhate kaḥ kṛcchraprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃkaṭaprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃbādhaprāptaḥ kaḥ kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasaṃbādhaprāptaḥ ko 'pāyanimnaḥ ko 'pāyapravaṇaḥ ko 'pāyaprāgbhāraḥ kam aham apāyād uddhṛtya svarge mokṣe ca pratiṣṭhāpayeyam
children.translated_text: Indeed it is the nature of the blessed Buddhas, who are greatly compassionate, active for the benefit of the world, the sole protectors, dwelling in calm and insight, skilled in the three bases of discipline, crossed beyond the four floods, firmly established with the soles of their feet on the four bases of miraculous power, long practiced through the night in the four means of attraction, rid of the five factors, passed beyond the five destinies, endowed with the six factors, perfected in the six <s>paramitas</s> (perfections), rich with the flowers of the seven factors of awakening, teachers of the eightfold path, skilled in the attainments of the nine successive abidings, strong with the ten powers, whose fame fills the ten directions, surpassing those who command hundreds of powers: three times by night and three times by day, surveying the world with the Buddha-eye, knowledge and vision arise: Who is declining? Who is prospering? Who has fallen into hardship? Who has fallen into distress? Who has fallen into constraint? Who has fallen into hardship, distress, and constraint? Who slopes toward the lower realms? Who inclines toward the lower realms? Who is headed down into the lower realms? Whom shall I lift from the lower realms and establish in heaven and liberation?

children.text: kasya kāmapaṅkanimagnasya hastoddhāram anupradadyām
children.translated_text: To whom, sunk in the mud of desire, shall I give the raising of a hand?

children.text: kam āryadhanavirahitam āryadhanaiśvaryādhipatye pratiṣṭhāpayeyam
children.translated_text: Whom, bereft of noble wealth, shall I establish in the lordship and sovereignty of noble wealth?

children.text: kasyājñānatimirapaṭalaparyavanaddhanetrasya jñānāñjanaśalākayā cakṣur viśodhayāmi
children.translated_text: Whose eyes, covered by the mass of the darkness of ignorance, shall I cleanse with the collyrium-stick of knowledge?

children.text: kasyānavaropitāni kuśalamūlāny avaropayeyam
children.translated_text: Whose roots of good, not yet planted, shall I plant?

children.text: kasyāvaropitāni paripācayeyam
children.translated_text: Whose planted roots of good shall I bring to maturity?

children.text: kasya paripakvāni vimocayeyam
children.translated_text: Whose matured roots shall I liberate?

children.text: āha ca
children.translated_text: And it is said:

children.text: apy evātikramed velāṃ sāgaro makarālayaḥ
children.translated_text: The ocean, abode of sea-monsters, might even pass beyond its shore and limit,

children.text: na tu vaineyavatsānāṃ buddho velām atikramet ||
children.translated_text: but the Buddha would not pass beyond the proper time for his trainable calves.

children.text: tato bhagavatā vaḍikasya gṛhapateḥ putrasya tām avasthāṃ dṛṣṭvā sūryasahasrātirekaprabhāḥ kanakavarṇā marīcayaḥ sṛṣṭāḥ yais tad gṛhaṃ samantād avabhāsitam
children.translated_text: Then, when the Blessed One saw that condition of the householder's son <s>Vaḍika</s>, he sent forth golden-colored rays with a splendor exceeding a thousand suns, by which that house was illuminated on every side.

children.text: kalpasahasraparibhāvitāś ca maitryaṃśava utsṛṣṭāḥ yair asya spṛṣṭamātraṃ śarīraṃ prahlāditam
children.translated_text: And he emitted rays of loving-kindness cultivated for a thousand eons, by which his body, as soon as it was touched, was refreshed and gladdened.

children.text: tato bhagavāṃs tasya dvārakoṣṭhakam anuprāptaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One came to his entrance chamber.

children.text: dauvārikapuruṣeṇāsya niveditaṃ bhagavān dvāre tiṣṭhatīti
children.translated_text: His doorkeeper announced to him, 'The Blessed One is standing at the door.'

children.text: atha vaḍikaḥ śreṣṭhiputro labdhaprasādo 'dhigatasamāśvāsa āha praviśatu bhagavān svāgataṃ bhagavate ākāṅkṣāmi bhagavato darśanam iti
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vaḍika</s>, the merchant's son, gaining faith and obtaining reassurance, said, 'Let the Blessed One enter. Welcome to the Blessed One. I long to see the Blessed One.'

children.text: atha bhagavān praviśya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One entered and sat down on the seat that had been prepared.

children.text: niṣadya bhagavān vaḍikam uvāca kiṃ te vaḍika bādhata iti
children.translated_text: After sitting down, the Blessed One said to <s>Vaḍika</s>, 'What is troubling you, <s>Vaḍika</s>?'

children.text: vaḍika uvāca kāyikaṃ ca me duḥkhaṃ cetasikaṃ ceti
children.translated_text: <s>Vaḍika</s> said, 'I have both bodily pain and mental pain.'

children.text: tato 'sya bhagavatā sarvasatveṣu maitryupadiṣṭā ayaṃ te cetasikasya pratipakṣa iti
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One taught him loving-kindness toward all beings, saying, 'This is the antidote for your mental pain.'

children.text: laukikaṃ ca cittam utpādayāmāsa aho bata śakro devendro gandhamādanāt parvatāt kṣīrikām oṣadhīm ānayed iti
children.translated_text: And he produced a worldly thought: 'Ah, may <s>Sakra</s>, lord of the gods, bring the milky medicinal herb from Mount <s>Gandhamadana</s>.'

children.text: sahacittotpādād bhagavataḥ śakro devendro gandhamādanāt parvatāt kṣīrikām oṣadhīm ānīya bhagavate dattavān
children.translated_text: At the very arising of the Blessed One's thought, <s>Sakra</s>, lord of the gods, brought the milky medicinal herb from Mount <s>Gandhamadana</s> and gave it to the Blessed One.

children.text: bhagavatā ca svapāṇinā gṛhītvā vaḍikāya dattā iyaṃ te kāyikasya duḥkhasya paridāhaśamanīti ||
children.translated_text: And the Blessed One took it with his own hand and gave it to <s>Vaḍika</s>, saying, 'This is the calming of the burning of your bodily pain.'

children.text: sa kāyikaṃ prasrabdhisukhaṃ labdhvā bhagavato 'ntike cittaṃ prasādayāmāsa
children.translated_text: Having obtained the bodily happiness of tranquility, he made his mind clear with faith in the presence of the Blessed One.

children.text: prasannacittaś ca rājñaḥ prasenajito nivedya bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaṃ bhojayitvā śatasahasreṇa vastreṇācchādya sarvapuṣpamālyair abhyarcitavān
children.translated_text: And with a mind clear with faith, after informing King <s>Prasenajit</s>, he fed the Blessed One together with the community of disciples, clothed him with cloth worth a hundred thousand, and worshiped him with all kinds of flowers and garlands.

children.text: tataś cetanāṃ puṣṇāti sma praṇidhiṃ ca cakāra anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena yathaivāhaṃ bhagavatā anuttareṇa vaidyarājena cikitsitaḥ evam aham apy anāgate 'dhvani andhe loke anāyake apariṇāyake buddho bhūyāsam atīrṇānāṃ sattvānāṃ tārayitā amuktānāṃ mocayitā anāśvastānām āśvāsayitā aparinirvṛtānāṃ parinirvāpayiteti ||
children.translated_text: Then he nourished his intention and made a vow: 'By this root of good, by this arising of thought, and by this renunciation of a gift-offering, just as I have been treated by the Blessed One, the unsurpassed king of physicians, so may I too in a future time, in a blind world without a guide and without a leader, become a Buddha, a ferrier of beings not yet ferried, a liberator of those not yet liberated, a comforter of those not yet comforted, and one who brings to final nirvana those not yet finally nirvanized.'

children.text: atha bhagavān vaḍikasya dhātuparaṃparāṃ karmaparaṃparāṃ ca jñātvā smitaṃ prāvirakārṣīt
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, knowing <s>Vaḍika</s>'s succession of elements and succession of karma, revealed a smile.

children.text: dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhān niścārya kāścid adhastād gacchanti kāścid upariṣṭād gacchanti
children.translated_text: Indeed it is the nature of things that, at the time when the blessed Buddhas reveal a smile, blue, yellow, red, and white flames issue from their mouths; some go downward and some go upward.

children.text: yā adhastād gacchanti tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanam avīcim arbudaṃ nirarbudaṃ aṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvam utpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaṃ narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakās teṣu śītībhūtā nipatanti ye śītanarakās teṣu uṣṇībhūtā nipatanti tena teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante
children.translated_text: Those that go downward go to the hells: <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s>. In the hot hells they fall as cool; in the cold hells they fall as warm. By that, the distinctive torments of those beings subside.

children.text: teṣām evaṃ bhavati kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ āhosvid anyatropapannā iti
children.translated_text: Then it occurs to them, 'Have we, sirs, fallen away from here, or have we been reborn somewhere else?'

children.text: teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati
children.translated_text: In order to produce faith in them, the Blessed One sends forth an apparition.

children.text: teṣāṃ nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavati na hy eva vayaṃ bhavantaḥ itaś cyutāḥ nāpy anyatropapannāḥ
children.translated_text: When they see the apparition, this occurs to them: "Indeed, sirs, we have not passed away from here, nor have we been reborn elsewhere.

children.text: api tv ayam apūrvadarśanaḥ sattvaḥ asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante
children.translated_text: Rather, this being, never seen before, is such that by his power the special causes of our suffering subside."

children.text: te nirmite cittam abhiprasādya tan narakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇanti yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti
children.translated_text: Having made their minds clear with faith toward the apparition, they exhaust the karma to be experienced in hell and take rebirth among gods and humans, where they become fit vessels for the truths.

children.text: yā upariṣṭād gacchanti tāś cāturmahārājikāṃs trayastriṃśān yāmāṃs tuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhān apramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān abṛhān atapān sudṛśān sudarśanān akaniṣṭhān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmety udghoṣayanti gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante
children.translated_text: Those rays that go upward, after going to the gods of the Four Great Kings, the Thirty-three, the Yāmas, the Tuṣitas, the Nirmāṇaratis, the Paranirmitavaśavartins, the Brahmakāyikas, the Brahmapurohitas, the Mahābrahmās, the Parīttābhas, the Apramāṇābhas, the Ābhāsvaras, the Parīttaśubhas, the Apramāṇaśubhas, the Śubhakṛtsnas, the Anabhrakas, the Puṇyaprasavas, the Bṛhatphalas, the Abṛhas, the Atapas, the Sudṛśas, the Sudarśanas, and the Akaniṣṭha gods, proclaim, "Impermanent, painful, empty, without self," and speak two verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane
children.translated_text: "Begin; go forth; apply yourselves in the Buddha's teaching.

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāram iva kuñjaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Shake off the army of death, as an elephant shakes a reed hut.

children.text: yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati
children.translated_text: For whoever in this <s>dharmavinaya</s> (teaching and discipline) lives heedfully

children.text: prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: will abandon the cycle of birth and bring suffering to an end."

children.text: atha tā arciṣas trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātum anvāhiṇḍya bhagavantam eva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti
children.translated_text: Then those rays, after wandering through the three-thousand great-thousand world-system, follow the Blessed One close behind, again and again.

children.text: tad yadi bhagavān atītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If the Blessed One wishes to predict past karma, they disappear behind the Blessed One.

children.text: anāgataṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati purastād antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the future, they disappear in front of him.

children.text: narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pādatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth in hell, they disappear in the soles of his feet.

children.text: tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pārṣṇyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as an animal, they disappear at his heels.

children.text: pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as a <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost), they disappear in his big toe.

children.text: manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati jānunor antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as a human, they disappear at his knees.

children.text: balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict kingship as a powerful wheel-turning king, they disappear in his left palm.

children.text: cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict kingship as a wheel-turning king, they disappear in his right palm.

children.text: devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati nābhyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth among the gods, they disappear at his navel.

children.text: śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati āsye 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the awakening of a disciple, they disappear in his mouth.

children.text: pratyekabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati ūrṇāyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the awakening of a solitary Buddha, they disappear in his <s>ūrṇā</s>.

children.text: anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati uṣṇīṣe antardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict unsurpassed perfect awakening, they disappear in his <s>uṣṇīṣa</s>.

children.text: atha ca tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata uṣṇīṣe 'ntarhitāḥ
children.translated_text: And then those rays circumambulated the Blessed One three times to the right and vanished into the Blessed One's <s>uṣṇīṣa</s>.

children.text: athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with folded hands, asked the Blessed One:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro vaktrāntarān niṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ
children.translated_text: "A cluster, varied and painted with a thousand colors, has issued from within your mouth,

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantād divākareṇodayatā yathaiva ||
children.translated_text: by which the quarters all around have been illuminated, just as by the rising sun."

children.text: gāthāś ca bhāṣate
children.translated_text: And he speaks verses:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā buddhā jagaty uttamahetubhūtāḥ
children.translated_text: "Free from renewed becoming, having abandoned misery and pride, the Buddhas, who are the supreme cause in the world,

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ smitam upadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Jinas</s>, conquerors of their enemies, do not show a smile, white as a conch or lotus fiber, without a reason.

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayam adhigamya dhīra buddhyā śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām
children.translated_text: Therefore, having yourself understood at once with wise, heroic insight, O hero, O ascetic, O lord of <s>Jinas</s>, for the hearers who desire to know,

children.text: dhīrābhir munivṛṣa vāgbhir uttamābhir utpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: O steadfast bull among sages, remove the arisen doubt with your firm, excellent, auspicious words.

children.text: nākasmāllavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ saṃbuddhāḥ smitam upadarśayanti nāthāḥ
children.translated_text: The perfectly awakened lords, firm as the king of mountains in the salt ocean, do not show a smile without cause.

children.text: yasyārthe smitam upadarśayanti dhīrāḥ taṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The crowds of people desire to hear the matter for whose sake the steadfast ones show a smile."

children.text: bhagavān āha evam etad ānanda evam etat
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>; so it is.

children.text: nāhetvapratyayam ānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti
children.translated_text: Not without cause and condition, <s>Ānanda</s>, do <s>Tathāgatas</s>, arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas reveal a smile.

children.text: paśyasy anena vaḍikena gṛhapatiputreṇa mamaivaṃvidhaṃ satkāraṃ kṛtam
children.translated_text: Do you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, that this householder's son <s>Vaḍika</s> has shown me such honor?"

children.text: evaṃ bhadanta
children.translated_text: "Yes, venerable sir."

children.text: eṣa ānanda vaḍiko gṛhapatiputro 'nena kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca trikalpāsaṃkhyeyasamudānītāṃ bodhiṃ samudānīya mahākaruṇāparibhāvitāḥ ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ paripūrya śākyamunir nāma samyaksaṃbuddho bhaviṣyati daśabhir balaiś caturbhir vaiśāradyais tribhir āveṇikaiḥ smṛtyupasthānair mahākaruṇayā ca
children.translated_text: "This householder's son <s>Vaḍika</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, through this root of good, through this arising of the thought of awakening and this renunciation of a gift-offering, after gathering the awakening accumulated over three incalculable eons and fulfilling the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), suffused with great compassion, will become a perfectly awakened Buddha named <s>Śākyamuni</s>, endowed with the ten powers, the four confidences, the three special applications of mindfulness, and great compassion.

children.text: ayam asya deyadharmo yo mamāntike cittaprasāda iti ||
children.translated_text: This is his gift-offering: clarity of faith in his mind toward me."

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasas te ca bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: And those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.

children.text: Chapter 6

buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme ||
children.translated_text: The Buddha, the Blessed One, honored, highly revered, respected, and worshiped by kings, royal ministers, wealthy men, townspeople, guild leaders, caravan merchants, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, thus worshiped by gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, known as a Buddha, the Blessed One, of great merit and receiving robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicines and requisites for sickness, was dwelling with the community of disciples at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, in the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.

children.text: yadā bhagavāṃl loke notpanna āsīt tadā rājā prasenajit tīrthikadevatārcanaṃ kṛtavān puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanaiḥ
children.translated_text: When the Blessed One had not yet arisen in the world, King <s>Prasenajit</s> had performed worship of sectarian deities with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, and ointments.

children.text: yadā tu bhagavāṃl loke utpannaḥ rājā ca prasenajid daharasūtrodāharaṇena vinīto bhagavacchāsane śraddhāṃ pratilabdhavān tadā prītisaumanasyajātas trir bhagavantam upasaṃkramya dīpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanair abhyarcayati ||
children.translated_text: But when the Blessed One had arisen in the world, and King <s>Prasenajit</s>, trained by the citation of the <s>Daharasūtra</s>, had gained faith in the Blessed One's teaching, then, filled with joy and gladness, he approached the Blessed One three times and worshiped him with lamps, incense, perfumes, garlands, and ointments.

children.text: athānyatama ārāmiko navaṃ padmam ādāya rājñaḥ prasenajito 'rthaṃ śrāvastīṃ praviśati
children.translated_text: Then a certain ārāmika, taking a fresh lotus, entered <s>Śrāvastī</s> for the sake of King <s>Prasenajit</s>.

children.text: tīrthikopāsakena ca dṛṣṭaḥ pṛṣṭaś ca kim idaṃ padmaṃ vikrīṇīṣe sa kathayati āmeti
children.translated_text: He was seen by a sectarian lay devotee and asked, 'Are you selling this lotus?' He said, 'Yes.'

children.text: sa kretukāmo yāvad anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatis taṃ pradeśam anuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He wanted to buy it, until the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> arrived at that place.

children.text: tena tasmād dviguṇena mūlyena vardhitam
children.translated_text: By him the price was raised to twice as much as that.

children.text: tataḥ parasparaṃ vardhamānau yāvacchatasahasraṃ vardhitavantau
children.translated_text: Then, raising the price against one another, they raised it as far as one hundred thousand.

children.text: athārāmikasyaitad abhavat ayam anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatir acañcalaḥ sthirasattvaḥ
children.translated_text: Then it occurred to the ārāmika, 'This householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> is unmoving, a being of firm resolve.

children.text: nūnam atra kāraṇena bhavitavyam iti
children.translated_text: Surely there must be some reason here.'

children.text: tena saṃśayajātena sa tīrthikābhiprasannaḥ puruṣaḥ pṛṣṭaḥ kasyārthe bhavān evaṃ vardhata iti
children.translated_text: With doubt arisen, he asked that man, who was devoted to the sectarians, 'For whose sake, sir, are you bidding so high?'

children.text: sa āha ahaṃ bhagavato nārāyaṇasyārthe iti ||
children.translated_text: He said, 'For the sake of the Blessed <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.'

children.text: anāthapiṇḍada āha ahaṃ bhagavato buddhasyārthe iti
children.translated_text: <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> said, 'For my part, it is for the sake of the Blessed Buddha.'

children.text: ārāmika āha ka eṣa buddho nāmeti tato 'nāthapiṇḍadena vistareṇāsya buddhaguṇā ākhyātāḥ
children.translated_text: The ārāmika said, 'Who is this one called Buddha?' Then <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> described the Buddha's qualities to him in detail.

children.text: tata ārāmiko 'nāthapiṇḍadam āha gṛhapate ahaṃ svayam eva taṃ bhagavantam abhyarcayiṣya iti ||
children.translated_text: Then the ārāmika said to <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, 'Householder, I myself will worship that Blessed One.'

children.text: tato 'nāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatir ārāmikam ādāya yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, taking the ārāmika along, approached the place where the Blessed One was.

children.text: dadarśārāmiko buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam
children.translated_text: The ārāmika saw the Buddha, the Blessed One, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man, his body shining with the eighty secondary marks, adorned with an armspan radiance, with a splendor surpassing a thousand suns, like a moving mountain of jewels, auspicious on every side.

children.text: sahadarśanāc ca ārāmikeṇa tat padmaṃ bhagavati kṣiptam
children.translated_text: And at the very sight of him, the ārāmika threw that lotus toward the Blessed One.

children.text: tataḥ kṣiptamātraṃ śakaṭacakramāṇaṃ bhūtvā upari bhagavataḥ sthitam ||
children.translated_text: Then, as soon as it was thrown, it became the size of a cart wheel and stood above the Blessed One.

children.text: atha sa ārāmikas tat pratihāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā mūlanikṛtta iva drumo bhagavataḥ pādayor nipatya kṛtakarapuṭaś cetanāṃ puṣṇāti praṇidhiṃ ca kartum ārabdhaḥ anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca andhe loke anāyake apariṇāyake buddho bhūyāsam atīrṇānāṃ sattvānāṃ tārayitāmuktānāṃ mocayitā anāśvastānām āśvāsayitā aparinirvṛtānāṃ parinirvāpayiteti ||
children.translated_text: Then that ārāmika, seeing that miracle, fell at the Blessed One's feet like a tree cut off at the root; with joined palms he nourished his intention and began to make a vow: 'By this root of good, by this arising of thought, and by this renunciation of a gift-offering, in a blind world without a guide and without a leader, may I become a Buddha, a ferrier of beings not yet ferried, a liberator of those not yet liberated, a comforter of those not yet comforted, and one who brings to final nirvana those not yet finally nirvanized.'

children.text: atha bhagavāṃs tasyārāmikasya hetuparaṃparāṃ karmaparaṃparāṃ ca jñātvā smitaṃ prāvirakārṣīt
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, knowing that ārāmika's succession of causes and succession of karma, revealed a smile.

children.text: dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhān niścārya kāścid adhastād gacchanti kāścid upariṣṭād gacchanti
children.translated_text: Indeed it is the nature of things that, at the time when the blessed Buddhas reveal a smile, blue, yellow, red, and white flames issue from their mouths; some go downward and some go upward.

children.text: yā adhastād gacchanti tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanam avīcim arbudaṃ nirarbudaṃ aṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvam utpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaṃ narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakās teṣu śītībhūtā nipatanti ye śītanarakās teṣūṣṇībhūtā nipatanti
children.translated_text: Those that go downward go to the hells: <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s>; in the hot hells they fall as cool, and in the cold hells they fall as warm.

children.text: tena teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante
children.translated_text: By that, the particular torments of those beings subside.

children.text: teṣām evaṃ bhavati kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ āhosvid anyatropapannā iti
children.translated_text: It occurs to them, 'Have we, sirs, fallen away from here, or have we been reborn somewhere else?'

children.text: teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati
children.translated_text: In order to generate faith in them, the Blessed One sends forth a created apparition.

children.text: teṣāṃ nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavati na hy eva vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutā nāpy anyatropapannāḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that apparition, it occurs to them, 'No indeed, sirs, we have not fallen away from here, nor have we been reborn elsewhere.

children.text: api tv ayam apūrvadarśanaḥ sattvaḥ asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti
children.translated_text: Rather, this being, never seen before, has caused the particular torments of ours to subside through his power.'

children.text: te nirmite cittam abhiprasādya tan narakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇanti yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti
children.translated_text: They make their minds clear with faith in the apparition, exhaust the karma to be experienced in hell, and take rebirth among gods and humans, where they become vessels for the truths.

children.text: yā upariṣṭād gacchanti tāś cāturmahārājikāṃs trayastriṃśān yāmāṃs tuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhān apramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān abṛhān atapān sudṛśān sudarśanān akaniṣṭhān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmety udghoṣayanti gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante
children.translated_text: Those that go upward, after going to the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> realm, the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, the <s>Yāma</s>, the <s>Tuṣita</s>, the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>, the <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, the <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, the <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, the <s>Parīttābha</s>, the <s>Apramāṇābha</s>, the <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, the <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, the <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, the <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, the <s>Anabhraka</s>, the <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, the <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, the <s>Abṛha</s>, the <s>Atapa</s>, the <s>Sudṛśa</s>, the <s>Sudarśana</s>, and the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s>, proclaim, "Impermanent, painful, empty, without self," and they speak two verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane
children.translated_text: "Set out, go forth, apply yourselves to the Buddha's teaching.

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāram iva kuñjaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Shake off the army of death as an elephant shakes a reed hut.

children.text: yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati
children.translated_text: For whoever lives heedfully in this <s>dharmavinaya</s> (teaching and discipline),

children.text: prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: having abandoned the cycle of birth and rebirth, will make an end of suffering."

children.text: atha tā arciṣas trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātum anvāhiṇḍya bhagavantam eva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti
children.translated_text: Then those rays, after roaming through the three-thousand-great-thousand world-system, follow right behind the Blessed One.

children.text: tad yadi bhagavān atītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: Now, if the Blessed One wishes to predict past karma, they disappear behind the Blessed One.

children.text: anāgataṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati purastād antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the future, they disappear in front of him.

children.text: narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pādatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth in hell, they disappear beneath the soles of his feet.

children.text: tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pārṣṇyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as an animal, they disappear at his heels.

children.text: pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as a preta, they disappear at his big toe.

children.text: manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati jānunor antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as a human, they disappear at his knees.

children.text: balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the kingship of a powerful wheel-turning king, they disappear in his left palm.

children.text: cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the kingship of a wheel-turning king, they disappear in his right palm.

children.text: devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati nābhyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth among the gods, they disappear at his navel.

children.text: śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati āsye 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the awakening of a disciple, they disappear in his mouth.

children.text: pratyekabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati ūrṇāyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the awakening of a solitary Buddha, they disappear in his <s>ūrṇā</s>.

children.text: anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati uṣṇīṣe antardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict unsurpassed perfect awakening, they disappear in his <s>uṣṇīṣa</s>.

children.text: atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata uṣṇīṣe 'ntarhitāḥ
children.translated_text: Then those rays circumambulated the Blessed One three times to the right and vanished into the Blessed One's <s>uṣṇīṣa</s>.

children.text: athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with folded hands, asked the Blessed One:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro vaktrāntarān niṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ
children.translated_text: "A cluster, varied and painted with a thousand colors, has issued from within your mouth,

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantād divākareṇodayatā yathaiva ||
children.translated_text: by which the quarters all around have been illuminated, just as by the rising sun."

children.text: gāthāś ca bhāṣate
children.translated_text: And he speaks verses:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā buddhā jagaty uttamahetubhūtāḥ
children.translated_text: "Free from renewed becoming, having abandoned misery and pride, the Buddhas, who are the supreme cause in the world,

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ smitam upadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Jinas</s>, conquerors of their enemies, do not show a smile, white as a conch or lotus fiber, without a reason.

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayam adhigamya vīra buddhyā śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām
children.translated_text: Therefore, having yourself understood at once with wise, heroic insight, O hero, O ascetic, O lord of <s>Jinas</s>, for the hearers who long to know,

children.text: dhīrābhir munivṛṣa vāgbhir uttamābhir utpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: O steadfast bull among sages, remove the arisen doubt with your firm, excellent, auspicious words.

children.text: nākasmāl lavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ saṃbuddhāḥ smitam upadarśayanti nāthāḥ
children.translated_text: The perfectly awakened lords, firm as the king of mountains in the salt ocean, do not show a smile without cause.

children.text: yasyārthe smitam upadarśayanti dhīrāḥ taṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The crowds of people desire to hear the matter for whose sake the steadfast ones show a smile."

children.text: bhagavān āha evam etad ānanda evam etat
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>; so it is.

children.text: nāhetvapratyayam ānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti
children.translated_text: Not without cause and condition, <s>Ānanda</s>, do <s>Tathāgatas</s>, arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas reveal a smile.

children.text: paśyasy ānanda anenārāmikeṇa prasādajātena mamaivaṃvidhāṃ pūjām kṛtām
children.translated_text: Do you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, that this ārāmika, with faith arisen, has performed such worship for me?"

children.text: evaṃ bhadanta
children.translated_text: "Yes, venerable sir."

children.text: eṣa ārāmiko 'nena kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca trikalpāsaṃkhyeyasamudānītāṃ bodhiṃ samudānīya mahākaruṇāparibhāvitāḥ ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ paripūrya padmottamo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho bhaviṣyati daśabhir balaiś caturbhir vaiśāradyais tribhir āveṇikaiḥ smṛtyupasthānair mahākaruṇayā ca
children.translated_text: "This ārāmika, through this root of good, through this arising of thought, and through the renunciation of a gift-offering, after gathering the awakening accumulated over three incalculable eons and fulfilling the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), suffused with great compassion, will become a perfectly awakened Buddha named <s>Padmottama</s>, endowed with the ten powers, the four confidences, the three special applications of mindfulness, and great compassion.

children.text: ayam asya deyadharmo yo mamāntike cittaprasāda iti ||
children.translated_text: This is his gift-offering: clarity of faith in his mind in my presence."

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: And those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.

children.text: Chapter 7

buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme ||
children.translated_text: The Buddha, the Blessed One, honored, highly revered, respected, and worshiped by kings, royal ministers, wealthy men, townspeople, guild leaders, caravan merchants, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, thus worshiped by gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, known as a Buddha, the Blessed One, of great merit and receiving robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicines and requisites for sickness, was dwelling with the community of disciples at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, in the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.

children.text: tena khalu samayenottarapañcālarājo dakṣiṇapañcālarājena saha prativiruddho babhūva
children.translated_text: At that time the king of northern <s>Pañcāla</s> had become hostile toward the king of southern <s>Pañcāla</s>.

children.text: atha rājā prasenajit kauśalyo yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kauśala</s> approached the place where the Blessed One was.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Having approached, he bowed with his head at the Blessed One's feet and sat down to one side.

children.text: ekānte niṣaṇṇo rājā prasenajit kauśalyo bhagavantam idam avocat bhagavān nāma bhadanta anuttaro dharmarājo vyasanagatānāṃ sattvānāṃ paritrātā anyonyavairiṇāṃ vairapraśamayitā
children.translated_text: Seated in solitude, King <s>Prasenajit Kauśalya</s> said this to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, the Blessed One is called the unsurpassed <s>dharmarāja</s> (king of dharma), the rescuer of beings fallen into calamity, the pacifier of enmity among those hostile to one another.

children.text: ayaṃ cottarapañcālo rājā dakṣiṇapañcālarājena saha prativiruddhaḥ
children.translated_text: And this king of northern <s>Pañcāla</s> is in conflict with the king of southern <s>Pañcāla</s>.

children.text: tau parasparam eva mahājanavipraghātaṃ kurutaḥ
children.translated_text: The two of them are causing harm to many people against each other.

children.text: tayor bhagavān dīrgharātrānugatasya vairasyopaśamaṃ kuryād anukampām upādāyeti
children.translated_text: May the Blessed One, out of compassion, bring about the pacification of their enmity, which has followed them for a long time."

children.text: adhivāsayati bhagavān rājñaḥ prasenajitaḥ kauśalyasya tūṣṇībhāvena
children.translated_text: The Blessed One consented to King <s>Prasenajit Kauśalya</s> by silence.

children.text: atha rājā prasenajit kauśalyo bhagavatas tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvotthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Prasenajit Kauśalya</s>, knowing that the Blessed One had consented by silence, bowed his head to the Blessed One's feet, rose from his seat, and departed.

children.text: atha bhagavāṃs tasyā eva rātrer atyayāt pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya yena vārāṇasī kāśīnāṃ nagaraṃ tena cārikāṃ prakrāntaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, when that very night had passed, dressed in the morning, took his bowl and robe, and set out on a journey toward <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, the city of the <s>Kāśis</s>.

children.text: anupūrveṇa cārikāṃ caran vārāṇasīm anuprāpto vārāṇasyāṃ viharati ṛṣipatane mṛgadāve
children.translated_text: Traveling gradually on his journey, he arrived at <s>Vārāṇasī</s>; he dwelt at <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, in <s>Ṛṣipatana</s>, in the Deer Park.

children.text: yāvat tayor viditaṃ bhagavān asmadvijitam anuprāpta iti
children.translated_text: Eventually those two learned, "The Blessed One has arrived in our territory."

children.text: yāvad bhagavatā ṛddhibalena caturaṅgabalakāyaṃ nirmāyottarapañcālarājas trāsitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, by his power of miraculous ability, created a fourfold army and frightened the king of northern <s>Pañcāla</s>.

children.text: sa bhīta ekaratham abhiruhya bhagavatsakāśam upasaṃkrāntaḥ
children.translated_text: Afraid, he mounted a single chariot and approached the Blessed One's presence.

children.text: tasya bhagavatā vairapraśamāya dharmo deśitaḥ
children.translated_text: The Blessed One taught him the <s>dharma</s> for the pacification of enmity.

children.text: sa taṃ dharmaṃ śrutvā bhagavatsakāśe pravrajitaḥ
children.translated_text: After hearing that <s>dharma</s>, he went forth in the Blessed One's presence.

children.text: tena yujyamānena ghaṭamānena vyāyacchamānena sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam ||
children.translated_text: As he applied himself, exerted himself, and strove, through the abandonment of all defilements he realized <s>arhatship</s>.

children.text: dakṣiṇapañcālarājenāpi bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃghas traimāsyaṃ śatarasenāhāreṇopanimantritaḥ śatasahasreṇa ca vastreṇācchāditaḥ
children.translated_text: The king of southern <s>Pañcāla</s> too invited the Blessed One together with the community of disciples for the three-month rains retreat, provided him with food in the amount of a hundred measures, and clothed him with one hundred thousand garments.

children.text: praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca andhe loke anāyake apariṇāyake buddho bhūyāsam atīrṇānāṃ sattvānāṃ tārayitāmuktānāṃ mocayitā anāśvastānām āśvāsayitā aparinirvṛtānāṃ parinirvāpayiteti ||
children.translated_text: He made a vow: "By this root of good, by this arising of thought, and by this renunciation of a gift-offering, in a blind world without a guide and without a leader, may I become a Buddha, a ferrier of beings not yet ferried, a liberator of those not yet liberated, a comforter of those not yet comforted, and one who brings to final <s>nirvāṇa</s> those not yet finally nirvanized."

children.text: atha bhagavān dakṣiṇapañcālarājasya hetuparaṃparāṃ karmaparaṃparāṃ ca jñātvā smitaṃ prāvirakārṣīt
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, knowing the succession of causes and succession of karma of the king of southern <s>Pañcāla</s>, revealed a smile.

children.text: dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhān niścārya kāścid adhastād gacchanti kāścid upariṣṭād gacchanti
children.translated_text: Indeed it is the nature of things that, at the time when the blessed Buddhas reveal a smile, blue, yellow, red, and white flames issue from their mouths; some go downward and some go upward.

children.text: yā adhastād gacchanti tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanam avīcim arbudaṃ nirarbudaṃ aṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvam utpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaṃ narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakās teṣu śītībhūtā nipatanti ye śītanarakās teṣūṣṇībhūtā nipatanti
children.translated_text: Those that go downward go to the hells: <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s>; in the hot hells they fall as cool, and in the cold hells they fall as warm.

children.text: tena teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante
children.translated_text: By that, the particular torments of those beings subside.

children.text: teṣām evaṃ bhavati kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ āhosvid anyatropapannā iti
children.translated_text: It occurs to them, "Have we, sirs, fallen away from here, or have we been reborn somewhere else?"

children.text: teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati
children.translated_text: In order to generate faith in them, the Blessed One sends forth a created apparition.

children.text: teṣāṃ nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca evaṃ bhavati na hy eva vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutā nāpy anyatropapannāḥ
children.translated_text: And seeing that apparition, it occurs to them, "No indeed, sirs, we have not fallen away from here, nor have we been reborn elsewhere.

children.text: api tv ayam apūrvadarśanaḥ sattvaḥ asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti
children.translated_text: Rather, this being, never seen before, has caused our particular torments to subside through his power."

children.text: te nirmite cittam abhiprasādya tan narakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇanti yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti
children.translated_text: They make their minds clear with faith in the apparition, exhaust the karma to be experienced in hell, and take rebirth among gods and humans, where they become vessels for the truths.

children.text: yā upariṣṭād gacchanti tāś cāturmahārājikāṃs trayastriṃśān yāmāṃs tuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhān apramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān abṛhān atapān sudṛśān sudarśanān akaniṣṭhān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmety udghoṣayanti gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante
children.translated_text: Those that go upward go to the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājikas</s>, <s>Trāyastriṃśas</s>, <s>Yāmas</s>, <s>Tuṣitas</s>, <s>Nirmāṇaratis</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartins</s>, the <s>Brahmakāyikas</s>, <s>Brahmapurohitas</s>, <s>Mahābrahmās</s>, <s>Parīttābhas</s>, <s>Apramāṇābhas</s>, <s>Ābhāsvaras</s>, <s>Parīttaśubhas</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubhas</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsnas</s>, <s>Anabhrakas</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasavas</s>, <s>Bṛhatphalas</s>, <s>Abṛhas</s>, <s>Atapas</s>, <s>Sudṛśas</s>, <s>Sudarśanas</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭhas</s>; having gone there, they proclaim, "Impermanent, suffering, empty, without self," and they speak two verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane
children.translated_text: "Set out, go forth, apply yourselves in the teaching of the Buddha.

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāram iva kuñjaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Shake off the army of death, as an elephant shakes a reed hut.

children.text: yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati
children.translated_text: For whoever will live heedfully in this <s>dharmavinaya</s> (teaching and discipline),

children.text: prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: having abandoned the cycle of birth, will bring about the end of suffering."

children.text: atha tā arciṣas trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātum anvāhiṇḍya bhagavantam eva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti
children.translated_text: Then those flames, having wandered through the three-thousand great-thousand world-system, follow the Blessed One from behind, again and again.

children.text: tad yadi bhagavān atītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If the Blessed One wishes to predict past karma, they disappear behind the Blessed One.

children.text: anāgataṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati purastād antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the future, they disappear in front of him.

children.text: narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pādatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth in hell, they disappear at the soles of his feet.

children.text: tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pārṣṇyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as an animal, they disappear at his heels.

children.text: pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth among the pretas, they disappear in his toes.

children.text: manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati jānunor antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth among humans, they disappear in his knees.

children.text: balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the kingdom of a powerful wheel-turning king, they disappear in his left palm.

children.text: cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the kingdom of a wheel-turning king, they disappear in his right palm.

children.text: devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati nābhyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth among gods, they disappear in his navel.

children.text: śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati āsye 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the awakening of a disciple, they disappear in his mouth.

children.text: pratyekabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati ūrṇāyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the awakening of a solitary Buddha, they disappear in his <s>ūrṇā</s>.

children.text: anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati uṣṇīṣe antardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict unsurpassed perfect awakening, they disappear in his <s>uṣṇīṣa</s>.

children.text: atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata uṣṇīṣe 'ntarhitāḥ
children.translated_text: And then those flames circumambulated the Blessed One three times to the right and vanished into the Blessed One's <s>uṣṇīṣa</s>.

children.text: athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with folded hands, asked the Blessed One:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro vaktrāntarān niṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ
children.translated_text: "A cluster, varied and painted with a thousand colors, has issued from within your mouth,

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantād divākareṇodayatā yathaiva ||
children.translated_text: by which the quarters all around have been illuminated, just as by the rising sun."

children.text: gāthāś ca bhāṣate
children.translated_text: And he speaks verses:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā buddhā jagaty uttamahetubhūtāḥ
children.translated_text: "Free from arising, having abandoned misery and pride, the Buddhas, who are the supreme cause in the world,

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ smitam upadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Jinas</s>, conquerors of their enemies, do not show a smile, white as a conch or lotus fiber, without a reason.

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayam adhigamya vīra buddhyā śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām
children.translated_text: Therefore, having yourself understood at once with wise, heroic insight, O hero, O ascetic, O lord of <s>Jinas</s>, for the hearers who desire to know,

children.text: dhīrābhir munivṛṣa vāgbhir uttamābhirutpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: O steadfast bull among sages, remove the arisen doubt with your firm, excellent, auspicious words.

children.text: nākasmāl lavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ saṃbuddhāḥ smitam upadarśayanti nāthāḥ
children.translated_text: The perfectly awakened lords, firm as the king of mountains in the salt ocean, do not show a smile without cause.

children.text: yasyārthe smitam upadarśayanti dhīrāḥ taṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The crowds of people desire to hear the matter for whose sake the steadfast ones show a smile."

children.text: bhagavān āha evam etad ānanda evam etat
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>; so it is.

children.text: nāhetvapratyayam ānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti
children.translated_text: Not without cause and condition, <s>Ānanda</s>, do <s>Tathāgatas</s>, arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas reveal a smile.

children.text: paśyasy ānanda dakṣiṇapañcālarājena mamaivaṃvidhaṃ satkāraṃ kṛtam
children.translated_text: Do you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, that the king of <s>Dakṣiṇapañcāla</s> has shown me such honor?"

children.text: evaṃ bhadanta
children.translated_text: "Yes, venerable sir."

children.text: eṣa ānanda pañcālarājo 'nena kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca trikalpāsaṃkhyeyasamudānītāṃ bodhiṃ samudānīya mahākaruṇāparibhāvitāḥ ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ paripūrya vijayo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho bhaviṣyati daśabhir balaiś caturbhir vaiśāradyais tribhir āveṇikaiḥ smṛtyupasthānair mahākaruṇayā ca
children.translated_text: "This king of <s>Pañcāla</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, through this root of good, through this arising of thought and this renunciation of a gift-offering, after gathering the awakening accumulated over three incalculable eons and fulfilling the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), suffused with great compassion, will become a perfectly awakened Buddha named <s>Vijaya</s>, endowed with the ten powers, the four confidences, the three special applications of mindfulness, and great compassion.

children.text: ayam asya deyadharmo yo mamāntike cittaprasādaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is his gift-offering: the clarity of faith in his mind toward me."

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: And those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.

children.text: Chapter 8

buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme ||
children.translated_text: The Buddha, the Blessed One, honored, highly revered, respected, and worshiped by kings, royal ministers, wealthy men, townspeople, guild leaders, caravan merchants, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, thus worshiped by gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, known as a Buddha, the Blessed One, of great merit and receiving robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicines and requisites for sickness, was dwelling with the community of disciples at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, in the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.

children.text: tena khalu samayena śrāvastyāṃ dvau śreṣṭhinau
children.translated_text: At that time there were two guild leaders in <s>Śrāvastī</s>.

children.text: tāv anyonyaṃ prativiruddhau babhūvatuḥ
children.translated_text: They were hostile to one another.

children.text: tābhyām ekaḥ pūraṇe 'bhiprasannaḥ dvitīyo buddhe bhagavati
children.translated_text: Of the two, one had faith in <s>Pūraṇa</s>, and the second in the Buddha, the Blessed One.

children.text: tatas tayoḥ parasparaṃ kathāsāṃkathyaviniścaye vartamāne pūraṇopāsaka āha buddhāt pūraṇo viśiṣṭatara iti
children.translated_text: Then, while the two of them were engaged in discussion and debate with each other, the lay devotee of <s>Pūraṇa</s> said, "<s>Pūraṇa</s> is superior to the Buddha."

children.text: buddhopāsaka āha bhagavān samyaksaṃbuddho viśiṣṭatara iti
children.translated_text: The lay devotee of the Buddha said, "The Blessed One, the perfectly awakened Buddha, is superior."

children.text: tatas tābhyāṃ sarvasvāpaharaṇe bandhanikṣepaḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the two of them made a wager involving the forfeiture of all their property.

children.text: yāvad rājñaḥ prasenajitaḥ śrutam
children.translated_text: Eventually King <s>Prasenajit</s> heard of it.

children.text: tenāmātyānām ājñā dattā tayor mīmāṃsā kartavyeti
children.translated_text: He gave an order to his ministers: "An inquiry into those two is to be made."

children.text: tatas tair amātyaiḥ sarvavijite ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kāritam saptame divase buddhatīrthikopāsakayor mīmāṃsā bhaviṣyati ye cādbhutāni draṣṭukāmās te āgacchantv iti
children.translated_text: Then those ministers had a bell proclamation made throughout the whole realm: "On the seventh day there will be an inquiry between the lay devotee of the Buddha and the lay devotee of the sectarians. Let those who wish to see marvels come."

children.text: tataḥ saptame divase vistīrṇāvakāśe pṛthivīpradeśe 'nekeṣu prāṇiśatasahasreṣu saṃnipatiteṣu gaganatale cānekeṣu devatāsahasreṣu saṃnipatiteṣu gomayamaṇḍalake kﾱpte sarvagandhamālyeṣūpahṛteṣu pūrvataraṃ tīrthikopāsakena satyopayācanaṃ kṛtam yena satyena pūraṇaprabhṛtayaḥ ṣaṭ śāstāro loke śreṣṭhāḥ anena satyenemāni puṣpāṇi ayaṃ ca dhūpaḥ idaṃ ca pānīyaṃ tān upagacchantv iti ||
children.translated_text: Then, on the seventh day, when many hundreds of thousands of beings had assembled on a broad, open piece of ground, and many thousands of deities had assembled in the sky, when a circle of cow dung had been prepared and every kind of perfume and garland had been offered, the sectarian devotee first made an invocation of truth: "By the truth that the six teachers beginning with <s>Pūraṇa</s> are the best in the world, by this truth may these flowers, this incense, and this water go to them."

children.text: tato mahājanakāyena kilakilāprakṣveḍoccair nādo muktaḥ yam abhivīkṣya tīrthyopāsakas tuṣṇībhūto maṅkubhūtaḥ srastaskandho 'dhomukho niṣpratibhānaḥ pradhyānaparamaḥ kare kapolaṃ dattvā cintāparo vyavasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the great crowd let out a loud cry of shouting and exclamation. Seeing this, the sectarian devotee became silent, embarrassed, his shoulders drooping, his face downcast, speechless, sunk in dejection; placing his cheek in his hand, he stood absorbed in thought.

children.text: tato bhagavacchrāvakeṇa harṣotkaṇṭhajātena prasādavikasitābhyāṃ nayanābhyām ekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇajānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya satyopayācanaṃ kṛtam yena satyena bhagavān sarvasattvānām agryaḥ anena satyenemāni puṣpāṇi dhūpa udakaṃ bhagavantam upagacchantv iti
children.translated_text: Then the disciple of the Blessed One, filled with longing born of joy, with eyes opened wide by faith, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee on the ground, and made an appeal to truth: "By the truth that the Blessed One is foremost among all beings, by this truth may these flowers, incense, and water go to the Blessed One."

children.text: evaṃ pravyāhṛtamātre tāni puṣpāṇi haṃsapaṅktir ivākāśe jetavanābhimukhaṃ samprasthitāni dhūpo 'bhrakūṭavat udakaṃ vaiḍūryaśalākavat
children.translated_text: As soon as this had been spoken, those flowers set out through the sky toward <s>Jetavana</s> like a row of swans; the incense went like a mass of cloud, and the water like a rod of beryl.

children.text: atha sa mahājanakāyas tat prātihāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā kilakilāprakṣveḍoccaiḥśabdaṃ kurvaṃs teṣāṃ samprasthitānāṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanubaddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then that great crowd of people, seeing the miracle, making shrill cries and loud shouts, followed along behind them as they proceeded.

children.text: tatas tāni puṣpāṇi bhagavata upari sthitāni dhūpa udakaṃ cāgrataḥ
children.translated_text: Then those flowers stood above the Blessed One, while the incense and water were in front.

children.text: tataḥ sa mahājanakāyo labdhaprasādo bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya
children.translated_text: Then that great crowd of people, having gained faith, bowed at the Blessed One's feet and sat down before him to hear the Dharma.

children.text: teṣāṃ bhagavān idaṃ sūtraṃ bhāṣate sma
children.translated_text: The Blessed One taught them this sūtra:

children.text: tisra imā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo 'graprajñaptayaḥ
children.translated_text: "There are these three foremost declarations, brahmins and householders.

children.text: katamās tisraḥ buddhe agraprajñaptiḥ dharme saṃghe agraprajñaptiḥ
children.translated_text: What are the three? The foremost declaration concerning the Buddha; the foremost declaration concerning the Dharma and the Saṃgha.

children.text: buddhe agraprajñaptiḥ katamā ye kecid brāhmaṇagṛhapatayaḥ sattvā apadā vā dvipadā vā bahupadā vā rūpiṇo vā arūpiṇo vā saṃjñino vā asaṃjñino vā naivasaṃjñino nāsaṃjñinaḥ tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhas teṣām agra ākhyātaḥ
children.translated_text: What is the foremost declaration concerning the Buddha? Whatever beings there are, brahmins and householders, whether footless, two-footed, or many-footed, whether formed or formless, percipient, non-percipient, or neither percipient nor non-percipient, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the arhat, the perfectly awakened Buddha, is declared foremost among them.

children.text: ye kecid buddhe 'bhiprasannāḥ agre te 'bhiprasannāḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever people have full faith in the Buddha have full faith in the foremost.
