children.text: teṣām agre 'bhiprasannānām agra eva vipākaḥ pratikāṅkṣitavyo deveṣu vā devabhūtānāṃ manuṣyeṣu vā manuṣyabhūtānām
children.translated_text: For those who have full faith in the foremost, the foremost result is to be expected, whether among gods when they have become gods, or among humans when they have become humans.

children.text: iyam ucyate brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo buddhe agraprajñaptiḥ
children.translated_text: This, brahmins and householders, is called the foremost declaration concerning the Buddha.

children.text: dharme agraprajñaptiḥ katamā ye kecid dharmāḥ saṃskṛtā vā asaṃskṛtā vā virāgo dharmas teṣām agra ākhyātaḥ
children.translated_text: What is the foremost declaration concerning the Dharma? Whatever dharmas there are, conditioned or unconditioned, the Dharma of dispassion is declared foremost among them.

children.text: ye kecid dharme 'bhiprasannā agre te 'bhiprasannāḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever people have full faith in the Dharma have full faith in the foremost.

children.text: teṣām agre 'bhiprasannānām agra eva vipākaḥ pratikāṅkṣitavyo deveṣu vā devabhūtānāṃ manuṣyeṣu vā manuṣyabhūtānām
children.translated_text: For those who have full faith in the foremost, the foremost result is to be expected, whether among gods when they have become gods, or among humans when they have become humans.

children.text: iyam ucyate brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo dharme agraprajñaptiḥ
children.translated_text: This, brahmins and householders, is called the foremost declaration concerning the Dharma.

children.text: saṃgheṣu agraprajñaptiḥ katamā ye kecit saṃghā vā gaṇā vā pūgā vā pariṣado vā tathāgataśrāvakasaṃghas teṣām agra ākhyātaḥ
children.translated_text: What is the foremost declaration concerning communities? Whatever communities, groups, assemblies, or gatherings there are, the community of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s disciples is declared foremost among them.

children.text: ye kecit saṃghe 'bhiprasannāḥ agre te 'bhiprasannāḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever people have full faith in the Saṃgha have full faith in the foremost.

children.text: teṣām agre 'bhiprasannānām agra eva vipākaḥ pratikāṅkṣitavyo deveṣu vā devabhūtānāṃ manuṣyeṣu vā manuṣyabhūtānām
children.translated_text: For those who have full faith in the foremost, the foremost result is to be expected, whether among gods when they have become gods, or among humans when they have become humans.

children.text: iyam ucyate brāhmaṇagṛhapatayaḥ saṃghe agraprajñaptiḥ
children.translated_text: This, brahmins and householders, is called the foremost declaration concerning the Saṃgha."

children.text: asmin khalu dharmaparyāye bhāṣyamāṇe teṣāṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnāṃ kaiścid buddhadharmasaṃgheṣu prasādaḥ pratilabdhaḥ kaiściccharaṇagamanaśikṣāpadāni gṛhītāni kaiścit pravrajya idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikaraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam
children.translated_text: While this Dharma discourse was being taught, some of those brahmins and householders gained faith in the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṃgha; some undertook the refuge-going and the training precepts; and some, having gone forth, understood this very five-spoked wheel of saṃsāra to be unstable though moving, and, overcoming all courses of conditioned things as having the nature of falling, breaking apart, changing, and being destroyed, realized arhatship through the abandoning of all defilements.

children.text: tena ca tīrthyopāsakena tathāgatāntike prasādaḥ pratilabdhaḥ
children.translated_text: And that sectarian lay devotee gained faith in the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: tato mūlanikṛtta iva drumaḥ bhagavataḥ pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca andhe loke anāyake apariṇāyake buddho bhūyāsam atīrṇānāṃ sattvānāṃ tārayitā amuktānāṃ mocayitā anāśvastānām āśvāsayitā aparinirvṛtānāṃ parinirvāpayiteti ||
children.translated_text: Then, like a tree cut off at the root, he fell at the Blessed One's feet and began to make a vow: "By this root of good, by this arising of thought, and by this renunciation of a gift-offering, in a blind world without a guide and without a leader, may I become a Buddha, a ferrier of beings not yet ferried, a liberator of those not yet liberated, a comforter of those not yet comforted, and one who brings to final nirvana those not yet finally nirvanized."

children.text: atha bhagavāṃs tasya tīrthikopāsakasya hetuparaṃparāṃ karmaparaṃparāṃ ca jñātvā smitaṃ prāvirakārṣīt
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, knowing the succession of causes and succession of karma of that sectarian lay devotee, revealed a smile.

children.text: dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhān niścārya kāścid adhastād gacchanti kāścid upariṣṭād gacchanti
children.translated_text: Indeed it is the nature of things that, at the time when the blessed Buddhas reveal a smile, blue, yellow, red, and white flames issue from their mouths; some go downward and some go upward.

children.text: yā adhastād gacchanti tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanam avīcim arbudaṃ nirarbudaṃ aṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvam utpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaṃ narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakāsteṣu śītībhūtā nipatanti ye śītanarakās teṣūṣṇībhūtā nipatanti
children.translated_text: Those that go downward go to the hells: <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s>; in the hot hells they fall as cool, and in the cold hells they fall as warm.

children.text: tena teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante
children.translated_text: By that, the particular torments of those beings subside.

children.text: teṣām evaṃ bhavati kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ āhosvid anyatropapannā iti
children.translated_text: It occurs to them, "Have we, sirs, fallen away from here, or have we been reborn somewhere else?"

children.text: teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati
children.translated_text: In order to generate faith in them, the Blessed One sends forth a created apparition.

children.text: teṣāṃ nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavati na hy eva vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutā nāpy anyatropapannāḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that apparition, it occurs to them, "No indeed, sirs, we have not fallen away from here, nor have we been reborn elsewhere."

children.text: api tv ayam apūrvadarśanaḥ sattvaḥ asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti
children.translated_text: Rather, this being, never seen before, has caused the particular torments of ours to subside through his power.

children.text: te nirmite cittam abhiprasādya tan narakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇanti yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti
children.translated_text: They make their minds clear with faith in the apparition, exhaust the karma to be experienced in hell, and take rebirth among gods and humans, where they become vessels for the truths.

children.text: yā upariṣṭād gacchanti tāś cāturmahārājikāṃs trayastriṃśān yāmāṃs tuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhān apramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān abṛhān atapān sudṛśān sudarśanān akaniṣṭhān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmety udghoṣayanti gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante
children.translated_text: Those that go upward go to the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājikas</s>, the <s>Trāyastriṃśas</s>, the <s>Yāmas</s>, the <s>Tuṣitas</s>, the <s>Nirmāṇaratis</s>, the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartins</s>, the <s>Brahmakāyikas</s>, the <s>Brahmapurohitas</s>, the <s>Mahābrahmās</s>, the gods of limited radiance, immeasurable radiance, and streaming radiance, the gods of limited beauty, immeasurable beauty, and complete beauty, the cloudless gods, the producers of merit, the great-fruit gods, the <s>Abṛhas</s>, the <s>Atapas</s>, the <s>Sudṛśas</s>, the <s>Sudarśanas</s>, and the <s>Akaniṣṭhas</s>; having gone there, they proclaim, "Impermanent, suffering, empty, without self," and they speak two verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane
children.translated_text: "Begin! Go forth! Apply yourselves to the Buddha's teaching.

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāram iva kuñjaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Shake off the army of death, as an elephant shakes a reed hut.

children.text: yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati
children.translated_text: For whoever in this <s>dharmavinaya</s> (teaching and discipline) lives heedfully

children.text: prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: will abandon the cycle of birth and bring suffering to an end."

children.text: atha tā arciṣas trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātum anvāhiṇḍya bhagavantam eva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti
children.translated_text: Then those flames, having wandered through the three-thousand great-thousand world system, follow directly behind the Blessed One.

children.text: tad yadi bhagavān atītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If the Blessed One wishes to predict past karma, they disappear behind the Blessed One.

children.text: anāgataṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati purastād antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the future, they disappear in front.

children.text: narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pādatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth in hell, they disappear at the soles of his feet.

children.text: tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pārṣṇyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as an animal, they disappear at his heels.

children.text: pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as a preta, they disappear at his big toe.

children.text: manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati jānunor antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as a human, they disappear at his knees.

children.text: balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict kingship as a powerful wheel-turning monarch, they disappear in his left palm.

children.text: cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict kingship as a wheel-turning monarch, they disappear in his right palm.

children.text: devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati nābhyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth among the gods, they disappear at his navel.

children.text: śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati āsye 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the awakening of a disciple, they disappear in his mouth.

children.text: pratyekabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati ūrṇāyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the awakening of a solitary Buddha, they disappear in his <s>ūrṇā</s>.

children.text: anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati uṣṇīṣe antardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict unsurpassed perfect awakening, they disappear in his <s>uṣṇīṣa</s>.

children.text: atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata uṣṇīṣe 'ntarhitāḥ
children.translated_text: Then those flames circumambulated the Blessed One three times to the right and vanished into the Blessed One's <s>uṣṇīṣa</s>.

children.text: athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with folded hands, asked the Blessed One:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro vaktrāntarān niṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ
children.translated_text: "A cluster, varied and painted with a thousand colors, has issued from within your mouth,

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantād divākareṇodayatā yathaiva ||
children.translated_text: by which the quarters all around have been illuminated, just as by the rising sun.

children.text: gāthāś ca bhāṣate
children.translated_text: And he speaks verses:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā buddhā jagaty uttamahetubhūtāḥ
children.translated_text: "Free from renewed becoming, having abandoned misery and pride, the Buddhas, who are the supreme cause in the world,

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ smitam upadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Jinas</s>, conquerors of their enemies, do not show a smile, white as a conch or lotus fiber, without a reason.

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayam adhigamya vīra buddhyā śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām
children.translated_text: Therefore, having yourself understood at once with wise, heroic insight, O hero, O ascetic, O lord of <s>Jinas</s>, for the hearers who desire to know,

children.text: dhīrābhir munivṛṣa vāgbhir uttamābhir utpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: O steadfast bull among sages, remove the arisen doubt with your firm, excellent, auspicious words.

children.text: nākasmāl lavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ saṃbuddhāḥ smitam upadarśayanti nāthāḥ
children.translated_text: The perfectly awakened lords, firm as the king of mountains in the salt ocean, do not show a smile without cause.

children.text: yasyārthe smitam upadarśayanti dhīrāḥ taṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The crowds of people desire to hear the matter for whose sake the steadfast ones show a smile."

children.text: bhagavān āha evam etad ānanda evam etat
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>; so it is.

children.text: nāhetvapratyayam ānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti
children.translated_text: Not without cause and condition, <s>Ānanda</s>, do <s>Tathāgatas</s>, arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas reveal a smile.

children.text: paśyasy ānanda anena tīrthikopāsakena mamaivaṃvidhaṃ satkāraṃ kṛtam
children.translated_text: Do you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, that this sectarian lay devotee has shown me such honor?"

children.text: evaṃ bhadanta
children.translated_text: "Yes, venerable sir."

children.text: eṣa ānanda tīrthopāsako 'nena kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca trikalpāsaṃkhyeyasamudānītāṃ bodhiṃ samudānīya mahākaruṇāparibhāvitāḥ ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ paripūrya acalo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho bhaviṣyati daśabhir balaiś caturbhir vaiśāradyais tribhir āveṇikaiḥ smṛtyupasthānair mahākaruṇayā ca
children.translated_text: "This sectarian lay devotee, <s>Ānanda</s>, through this root of good, through this arising of the thought and this renunciation of a gift-offering, after gathering the awakening accumulated over three incalculable eons and fulfilling the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), suffused with great compassion, will become a perfectly awakened Buddha named <s>Acala</s>, endowed with the ten powers, the four confidences, the three special applications of mindfulness, and great compassion.

children.text: ayam asya deyadharmo yo mamāntike cittaprasāda iti ||
children.translated_text: This is his gift-offering: clarity of faith in his mind toward me."

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: And those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.

children.text: Chapter 9

buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme
children.translated_text: The Buddha, the Blessed One, honored, highly revered, respected, and worshiped by kings, royal ministers, wealthy men, townspeople, guild leaders, caravan merchants, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, thus worshiped by gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, known as a Buddha, the Blessed One, of great merit and receiving robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicines and requisites for sickness, was dwelling with the community of disciples at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, in the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.

children.text: tena khalu samayena rājā prasenajit kauśalo rājā ca ajātaśatruḥ ubhāv apy etau parasparaṃ viruddhau babhūvatuḥ
children.translated_text: At that time King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s> and King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, these two, had become hostile to one another.

children.text: atha rājā ajātaśatruś caturaṅgabalakāyaṃ saṃnahya hastikāyam aśvakāyaṃ rathakāyaṃ pattikāyaṃ rājānaṃ prasenajitaṃ kauśalam abhiniryāto yuddhāya ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, having arrayed his fourfold army, the elephant corps, cavalry, chariot corps, and infantry, marched out against King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s> for battle.

children.text: aśrauṣīd rājā prasenajit kauśalaḥ rājā ajātaśatruś caturaṅgabalakāyaṃ saṃnahya hastikāyam aśvakāyaṃ rathakāyaṃ pattikāyaṃ ca abhiniryāto yuddhāyeti
children.translated_text: King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s> heard, "King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, having arrayed his fourfold army, the elephant corps, cavalry, chariot corps, and infantry, has marched out for battle."

children.text: śrutvā ca caturaṅgabalakāyaṃ saṃnahya hastikāyam aśvakāyaṃ rathakāyaṃ pattikāyaṃ rājānam ajātaśatruṃ pratyabhiniryāto yuddhāya
children.translated_text: And when he heard it, having arrayed his fourfold army, the elephant corps, cavalry, chariot corps, and infantry, he marched out in response against King <s>Ajātaśatru</s> for battle.

children.text: atha rājñā ajātaśatruṇā rājñaḥ prasenajitaḥ kauśalasya sarvo hastikāyaḥ paryastaḥ aśvakāyo rathakāyaḥ pattikāyaḥ paryastaḥ
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Ajātaśatru</s> routed the whole elephant corps of King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s>; his cavalry, chariot corps, and infantry were routed.

children.text: rājā prasenajit kauśalo jito bhīto bhagnaḥ parājitaḥ parāpṛṣṭhīkṛta ekarathena śrāvastīṃ praviṣṭaḥ
children.translated_text: King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s>, defeated, afraid, shattered, conquered, and put to flight, entered <s>Śrāvastī</s> in a single chariot.

children.text: evaṃ yāvat trir api ||
children.translated_text: So it went on, up to three times.

children.text: atha rājā prasenajit kauśalaḥ śokāgāraṃ praviśya kare kapolaṃ dattvā cintāparo vyavasthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s> entered the chamber of grief, placed his hand on his cheek, and remained absorbed in thought.

children.text: tatra ca śrāvastyām anyatamaḥ śreṣṭhī āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī
children.translated_text: There in <s>Śrāvastī</s> there was a certain guildmaster, rich, of great wealth and great possessions, with broad and extensive property, endowed with the wealth of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> and rivaling the wealth of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>.

children.text: tena śrutaṃ yathā rājā prasenajit kauśalo jito bhagnaḥ parāpṛṣṭhīkṛtaḥ ekaratheneha praviṣṭa iti
children.translated_text: He heard that King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s>, defeated, shattered, and put to flight, had entered here in a single chariot.

children.text: śrutvā ca punar yena rājā prasenajit kauśalas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ
children.translated_text: And having heard this, he approached King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s>.

children.text: upasaṃkramya rājānaṃ prasenajitaṃ kauśalaṃ jayenāyuṣā ca vardhayitvā ca kimarthaṃ deva śokaḥ kriyate ahaṃ devasya tāvat suvarṇam anuprayacchāmi yena devaḥ punar api yatheṣṭapracāraṇaṃ kariṣyatīti
children.translated_text: Having approached, he wished King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s> victory and long life and said, "Why does Your Majesty grieve? I will give Your Majesty enough gold that Your Majesty will again be able to act as he wishes."

children.text: tena tasya mahān suvarṇarāśiḥ kṛtaḥ yatropaviṣṭaḥ puruṣa utthitaṃ puruṣaṃ na paśyati utthito vā upaviṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: He made for him a great heap of gold, where a seated man could not see a standing man, nor a standing man a seated one.

children.text: atha rājñā prasenajitkauśalyena svaviṣaye carapuruṣāḥ samantata utsṛṣṭāḥ śṛṇuta janapravādān iti
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s> sent out spies everywhere in his own territory, saying, "Listen to the talk of the people."

children.text: yāvaj jetavane dvau mallāv anyonyaṃ saṃjalpaṃ kurutaḥ asti kesarī nāma saṃgrāmaḥ
children.translated_text: At length, in <s>Jetavana</s>, two wrestlers were conversing with one another: "There is a battle formation called <s>Kesarī</s>.

children.text: tatra ye kātarāḥ puruṣās te saṃgrāmaśirasi sthāpyante ye madhyās te madhye ye utkṛṣṭāḥ śūrapuruṣās te pṛṣṭhata iti
children.translated_text: In it, the cowardly men are placed at the front of the battle, the middling ones in the middle, and the excellent brave men at the rear."

children.text: tatas te rājñe iti veditavantaḥ
children.translated_text: Then they reported this to the king.

children.text: śrutvā ca rājā prasenajit kauśalas tathā caturaṅgabalakāyaṃ saṃnāhya hastikāyam aśvakāyaṃ rathakāyaṃ pattikāyaṃ ca rājānam ajātaśatrum abhiniryāto yuddhāya
children.translated_text: And having heard it, King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s> arrayed the fourfold army in that way, the elephant corps, cavalry, chariot corps, and infantry, and marched out against King <s>Ajātaśatru</s> for battle.

children.text: tato rājñā prasenajitā kauśalena rājño 'jātaśatror vaidehīputrasya sarvo hastikāyaḥ paryastaḥ aśvakāyo rathakāyaḥ pattikāyaḥ paryastaḥ
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s> routed the whole elephant corps of King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, son of <s>Vaidehī</s>; his cavalry, chariot corps, and infantry were routed.

children.text: rājānam apy ajātaśatruṃ vaidehīputraṃ jitaṃ bhītabhagnaparājitaṃ parāpṛṣṭhīkṛtaṃ jīvagrāhaṃ gṛhītvā ekarathe 'bhiropya yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ
children.translated_text: And having captured King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, son of <s>Vaidehī</s>, alive, defeated, afraid, shattered, conquered, and put to flight, he made him mount a single chariot and approached the Blessed One.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣīdati
children.translated_text: Having approached, he bowed his head to the Blessed One's feet and sat to one side.

children.text: ekāntaniṣaṇṇo rājā prasenajitkauśalo bhagavantam ity avocat ayaṃ hi bhadanta rājā ajātaśatrur dīrgharātram avairasya me vairī asapatnasya sapatnaḥ
children.translated_text: Seated to one side, King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s> said this to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, this King <s>Ajātaśatru</s> has long been an enemy to me, who had no enmity, and a foe to me, who had no foe.

children.text: na cecchāmy enaṃ jīvitād vyaparopayitum yasmād vayasyaputro 'yaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: But I do not wish to deprive him of life, because he is the son of a friend.

children.text: muñcāmy enam iti
children.translated_text: I will release him."

children.text: muñca mahārājety uktvā bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāṃ gāthāṃ bhāṣate
children.translated_text: "Release him, great king," the Blessed One said, and at that time the Blessed One spoke a verse:

children.text: jayo vairaṃ prasavati duḥkhaṃ śete parājitaḥ
children.translated_text: "Victory gives birth to enmity; the defeated one sleeps in pain.

children.text: upaśāntaḥ sukhaṃ śete hitvā jayaparājayam ||
children.translated_text: The peaceful one sleeps happily, having abandoned victory and defeat."

children.text: atha rājñaḥ prasenajitaḥ kauśalasyaitad abhavat yan mayā rājyaṃ pratilabdham tad asya śreṣṭhinaḥ prasādāt
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s>: "That I have regained the kingdom is due to the favor of this guildmaster.

children.text: yannvaham enaṃ vareṇa pravārayeyam iti
children.translated_text: What if I were to invite him to choose a boon?"

children.text: atha rājā prasenajit kauśalas taṃ śreṣṭhinaṃ vareṇa pravārayati
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s> invited that guildmaster to choose a boon.

children.text: sa kathayati ākāṅkṣāmi varam saptāhaṃ me yathābhirucitaṃ rājyam anuprayacchateti
children.translated_text: He said, "I desire this boon: grant me the kingdom for seven days, to do as I please."

children.text: tato rājñā sarvavijite ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kāritam dattaṃ me śreṣṭhine saptāham ekaṃ rājyam iti
children.translated_text: Then the king had a bell proclamation made throughout all his conquered realm: "I have given the guildmaster the kingdom for one week."

children.text: yāvat tena śreṣṭhinā buddhapramukho bhikṣusaṃghaḥ saptāhaṃ bhaktenopanimantritaḥ rājā ca prasenajit saparivāraḥ
children.translated_text: Then that guildmaster invited the community of monks headed by the Buddha for seven days of meals, and also King <s>Prasenajit</s> with his retinue.

children.text: yāvantaś ca kāśikośaleṣu janakāyāḥ prativasanti teṣāṃ dūtasaṃpreṣaṇaṃ kṛtam saptāhaṃ yūyaṃ sakalā yatheṣṭacāriṇaḥ sukhasparśaṃ viharata
children.translated_text: And to all the communities of people dwelling in <s>Kāśi</s> and <s>Kosala</s> he sent messengers, saying, "For seven days, all of you, going about as you wish, live in comfort.

children.text: kiṃcid āgatya buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchata dharmaṃ ca bhikṣusaṃghaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Come here and go for refuge to the Buddha, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the community of monks.

children.text: māmakaṃ ca bhojanaṃ bhuñjānās tathāgataṃ paryupāsadhvam iti
children.translated_text: And while eating my food, attend upon the <s>Tathāgata</s>."

children.text: tena saptāhaṃ bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃgho mahatā satkāreṇa satkṛtaḥ bahūni ca prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi kuśale niyojitāni
children.translated_text: For seven days he honored the Blessed One together with the community of disciples with great hospitality, and many hundreds of thousands of living beings were directed toward what is wholesome.

children.text: saptāhasyātyayena bhagavataḥ pādayor nipatya cetanāṃ puṣṇāti praṇidhiṃ ca cakāra anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca andhe loke anāyake apariṇāyake buddho bhūyāsam atīrṇānāṃ sattvānāṃ tārayitā amuktānāṃ mocayitā anāśvastānām āśvāsayitā aparinirvṛtānāṃ parinirvāpayiteti ||
children.translated_text: After seven days had passed, he fell at the Blessed One's feet, strengthened his resolve, and made a vow: "By this root of good, by this arising of thought, and by this renunciation of a gift-offering, in a blind world without a guide and without a leader, may I become a Buddha, a ferrier of beings not yet ferried, a liberator of those not yet liberated, a comforter of those not yet comforted, and one who brings to final nirvana those not yet finally nirvanized."

children.text: atha bhagavāṃs tasya śreṣṭhino hetuparaṃparāṃ karmaparaṃparāṃ ca jñātvā smitaṃ prāvirakārṣīt
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, knowing the succession of causes and the succession of karma of that wealthy man, revealed a smile.

children.text: dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhān niścārya kāścid adhastād gacchanti kāścid upariṣṭād gacchanti
children.translated_text: Indeed it is the nature of things that, at the time when the blessed Buddhas reveal a smile, blue, yellow, red, and white flames issue from their mouths; some go downward and some go upward.

children.text: yā adhastād gacchanti tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanam avīcim arbudaṃ nirarbudaṃ aṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvam utpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaṃ narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakās teṣu śītībhūtā nipatanti ye śītanarakās teṣūṣṇībhūtā nipatanti
children.translated_text: Those that go downward go to the hells: <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s>; in the hot hells they fall as cool, and in the cold hells they fall as warm.

children.text: tena teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante
children.translated_text: By that, the particular torments of those beings subside.

children.text: teṣām evaṃ bhavati kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ āhosvid anyatropapannā iti
children.translated_text: It occurs to them, "Have we, sirs, fallen away from here, or have we been reborn somewhere else?"

children.text: teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati
children.translated_text: In order to generate faith in them, the Blessed One sends forth a created apparition.

children.text: teṣāṃ nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavati na hy eva vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutā nāpy anyatropapannāḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that apparition, it occurs to them, "No indeed, sirs, we have not fallen away from here, nor have we been reborn elsewhere."

children.text: api tv ayam apūrvadarśanaḥ sattvaḥ asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti
children.translated_text: Rather, this being, never seen before, has caused our particular torments to subside through his power.

children.text: te nirmite cittam abhiprasādya tan narakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇanti yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti
children.translated_text: They make their minds clear with faith in the apparition, exhaust the karma to be experienced in hell, and take rebirth among gods and humans, where they become vessels for the truths.

children.text: yā upariṣṭād gacchanti tāś cāturmahārājikāṃs trayastriṃśān yāmāṃs tuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhān apramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān abṛhān atapān sudṛśān sudarśanān akaniṣṭhān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmety udghoṣayanti gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante
children.translated_text: Those that go upward go to the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājikas</s>, the <s>Trāyastriṃśas</s>, the <s>Yāmas</s>, the <s>Tuṣitas</s>, the <s>Nirmāṇaratis</s>, the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartins</s>, the <s>Brahmakāyikas</s>, the <s>Brahmapurohitas</s>, the <s>Mahābrahmās</s>, the gods of limited radiance, immeasurable radiance, and streaming radiance, the gods of limited beauty, immeasurable beauty, and complete beauty, the cloudless gods, the producers of merit, the great-fruit gods, the <s>Abṛhas</s>, the <s>Atapas</s>, the <s>Sudṛśas</s>, the <s>Sudarśanas</s>, and the <s>Akaniṣṭhas</s>; having gone there, they proclaim, "Impermanent, suffering, empty, without self," and they speak two verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane
children.translated_text: "Begin! Go forth! Apply yourselves to the Buddha's teaching.

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāram iva kuñjaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Shake off the army of death, as an elephant shakes a reed hut.

children.text: yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati
children.translated_text: For whoever in this <s>dharmavinaya</s> (teaching and discipline) lives heedfully

children.text: prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: will abandon the cycle of birth and bring suffering to an end."

children.text: atha tā arciṣas trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātum anvāhiṇḍya bhagavantam eva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti
children.translated_text: Then those flames, having wandered through the three-thousand great-thousand world system, follow directly behind the Blessed One.

children.text: tad yadi bhagavān atītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If the Blessed One wishes to predict past karma, they disappear behind the Blessed One.

children.text: anāgataṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati purastād antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict future karma, they disappear in front.

children.text: narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pādatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth in hell, they disappear at the soles of his feet.

children.text: tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pārṣṇyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as an animal, they disappear at his heels.

children.text: pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as a preta, they disappear at his big toe.

children.text: manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati jānunor antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as a human, they disappear at his knees.

children.text: balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict kingship as a powerful wheel-turning monarch, they disappear in his left palm.

children.text: cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict kingship as a wheel-turning monarch, they disappear in his right palm.

children.text: devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati nābhyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth among the gods, they disappear at his navel.

children.text: śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati āsye 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the awakening of a disciple, they disappear in his mouth.

children.text: pratyekabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati ūrṇāyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the awakening of a solitary Buddha, they disappear in his <s>ūrṇā</s>.

children.text: anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati uṣṇīṣe antardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict unsurpassed perfect awakening, they disappear in his <s>uṣṇīṣa</s>.

children.text: atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata uṣṇīṣe 'ntarhitāḥ
children.translated_text: Then those flames circumambulated the Blessed One three times to the right and vanished into the Blessed One's <s>uṣṇīṣa</s>.

children.text: athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with folded hands, asked the Blessed One:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro vaktrāntarān niṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ
children.translated_text: "A cluster, varied and painted with a thousand colors, has issued from within your mouth,

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantād divākareṇodayatā yathaiva ||
children.translated_text: by which the quarters all around have been illuminated, just as by the rising sun.

children.text: gāthāś ca bhāṣate
children.translated_text: And he speaks verses:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā buddhā jagaty uttamahetubhūtāḥ
children.translated_text: "Free from renewed becoming, having abandoned misery and pride, the Buddhas, who are the supreme cause in the world,

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ smitam upadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Jinas</s>, conquerors of their enemies, do not show a smile, white as a conch or lotus fiber, without a reason.

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayam adhigamya vīra buddhyā śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām
children.translated_text: Therefore, having yourself understood at once with wise, heroic insight, O hero, O ascetic, O lord of <s>Jinas</s>, for the hearers who desire to know,

children.text: dhīrābhir munivṛṣa vāgbhir uttamābhir utpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: O steadfast bull among sages, remove the arisen doubt with your firm, excellent, auspicious words.

children.text: nākasmāl lavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ saṃbuddhāḥ smitam upadarśayanti nāthāḥ
children.translated_text: The perfectly awakened lords, firm as the king of mountains in the salt ocean, do not show a smile without cause.

children.text: yasyārthe smitam upadarśayanti dhīrāḥ taṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The crowds of people desire to hear the matter for whose sake the steadfast ones show a smile."

children.text: bhagavān āha evam etad ānanda evam etat
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>; so it is.

children.text: nāhetvapratyayam ānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti
children.translated_text: Not without cause and condition, <s>Ānanda</s>, do <s>Tathāgatas</s>, arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas reveal a smile.

children.text: paśyasi tvam ānanda anena śreṣṭhinā tathāgatasya saśrāvakasaṃghasyaivaṃvidhaṃ satkāraṃ kṛtam mahājanakāyaṃ ca kuśale niyuktam
children.translated_text: Do you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, that this guild leader has rendered such honor to the <s>Tathāgata</s> together with the community of disciples, and has engaged a great mass of people in wholesome action?

children.text: evaṃ bhadanta
children.translated_text: "Yes, venerable sir."

children.text: eṣa ānanda śreṣṭhī 'nena kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca trikalpāsaṃkhyeyasamudānītāṃ bodhiṃ samudānīya mahākaruṇāparibhāvitāḥ ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ paripūrya abhayaprado nāma samyaksaṃbuddho bhaviṣyati daśabhir balaiś caturbhir vaiśāradyais tribhir āveṇikaiḥ smṛtyupasthānair mahākaruṇayā ca
children.translated_text: This guild leader, <s>Ānanda</s>, through this root of good, this arising of the thought, and this renunciation of a gift-offering, after gathering the awakening accumulated over three incalculable eons and fulfilling the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), suffused with great compassion, will become a perfectly awakened Buddha named <s>Abhayaprada</s>, endowed with the ten powers, the four confidences, the three special applications of mindfulness, and great compassion.

children.text: ayam asya deyadharmo yo mamāntike cittaprasāda iti ||
children.translated_text: This is his gift-offering: clarity of faith in his mind toward me."

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: Delighted in mind, those monks rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.

children.text: Chapter 10

buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati nadyā ajiravatyā adhastān nāvikagrāme
children.translated_text: The Buddha, the Blessed One, honored, highly revered, respected, and worshiped by kings, royal ministers, wealthy men, townspeople, guild leaders, caravan merchants, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, thus worshiped by gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, known as a Buddha, the Blessed One, of great merit and receiving robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicines and requisites for sickness, was dwelling with the community of disciples at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, below the river <s>Ajiravatī</s>, in the boatmen's village.

children.text: atha te nāvikā yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntāḥ
children.translated_text: Then those boatmen approached the Blessed One.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte nyaṣīdan
children.translated_text: Having approached, they bowed with their heads to the Blessed One's feet and sat to one side.

children.text: ekāntaniṣaṇṇāṃs tān nāvikān bhagavān dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati
children.translated_text: While those boatmen were seated to one side, the Blessed One instructed, urged, encouraged, and delighted them with a discourse on <s>dharma</s> (the teaching).

children.text: anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīm
children.translated_text: Having in many ways instructed, urged, encouraged, and delighted them with a discourse on <s>dharma</s>, he became silent.

children.text: atha te nāvikā utthāyāsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantam ūcuḥ adhivāsayatu bhagavān asmākaṃ nadyā ajiravatyās tīre śvo bhaktena sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghena
children.translated_text: Then those boatmen rose from their seats, arranged their upper robes over one shoulder, bowed with folded hands toward the Blessed One, and said to the Blessed One, "May the Blessed One, together with the community of monks, consent to take tomorrow's meal from us on the bank of the river <s>Ajiravatī</s>.

children.text: nausaṃkrameṇottārayiṣyāma iti
children.translated_text: We will ferry you across by a boat-passage."

children.text: adhivāsayati bhagavān nāvikānāṃ tūṣṇībhāvena ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One consented to the boatmen by remaining silent.

children.text: atha nāvikā nadyā ajiravatyās tīram apagatapāṣāṇaśarkarakaṭhallaṃ vyavasthāpayāmāsur ucchritacchatradhvajapatākaṃ nānāpuṣpāvakīrṇaṃ gandhaghaṭikāvadhūpitam
children.translated_text: Then the boatmen prepared the bank of the river <s>Ajiravatī</s>, making it free of stones, gravel, and pebbles, with parasols, banners, and flags raised, strewn with various flowers, and perfumed by vessels of incense.

children.text: praṇītam āhāraṃ kṛtavantaḥ
children.translated_text: They prepared excellent food.

children.text: prabhūtaṃ ca puṣpasaṃgrahaṃ kṛtvā nausaṃkramaṃ puṣpamaṇḍapair alaṃkārayāmāsuḥ
children.translated_text: And after gathering an abundance of flowers, they adorned the boat-passage with flower pavilions.

children.text: bhagavataś ca dūtena kālam ārocayāmāsuḥ samayo bhadanta sajjaṃ bhaktam yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālaṃ manyata iti
children.translated_text: And through a messenger they announced the time to the Blessed One: "It is time, venerable sir; the meal is ready, if the Blessed One now thinks it is time."

children.text: atha bhagavān bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto yena nāvikagrāmakas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, surrounded by a group of monks and preceded by the community of monks, approached the boatmen's village.

children.text: upasaṃkramya purastād bhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane nyaṣīdat
children.translated_text: Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat at the head of the community of monks.

children.text: atha te nāvikāḥ sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ viditvā śucinā praṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpayati saṃpravārayati
children.translated_text: Then those boatmen, knowing that the community of monks headed by the Buddha was comfortably seated, satisfied and served them with pure, excellent hard and soft foods with their own hands.

children.text: anekaparyāyeṇa śucinā praṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpya saṃpravārya bhagavantaṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastam apanītapātraṃ nīcatarāṇy āsanāni gṛhītvā bhagavataḥ purastān niṣaṇṇā dharmaśravaṇāya
children.translated_text: Having in many ways satisfied and served them with pure, excellent hard and soft foods with their own hands, and knowing that the Blessed One had eaten, washed his hands, and put away his bowl, they took lower seats and sat before the Blessed One to hear the <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: atha bhagavāṃs teṣāṃ nāvikānām āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśīṃ caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikīṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kṛtavān yāṃ śrutvā anekair nāvikaiḥ srotaāpattiphalāni prāptāni kaiścit sakṛdāgāmiphalāni kaiścid anāgāmiphalāni kaiścit pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam kaiścicchrāvakabodhau cittāny utpāditāni kaiścit pratyekabodhau kaiścid anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, knowing the dispositions, latent tendencies, elements, and natures of those boatmen, gave such a teaching of <s>dharma</s> as leads to penetration of the four noble truths. Having heard it, many boatmen attained the fruits of stream-entry, some the fruits of once-returning, some the fruits of non-returning, some went forth and, through the abandonment of all defilements, directly realized arhatship, some produced thoughts toward the awakening of a disciple, some toward the awakening of a solitary Buddha, and some toward <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect awakening).

children.text: sarvā ca sā parṣad buddhanimnā dharmapravaṇā saṃghaprāgbhārā vyavasthitā
children.translated_text: And that whole assembly became inclined toward the Buddha, bent toward the <s>dharma</s>, and oriented toward the <s>saṃgha</s>.

children.text: tatas tair nāvikair bhagavān mahatā satkāreṇa nausaṃkrameṇottāritaḥ sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghena ||
children.translated_text: Then those boatmen ferried the Blessed One across by the boat-passage with great honor, together with the community of monks.

children.text: bhikṣavo buddhapūjādarśanād āvarjitamanaso buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ kutremāni bhagavataḥ kuśalamūlāni kṛtānīti
children.translated_text: The monks, their minds captivated by seeing the worship of the Buddha, asked the Buddha, the Blessed One, "Where were these roots of good of the Blessed One made?"

children.text: bhagavān āha tathāgatenaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni yena tathāgatasyaivaṃvidhā pūjā
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "Monks, by the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself, in former births, deeds were done and accumulated, furnished with their supports, ripened in their conditions, present like a flood, and bound to occur; by these there is such worship of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: icchatha bhikṣavaḥ śrotum evaṃ bhadanta
children.translated_text: Do you wish to hear, monks?" "Yes, venerable sir."

children.text: tena hi bhikṣavaḥ śṛṇuta sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuruta bhāṣiṣye ||
children.translated_text: Then, monks, listen, and attend carefully and well; I shall speak.

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani bhāgīratho nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān
children.translated_text: In the past, monks, in a past age, a perfectly awakened Buddha named <s>Bhāgīratha</s> arose in the world: a <s>Tathāgata</s>, arhat, perfectly awakened Buddha, endowed with knowledge and conduct, well-gone, knower of the world, unsurpassed guide of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, Buddha, Blessed One.

children.text: sa dvāṣaṣṭyarhatsahasraparivṛto janapadacārikāṃ caran gaṅgātīram anuprāptaḥ
children.translated_text: Surrounded by sixty-two thousand arhats, he was wandering on a tour through the country and reached the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>.

children.text: tasmin samaye 'nyataraḥ sārthavāho 'nekaśataparivāro nadyāṃ gaṅgāyāṃ sārtham uttārayati
children.translated_text: At that time a certain caravan leader, with many hundreds in his retinue, was ferrying his caravan across the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>.

children.text: tasmiṃś ca pradeśe mahattaskarabhayam
children.translated_text: And in that region there was great danger from bandits.

children.text: atha dadarśa sārthavāho bhāgīrathaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ dvāṣaṣṭyarhatsahasraparivṛtam
children.translated_text: Then the caravan leader saw the perfectly awakened Buddha <s>Bhāgīratha</s>, surrounded by sixty-two thousand arhats.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ cittaṃ prasādayāmāsa
children.translated_text: Seeing him, he then made his mind clear with faith.

children.text: prasannacittaś ca bhagavantam āmantritavān tatprathamataram eva bhagavantaṃ tārayiṣyāmīti
children.translated_text: And with a clear mind he invited the Blessed One, saying, "I will ferry the Blessed One across first of all."

children.text: adhivāsayati bhāgīrathaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sārthavāhasya tūṣṇībhāvena
children.translated_text: <s>Bhāgīratha</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, consented to the caravan leader by remaining silent.

children.text: tatas tena sārthavāhena bhāgīrathaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ dvāṣaṣṭyarhatsahasraparivṛto mahatyā vibhūtyā nausaṃkrameṇottāritaḥ
children.translated_text: Then that caravan leader ferried <s>Bhāgīratha</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, surrounded by sixty-two thousand arhats, across with great splendor by means of a crossing of boats.

children.text: praṇītena cāhāreṇa saṃtarpyānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: And after satisfying him with excellent food, he made a vow for unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: bhagavān āha kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena sārthavāho babhūva ahaṃ saḥ
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "What do you think, monks? The one who at that time, on that occasion, was the caravan leader: I was he.

children.text: mayā sa bhāgīrathaḥ samyaksaṃbuddho dvāṣaṣṭyarhatsahasraparivṛto nausaṃkrameṇottāritaḥ praṇītenāhāreṇa saṃtarpitaḥ praṇidhānaṃ ca kṛtam
children.translated_text: I ferried that perfectly awakened Buddha <s>Bhāgīratha</s>, surrounded by sixty-two thousand arhats, across by means of a crossing of boats, satisfied him with excellent food, and made a vow.

children.text: tasya me karmaṇo vipākenānantasaṃsāre mahatsukham anubhūtam
children.translated_text: As the result of that karma of mine, I experienced great happiness throughout endless <s>saṃsāra</s>.

children.text: idānīm apy anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhasyaivaṃvidhā pūjā
children.translated_text: Even now, after I have awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening, there is such worship.

children.text: tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam yacchāstāraṃ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, monks, you should train thus: 'We will honor the Teacher, highly revere him, esteem him, and worship him.

children.text: śāstāraṃ satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvopaniśritya vihariṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Having honored the Teacher, highly revered him, esteemed him, worshiped him, and relied upon him, we will dwell.'

children.text: ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, should you train."

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: Those monks, pleased in mind, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.

children.text: Chapter 11

buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ kauravyeṣu janapadacārikāṃ caran kauravyaṃ nagaram anuprāptaḥ
children.translated_text: The Buddha, the Blessed One, honored, highly revered, respected, and worshiped by kings, royal ministers, wealthy men, townspeople, guild leaders, caravan merchants, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, thus worshiped by gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, known as a Buddha, the Blessed One, of great merit and recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicines and requisites for sickness, together with the community of disciples, while wandering on a tour through the Kauravya country, reached the city of <s>Kauravya</s>.

children.text: sa ca kauravyo janakāyo buddhavaineya udāracittaḥ pradānaruciś ca
children.translated_text: And that Kauravya populace was fit to be trained by a Buddha, noble-minded, and fond of giving.

children.text: tato bhagavata etad abhavat yannvahaṃ śakraṃ devendraṃ marudgaṇaparivṛtam āhvayeyam yaddarśanād eṣāṃ kuśalamūlavivṛddhiḥ syād iti
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to the Blessed One: "What if I were to summon <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, surrounded by the host of <s>Maruts</s>, so that from seeing him there would be an increase of their roots of good?"

children.text: tato bhagavāṃllaukikaṃ cittam utpādayati aho bata śakro devendro marudgaṇasahāyo gośīrṣacandanamayaṃ stambham ādāya gacched iti ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One produced a worldly thought: "Ah, may <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, accompanied by the host of <s>Maruts</s>, come bringing a pillar made of gośīrṣa sandalwood!"

children.text: sahacittotpādācchakro devendro marudgaṇaparivṛta āgato yatra viśvakarmā catvāraś ca mahārājā anekadevanāgayakṣakumbhāṇḍaparivṛto gośīrṣacandanastambham ādāya
children.translated_text: As soon as that thought arose, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, surrounded by the host of <s>Maruts</s>, came, along with <s>Viśvakarman</s> and the four great kings, surrounded by many gods, nāgas, yakṣas, and kumbhāṇḍas, carrying a pillar of gośīrṣa sandalwood.

children.text: hāhākārakilakilāprakṣveḍoccair nādaṃ kurvāṇā bhagavato 'rthe gośīrṣacandanamayaṃ prāsādam abhisaṃskṛtavantaḥ
children.translated_text: Making cries of "hā hā," shouts of joy, clamorous calls, and loud noise, they constructed for the Blessed One's sake a palace made of gośīrṣa sandalwood.

children.text: tatas tasmin prāsāde śakreṇa devendreṇa bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃgho divyenāhāreṇa divyena śayanāsanena divyair gandhamālyapuṣpaiḥ satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then in that palace, by <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, the Blessed One together with the community of disciples was honored, highly revered, respected, and worshiped with divine food, divine bedding and seats, and divine perfumes, garlands, and flowers.

children.text: atha kauravyo janakāyas tāṃ divyāṃ vibhūṣikāṃ dṛṣṭvā paraṃ vismayam āpanna imāṃ cintām āpede nūnaṃ buddho bhagavāṃl loke 'gryaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the Kauravya populace, seeing that divine splendor, was seized with supreme amazement and conceived this thought: "Surely the Buddha, the Blessed One, is foremost in the world,

children.text: yat tu nāma sendrair devaiḥ pūjyata iti āvarjitamanā bhagavantam upasaṃkrāntaḥ
children.translated_text: for indeed he is worshiped by gods together with <s>Indra</s>." With their minds won over, they approached the Blessed One.

children.text: bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvaikānte nyaṣīdat
children.translated_text: Having bowed at the Blessed One's feet, they sat to one side.

children.text: ekāntaniṣaṇṇaḥ kauravyo janakāyas tasmin prāsāde 'tyarthaṃ prasādam utpādayati ||
children.translated_text: Sitting to one side, the Kauravya populace generated very great faith in that palace.

children.text: tena bhagavāṃs tat prāsādam antardhāpya anityatāpratisaṃyuktāṃ tādṛśīṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kṛtavān yāṃ śrutvā anekaiḥ kauravyanivāsibhir manuṣyaiḥ srotaāpattiphalāny anuprāptāni kaiścit sakṛdāgāmiphalāni kaiścid anāgāmiphalāni kaiścit pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam kaiścicchrāvakabodhau cittāny utpāditāni kaiścit pratyekāyāṃ bodhau kaiścid anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One caused that palace to disappear and gave such a Dharma teaching connected with impermanence that, having heard it, many human inhabitants of <s>Kauravya</s> attained the fruits of stream-entry; some attained the fruits of once-returning, some the fruits of non-returning; some, after going forth, through the abandonment of all defilements directly realized arhatship; some generated thoughts toward the awakening of a disciple, some toward solitary awakening, and some toward unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: sarvā ca sā parṣad buddhanimnā dharmapravaṇā saṃghaprāgbhārā vyavasthitā
children.translated_text: And that entire assembly was established as sloping toward the Buddha, inclined to the <s>Dharma</s> (teaching), and leaning toward the <s>Saṃgha</s> (community).

children.text: tatas te bhikṣavo bhagavato divyapūjādarśanād āvarjitamanaso buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ kutremāni bhagavatā kuśalamūlāni kṛtānīti
children.translated_text: Then those monks, their minds drawn by seeing the Blessed One's divine worship, asked the Buddha, the Blessed One, "Where were these roots of good made by the Blessed One?"

children.text: bhagavān āha tathāgatenaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni yena tathāgatasyaivaṃvidhā pūjā
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "It was by the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself, monks, in other former births, that deeds were done and accumulated; their requisites had been obtained, their conditions had matured, and they have come upon him like a flood, inevitably, so that there is such worship of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: icchatha bhikṣavaḥ śrotum evaṃ bhadanta
children.translated_text: Do you wish to hear it, monks?" "Yes, venerable sir."

children.text: tena hi bhikṣavaḥ śṛṇuta sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuruta bhāṣiṣye ||
children.translated_text: "Then listen, monks, and attend well and carefully; I will speak."

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani brahmā nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān
children.translated_text: "Once, monks, in the past, in a former time, a perfectly awakened Buddha named <s>Brahmā</s> arose in the world: a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an arhat, a perfectly awakened Buddha, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, knower of the world, unsurpassed guide of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One.

children.text: atha brahmā samyaksaṃbuddho dvāṣaṣṭyarhatsahasraparivṛto janapadacārikāṃ carann anyatamāṃ rājadhānīm anuprāptaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, surrounded by sixty-two thousand arhats, while wandering on a tour through the countryside, arrived at a certain royal capital.

children.text: aśrauṣīd rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣiktaḥ brahmā samyaksaṃbuddho dvāṣaṣṭyarhatsahasraparivṛto janapadacārikāṃ carann asmākaṃ vijitam anuprāpta iti
children.translated_text: A consecrated kṣatriya king heard, "<s>Brahmā</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, surrounded by sixty-two thousand arhats, while wandering on a tour through the countryside, has arrived in our dominion."

children.text: śrutvā ca punar mahatyā rājarddhyā mahatā rājānubhāvena yena bhagavān brahmā samyaksaṃbuddhas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ
children.translated_text: Having heard this, with great royal splendor and great royal power, he approached the Blessed One <s>Brahmā</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha.

children.text: upasaṃkramya brahmaṇaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte nyaṣīdat
children.translated_text: Having approached, he bowed with his head to the feet of <s>Brahmā</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, and sat down to one side.

children.text: ekāntaniṣaṇṇaṃ rājānaṃ kṣatriyaṃ mūrdhābhiṣiktaṃ bhagavān bodhikarakair dharmaiḥ samādāpayati
children.translated_text: As the consecrated kṣatriya king sat to one side, the Blessed One instructed him in teachings that produce awakening.

children.text: atha sa labdhaprasāda utthāyāsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantam idam avocat adhivāsayatu me bhagavān asyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ traimāsyavāsāya
children.translated_text: Then, having gained faith, he rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, bowed with folded hands toward the Blessed One, and said this to the Blessed One: "Let the Blessed One consent to a three-month residence in this royal capital of mine.

children.text: ahaṃ bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃgham upasthāsyāmi cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārair iti
children.translated_text: I will serve the Blessed One together with the community of disciples with robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicines and requisites for sickness."

children.text: adhivāsayati brahmā samyaksaṃbuddho rājñas tūṣṇībhāvena
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, consented to the king by silence.

children.text: atha sa rājā mūrdhābhiṣikto bhagavato 'rthe gośīrṣacandanamayaṃ prāsādaṃ kārayāmāsa
children.translated_text: Then that consecrated king had a palace made of gośīrṣa sandalwood built for the Blessed One.

children.text: sa taṃ vicitrair vastrālaṃkārair alaṃkṛtaṃ nānāpuṣpāvakīrṇaṃ gandhaghaṭikādhūpitaṃ bhagavataḥ saśrāvakasaṃghasya niryātya traimāsyaṃ praṇītenāhāreṇa saṃtarpya vividhair vastraviśeṣair ācchādyānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau praṇidhiṃ cakāra ||
children.translated_text: He handed it over to the Blessed One together with the community of disciples, adorned with variegated cloth ornaments, strewn with many kinds of flowers, and perfumed with fragrant incense vessels; after satisfying them for three months with excellent food and clothing them with various fine garments, he made a vow for unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: bhagavān āha kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣikto babhūva ahaṃ saḥ
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "What do you think, monks? The one who at that time, on that occasion, was the consecrated kṣatriya king was I.

children.text: yan mayā brahmaṇaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasyaivaṃvidhā pūjā kṛtā tasya me karmaṇo vipākenānantasaṃsāre mahatsukham anubhūtam
children.translated_text: Because such worship was done by me for <s>Brahmā</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, by the ripening of that karma I experienced great happiness through endless <s>saṃsāra</s> (cycle of rebirth).

children.text: idānīm apy anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhasyaivaṃvidhā pūjā
children.translated_text: Now too, having awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening, such worship comes to me.

children.text: tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam yacchāstāraṃ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, monks, you should train yourselves thus: 'We will honor the Teacher, revere him, esteem him, and worship him.

children.text: śāstāraṃ satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvopaniśritya vihariṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Having honored, revered, esteemed, and worshiped the Teacher, we will dwell relying upon him.'

children.text: ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, should you train yourselves."

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: Delighted in mind, those monks rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.

children.text: Chapter 12

buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme
children.translated_text: The Buddha, the Blessed One, honored, highly revered, esteemed, and worshiped by kings, royal ministers, wealthy men, townspeople, guild leaders, caravan merchants, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, thus worshiped by gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, known as a Buddha, the Blessed One, of great merit and receiving robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicines and requisites for sickness, was dwelling with the community of disciples at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, in the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.

children.text: tena khalu samayena śrāvastyāṃ pañcamātrāṇi vaṇikśatāni kāntāramārgapratipannāni
children.translated_text: At that time in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, five hundred merchants had set out on a wilderness road.

children.text: te mārgāt paribhraṣṭā vālukāsthalam anuprāptāḥ
children.translated_text: They strayed from the road and reached a sandy waste.

children.text: te dharmaśramaparipīḍitāḥ kṣīṇapathyādanāś ca madhyāhnasamaye tīkṣṇakararaśmisaṃtāpitā jaloddhṛtā iva matsyāḥ pṛthivyām āvartante duḥkhāṃ tīvrāṃ kharāṃ kaṭukām amanāpāṃ vedanāṃ vedayamānāḥ
children.translated_text: Oppressed by fatigue from the journey and with their provisions of food exhausted, at midday, scorched by sharp rays, they rolled on the ground like fish pulled out of water, experiencing a painful, intense, harsh, bitter, disagreeable feeling.

children.text: tāni devatāsahasrāṇy āyācante tadyathā śivavaruṇakuberavāsavādīni
children.translated_text: They entreated thousands of deities, such as <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Vāsava</s>, and others.

children.text: na cainān kaścit paritrātuṃ samarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But no one among them was able to rescue them.

children.text: tatra cānyatara upāsako buddhaśāsanābhijñaḥ
children.translated_text: There was there a certain lay follower who knew the Buddha's teaching.

children.text: sa tān vaṇija āha bhavanto buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchantv iti
children.translated_text: He said to those merchants, "Sirs, go for refuge to the Buddha."

children.text: tata ekaraveṇa sarva eva buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, with one voice, all of them went for refuge to the Buddha.

children.text: atrāntare nāsti kiṃcid buddhānāṃ bhagavatām ajñātam adṛṣṭam aviditam avijñātam
children.translated_text: In the meantime, there is nothing unknown, unseen, unlearned, or uncomprehended by the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.

children.text: dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahākāruṇikānāṃ lokānugrahapravṛttakānām ekārakṣāṇāṃ śamathavipaśyanāvihāriṇāṃ tridamathavastukuśalānāṃ caturoghottīrṇānāṃ caturṛddhipādacaraṇatalasupratiṣṭhitānāṃ caturṣu saṃgrahavastuṣu dīrgharātrakṛtaparicayānāṃ pañcāṅgaviprahīṇānāṃ pañcagatisamatikrāntānāṃ ṣaḍaṅgasamanvāgatānāṃ ṣaṭpāramitāparipūrṇānāṃ saptabodhyaṅgakusumāḍhyānām aṣṭāṅgamārgadeśikānāṃ navānupūrvavihārasamāpattikuśalānāṃ daśabalabalināṃ daśadiksamāpūrṇayaśasāṃ daśaśatavaśavartiprativiśiṣṭānāṃ trī rātres trir divasasya ca buddhacakṣuṣā lokaṃ vyavalokya jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate ko hīyate ko vardhate kaḥ kṛcchraprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃkaṭaprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃbādhaprāptaḥ kaḥ kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasaṃbādhaprāptaḥ ko 'pāyanimnaḥ ko 'pāyapravaṇaḥ ko 'pāyaprāgbhāraḥ
children.translated_text: Indeed, it is the nature of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who are greatly compassionate, active for the welfare of the world, sole protectors, dwelling in calm and insight, skilled in the three bases of taming, crossed beyond the four floods, firmly established with their feet upon the four bases of miraculous power, long familiar with the four means of gathering, free from the five factors, passed beyond the five destinies, endowed with the six qualities, complete in the six perfections, rich with the flowers of the seven factors of awakening, teachers of the eightfold path, skilled in the attainments of the nine successive abidings, mighty with the ten powers, whose fame fills the ten directions, and superior to those who wield power in the ten hundreds, that three times by night and three times by day, after surveying the world with the Buddha-eye, knowledge and vision arise: Who is declining? Who is increasing? Who has fallen into distress? Who has fallen into danger? Who has fallen into constraint? Who has fallen into distress, danger, and constraint? Who is inclined toward the lower realms? Who is headed toward the lower realms? Who is leaning toward the lower realms?

children.text: kam aham apāyād uddhṛtya svarge mokṣe ca pratiṣṭhāpayeyam kasya kāmapaṅkanimagnasya hastoddhāram anupradadyām kam āryadhanavirahitam āryadhanaiśvaryādhipatye pratiṣṭhāpayeyam kasyājñānatimirapaṭalaparyavanaddhanetrasya jñānāñjanaśalākayā cakṣur viśodhayāmi
children.translated_text: Whom shall I lift out of a lower realm and establish in heaven and liberation? To whom, sunk in the mire of desire, shall I extend a helping hand? Whom, lacking noble wealth, shall I establish in lordship over the riches of noble wealth? Whose eye, enveloped by the mass of darkness of ignorance, shall I cleanse with the collyrium-stick of knowledge?

children.text: kasyānavaropitāni kuśalamūlānyavaropayeyam kasyāvaropitāni paripācayeyam kasya paripakvāni vimocayeyam
children.translated_text: In whom shall I plant roots of good that have not been planted? Whose roots, once planted, shall I ripen? Whose roots, once ripened, shall I liberate?

children.text: āha ca
children.translated_text: And it is said:

children.text: apy evātikramed velāṃ sāgaro makarālayaḥ
children.translated_text: The ocean, abode of sea monsters, might even overstep its boundary,

children.text: na tu vaineyavatsānāṃ buddho velām atikramet ||
children.translated_text: but the Buddha does not miss the proper moment for those who are to be guided.

children.text: yāvat paśyati bhagavān saṃbahulān vaṇijo vyasanasaṃkaṭasaṃbādhaprāptān
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One saw many merchants who had fallen into calamity, danger, and constraint.

children.text: tataś cakṣuḥsaṃpreṣaṇamātreṇa jetavane 'ntarhito bhikṣugaṇaparivṛtas taṃ pradeśam anuprāptaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, by merely directing his gaze, he vanished from <s>Jetavana</s> and, surrounded by a group of monks, arrived at that place.

children.text: dadṛśus te vaṇijo bhagavantaṃ sabhikṣusaṃgham
children.translated_text: Those merchants saw the Blessed One together with the community of monks.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca uccair nādaṃ muktavantaḥ
children.translated_text: And on seeing him, they let out a loud cry.

children.text: tato bhagavatā laukikaṃ cittam utpāditam aho bata śakro devendro māhendraṃ varṣam utsṛjatu śītalāś ca vāyavo vāntv iti
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One produced a worldly thought: Ah, may <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, release a mighty Indra-rain, and may cool winds blow.

children.text: sahacittotpādād bhagavataḥ śakreṇa māhendraṃ varṣam utsṛṣṭam śītalāś ca vāyavaḥ preṣitāḥ yatas teṣāṃ vaṇijāṃ tṛṣā vigatā dāhaś ca praśāntaḥ
children.translated_text: At the arising of the Blessed One's thought, <s>Śakra</s> released a mighty Indra-rain and sent cool winds, so that the thirst of those merchants passed away and their burning was calmed.

children.text: tatas tair vaṇigbhiḥ saṃjñā pratilabdhā
children.translated_text: Then those merchants regained consciousness.

children.text: bhagavatā caiṣāṃ mārga ākhyāto yena śrāvastīm anuprāptāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the Blessed One showed them the road by which they reached <s>Śrāvastī</s>.

children.text: te mārgaśramaṃ prativinodya tato bhagavatsakāśam upasaṃkrāntāḥ
children.translated_text: After recovering from the fatigue of the road, they then approached the Blessed One.

children.text: teṣāṃ bhagavatā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā yāṃ śrutvā kaiścit srotaāpattiphalam adhigatam kaiścit sakṛdāgāmiphalam kaiścid anāgāmiphalam kaiścit pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam kaiścicchrāvakabodhau cittāny utpāditāni kaiścit pratyekāyāṃ bodhau kaiścid anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau
children.translated_text: For them the Blessed One gave such a teaching of the <s>dharma</s> as leads to penetration of the four noble truths. Having heard it, some attained the fruit of stream-entry, some the fruit of once-returning, some the fruit of non-returning; some, after going forth and abandoning all defilements, directly realized arhatship; some produced thoughts toward the awakening of a disciple, some toward solitary awakening, and some toward unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: yadbhūyasā ca sā parṣad buddhanimnā dharmapravaṇā saṃghaprāgbhārā vyavasthitā ||
children.translated_text: And for the most part that assembly became inclined toward the Buddha, bent toward the <s>dharma</s>, and oriented toward the <s>saṃgha</s>.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ āścaryaṃ bhagavan yāvad ime vaṇijo bhagavatā kāntāramārgāt paritrātāḥ
children.translated_text: The monks, having become doubtful, asked the Buddha, the Blessed One, cutter-off of all doubts: Wonderful, Blessed One, how these merchants were rescued by the Blessed One from the wilderness road.

children.text: sahacittotpādāc ca māhendravarṣaṃ vṛṣṭam
children.translated_text: And at the mere arising of his thought, a mighty Indra-rain fell,

children.text: śītalāś ca vāyavaḥ pravātā iti
children.translated_text: and cool winds blew.

children.text: bhagavān āha tathāgatenaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: By the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself, monks, in other former births, deeds were done and accumulated; they had obtained their supports, their conditions had matured, they had presented themselves like a flood, and they were bound to occur.

children.text: mayaitāni karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni
children.translated_text: These deeds were done and accumulated by me.

children.text: ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante nābdhātau na tejodhātau na vāyudhātau api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca
children.translated_text: Who else will experience them? No, monks, deeds done and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element. Rather, deeds done, whether wholesome or unwholesome, ripen only in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases.

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇy api kalpaśatair api
children.translated_text: Deeds do not perish, even after hundreds of eons;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām ||
children.translated_text: having obtained the conjunction and the time, they indeed bear fruit for embodied beings.

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani candano nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān
children.translated_text: Formerly, monks, in the past, in a former time, a perfectly awakened Buddha named <s>Candana</s> arose in the world: a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an arhat, a perfectly awakened Buddha, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, knower of the world, unsurpassed guide of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One.

children.text: atha candanaḥ samyaksaṃbuddho janapadacārikāṃ carann anyatamāṃ rājadhānīm anuprāptaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Candana</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, while wandering on a tour through the countryside, arrived at a certain royal capital.

children.text: atha rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣikto yena candanaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ
children.translated_text: Then a consecrated kṣatriya king approached <s>Candana</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha.

children.text: upasaṃkramya candanasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte nyaṣīdat
children.translated_text: Having approached, he bowed with his head at the feet of <s>Candana</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, and sat down to one side.

children.text: ekānte niṣaṇṇaṃ rājānaṃ kṣatriyaṃ mūrdhābhiṣiktaṃ candanaḥ samyaksaṃbuddho bodhikarakair dharmaiḥ samādāpayati
children.translated_text: As the consecrated kṣatriya king sat to one side, <s>Candana</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, instructed him in teachings that lead to awakening.

children.text: atha rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣikta utthāyāsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena candanaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhas tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya candanaṃ samyaksaṃbuddham idam avocat adhivāsayatu me bhagavān asyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ traimāsyavāsāya sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃgheneti
children.translated_text: Then the consecrated kṣatriya king rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee on the ground, bowed with folded hands toward <s>Candana</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, and said this to <s>Candana</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha: “May the Blessed One consent to a three-month residence in this royal capital of mine together with the community of monks.”

children.text: adhivāsayati candanaḥ samyaksaṃbuddho rājñas tūṣṇībhāvena
children.translated_text: <s>Candana</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, consented to the king by silence.

children.text: tatra ca samayena mahatī anāvṛṣṭiḥ prādurbhūtā yayā nadyudapānāny alpasalilāni saṃvṛttāni puṣpaphalaviyuktāś ca pādapāḥ ||
children.translated_text: At that time a great drought appeared, by which the rivers and wells came to have little water, and the trees were left without flowers and fruit.

children.text: tato rājā candanaṃ samyaksaṃbuddham adhyeṣituṃ pravṛttaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the king began to entreat <s>Candana</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha.

children.text: bhagavann asmin nagaramadhye puṣkariṇīṃ gandhodakaparipūrṇāṃ kārayiṣyāmi yatra bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ snāsyati
children.translated_text: “Blessed One, in the middle of this city I will have a lotus pond made, filled with scented water, where the Blessed One together with the community of disciples will bathe.

children.text: apy eva nāma bhagavataḥ snānād asmin me vijite devo varṣed iti
children.translated_text: Perhaps, through the Blessed One’s bathing, the god will rain in this dominion of mine.”

children.text: adhivāsayati bhagavāṃś candanaḥ samyaksaṃbuddho rājñas tuṣṇībhāvena
children.translated_text: The Blessed One, <s>Candana</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, consented to the king by silence.

children.text: tato rājñā kṣatriyeṇa mūrdhābhiṣiktenāmātyebhya ājñā dattā gandhodakaṃ sajjīkurvantu bhavantaḥ ratnamayāṃś ca kumbhān yena vayaṃ bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaṃ snāpayiṣyāma iti
children.translated_text: Then the consecrated kṣatriya king gave an order to his ministers: “Sirs, prepare scented water and jewel-made pitchers, with which we shall bathe the Blessed One together with the community of disciples.”

children.text: tato rājñā amātyagaṇaparivṛtena tan nagaram apagatapāṣāṇaśarkarakaṭhallaṃ vyavasthāpitam ucchritadhvajapatākaṃ nānāpuṣpāvakīrṇaṃ gandhodakapariṣiktaṃ vicitradhūpadhūpitam
children.translated_text: Then, by the king surrounded by the group of ministers, that city was put in order: cleared of stones, gravel, and potsherds, with flags and banners raised, strewn with various flowers, sprinkled with scented water, and perfumed with varied incense.

children.text: puṣkariṇī cāsya kāritā
children.translated_text: And a lotus pond was constructed for him.

children.text: tato bhagavāṃś candanaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sarvānugrahārtham ekacīvarakaḥ puṣkariṇyāṃ sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, <s>Candana</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, for the benefit of all, stood in the lotus pond wearing a single robe.
