children.text: tato rājñāmātyagaṇaparivṛtena candanaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ saśrāvakasaṃgho nānāgandhaparibhāvitenodakena snāpitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Candana</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, together with the community of disciples, was bathed by the king surrounded by the group of ministers with water perfumed by many fragrances.

children.text: sahasnānād eva candanasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya śakreṇa devendreṇa tathāvidhaṃ māhendraṃ varṣam utsṛṣṭaṃ yena sarvasasyāni niṣpannāni
children.translated_text: At the very moment of the bathing of <s>Candana</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, released such an Indra-rain that all the crops came to fruition.

children.text: taddhaitukaṃ ca mahājanakāyena buddhe bhagavati śraddhā pratilabdhā
children.translated_text: Because of that, the great mass of people acquired faith in the Buddha, the Blessed One.

children.text: aneke ca gandhastūpāḥ pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ
children.translated_text: And many fragrant stūpas were established.

children.text: ye ca tatra candanaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ sarve te parinirvṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: And all those who there went for refuge to <s>Candana</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final nirvāṇa).

children.text: aham ekas teṣām avaśiṣṭaḥ
children.translated_text: I alone am left from among them.

children.text: tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam yacchāstāraṃ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, monks, you should train yourselves thus: “We will honor the Teacher, highly revere him, esteem him, and worship him.

children.text: śāstāraṃ satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvopaniśritya vihariṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Having honored the Teacher, highly revered him, esteemed him, worshiped him, and relied upon him, we will dwell.”

children.text: ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, should you train yourselves.”

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasas te ca bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: Those monks, pleased in mind, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.

children.text: Chapter 13

buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho rājagṛham upaniśritya viharati veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe
children.translated_text: The Buddha, the Blessed One, honored, highly revered, esteemed, and worshiped by kings, royal ministers, wealthy men, townspeople, guild leaders, caravan merchants, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, thus worshiped by gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, known as a Buddha, the Blessed One, of great merit and recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicines and requisites for sickness, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling near <s>Rājagṛha</s> in <s>Veṇuvana</s>, at <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s>.

children.text: tasmiṃś ca nāḍakanthāyāṃ mahājanamarako babhūva
children.translated_text: And at that time in <s>Nāḍakanthā</s> there was a great epidemic among the people.

children.text: tato janakāyo rogaiḥ pīḍitaḥ tāni tāni devatāsahasrāṇy āyācate śivavaruṇakuberavāsavādīni
children.translated_text: Then the populace, afflicted by diseases, entreated many thousands of deities, such as <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Vāsava</s>, and others.

children.text: na cāsya sā ītir upaśamaṃ gacchati
children.translated_text: But that calamity of theirs did not come to an end.

children.text: athānyatama upāsako nāḍakanthāyāṃ prativasati
children.translated_text: Then a certain lay follower was living in <s>Nāḍakanthā</s>.

children.text: sa nāḍakantheyān brāhmaṇagṛhapatīn idam avocat eta yūyaṃ buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchata taṃ ca bhagavantam āyācadhvam ihāgamanāya
children.translated_text: He said this to the brahmins and householders of <s>Nāḍakanthā</s>: “Come, you should go for refuge to the Buddha, and entreat that Blessed One to come here.

children.text: apy eva bhagavatā svalpakṛcchreṇāsyā īter vyupaśamaḥ syād iti
children.translated_text: Perhaps, through the Blessed One, this calamity would be brought to an end with little difficulty.”

children.text: atha nāḍakantheyā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo bhagavantam āyācituṃ pravṛttāḥ āgacchatu bhagavān asmād vyasanasaṃkaṭān mocanāyeti ||
children.translated_text: Then the brahmins and householders of <s>Nāḍakanthā</s> began to entreat the Blessed One: “May the Blessed One come to deliver us from this calamity and distress.”

children.text: atrāntare nāsti kiṃcid buddhānāṃ bhagavatām ajñātam adṛṣṭam aviditam avijñātam
children.translated_text: In the meantime, there is nothing at all that is unknown, unseen, unrecognized, or not fully understood by the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.

children.text: dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahākāruṇikānāṃ lokānugrahapravṛttakānām ekārakṣāṇāṃ śamathavipaśyanāvihāriṇāṃ tridamathavastukuśalānāṃ caturoghottīrṇānāṃ caturṛddhipādacaraṇatalasupratiṣṭhitānāṃ caturṣu saṃgrahavastuṣu dīrgharātrakṛtaparicayānāṃ pañcāṅgaviprahīṇānāṃ pañcagatisamatikrāntānāṃ ṣaḍaṅgasamanvāgatānāṃ ṣaṭpāramitāparipūrṇānāṃ saptabodhyaṅgakusumāḍhyānām aṣṭāṅgamārgadeśikānāṃ navānupūrvavihārasamāpattikuśalānāṃ daśabalabalināṃ daśadiksamāpūrṇayaśasāṃ daśaśatavaśavartiprativiśiṣṭānāṃ trī rātres trir divasasya ca buddhacakṣuṣā lokaṃ vyavalokya jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate ko hīyate ko vardhate kaḥ kṛcchraprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃkaṭaprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃbādhaprāptaḥ kaḥ kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasaṃbādhaprāptaḥ ko 'pāyanimnaḥ ko 'pāyapravaṇaḥ ko 'pāyaprāgbhāraḥ
children.translated_text: Indeed, it is the nature of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who are greatly compassionate, engaged in benefiting the world, sole protectors, dwelling in calm and insight, skilled in the three means of taming, crossed beyond the four floods, their feet firmly set on the four bases of miraculous power, long familiar with the four means of gathering, rid of the five factors, gone beyond the five destinies, endowed with the six factors, having fulfilled the six perfections, rich with the flowers of the seven limbs of awakening, teachers of the eightfold path, skilled in the attainments of the nine successive abodes, strong with the ten powers, whose fame fills the ten directions, and distinguished beyond those who hold sway over ten hundreds, that three times by night and three times by day, after surveying the world with the Buddha-eye, their knowledge and vision arise: Who is declining? Who is prospering? Who has fallen into hardship? Who has fallen into danger? Who has fallen into distress? Who has fallen into hardship, danger, and distress? Who is sunk toward the lower realms? Who leans toward the lower realms? Who is heading toward the lower realms?

children.text: kam aham apāyād uddhṛtya svarge mokṣe ca pratiṣṭhāpayeyam kasya kāmapaṅkanimagnasya hastoddhāram anupradadyām kam āryadhanavirahitam āryadhanaiśvaryādhipatye pratiṣṭhāpayeyam kasyājñānatimirapaṭalaparyavanaddhanetrasya jñānāñjanaśalākayā cakṣur viśodhayāmi
children.translated_text: Whom shall I lift out of the lower realms and establish in heaven and liberation? To whom, sunk in the mire of sensual desire, shall I extend a helping hand? Whom, lacking noble wealth, shall I establish in the sovereignty and lordship of noble wealth? Whose eye, covered by the mass of the darkness of ignorance, shall I cleanse with the probe of the collyrium of knowledge?

children.text: kasyānavaropitāni kuśalamūlāny avaropayeyam kasyāvaropitāni paripācayeyam kasya paripakvāni vimocayeyam
children.translated_text: For whom shall I plant roots of good that have not been planted? Whose planted roots shall I ripen? Whose ripened roots shall I liberate?

children.text: āha ca
children.translated_text: And it is said:

children.text: apy evātikramed velāṃ sāgaro makarālayaḥ
children.translated_text: The ocean, abode of makaras, might perhaps pass beyond its shore;

children.text: na tu vaineyavatsānāṃ buddho velām atikramet ||
children.translated_text: but the Buddha would not pass beyond the proper time for the calves who are to be trained.

children.text: atha bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto nāḍakanthām anuprāptaḥ
children.translated_text: Then in the forenoon the Blessed One dressed, took his bowl and robe, and, surrounded by a group of monks and preceded by the community of monks, reached <s>Nāḍakanthā</s>.

children.text: tato bhagavatā tan nagaraṃ sarvaṃ hṛdimaitryā sphuṭam yato marakāḥ prakrāntāḥ ītiś ca vyupaśāntā
children.translated_text: Then that whole city was pervaded by the Blessed One with loving-kindness from his heart; from that the death-bringing afflictions departed, and the calamity subsided.

children.text: tatas teṣāṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnāṃ buddhadarśanān mahāprasāda utpannaḥ prasādajātaiś ca bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ saṃpravāritaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, from seeing the Buddha, great faith arose among those brahmins and householders; and when faith had arisen, they invited the Blessed One, together with the community of disciples, to accept robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicines and requisites for sickness.

children.text: tatas tebhyo bhagavatā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā yāṃ śrutvā anekair brāhmaṇagṛhapatibhiḥ srotaāpattiphalam anuprāptam aparaiḥ sakṛdāgāmiphalam aparaiḥ anāgāmiphalam aparaiḥ pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One gave them such a <s>Dharma</s> teaching leading to penetration of the four noble truths that, after hearing it, many brahmins and householders attained the fruit of stream-entry; others attained the fruit of once-returning, others the fruit of non-returning, and others, having gone forth, through the abandonment of all defilements directly realized arhatship.

children.text: sarvaṃ ca tan nagaraṃ buddhanimnaṃ dharmapravaṇaṃ saṃghaprāgbhāraṃ saṃvṛttam ||
children.translated_text: And that entire city became sloping toward the Buddha, inclined to the <s>Dharma</s>, and leaning toward the <s>Saṃgha</s>.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ āścaryaṃ bhadanta yāvad ime sattvā bhagavataḥ prasādād vyasanagatāḥ santo vyasanāt parimuktā iti
children.translated_text: The monks, filled with doubt, asked the Buddha, the Blessed One, the cutter off of all doubts: It is wonderful, venerable sir, how these beings, though fallen into disaster, have been freed from disaster through the Blessed One's grace.

children.text: bhagavān āha tathāgatenaivaitāni bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: Monks, these deeds were previously done and accumulated by the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself in other births; their requisites had been obtained, their conditions had matured, they had come upon him like a flood, and they were bound to occur.

children.text: mayaitāni karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni
children.translated_text: These deeds were done and accumulated by me.

children.text: ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante nābdhātau na tejodhātau na vāyudhātau api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca
children.translated_text: Who else will experience their result? Monks, deeds done and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element; rather, deeds done, wholesome and unwholesome, ripen only in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases.

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api
children.translated_text: Karmic deeds do not perish, even in hundreds of crores of eons;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām ||
children.translated_text: having met with the conjunction and the time, they bear fruit for embodied beings.

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani candro nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān
children.translated_text: Once, monks, in the past, in a former age, a perfectly awakened Buddha named <s>Candra</s> arose in the world: a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an arhat, a perfectly awakened Buddha, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, knower of the world, unsurpassed guide of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One.

children.text: atha candraḥ samyaksaṃbuddho janapadacārikāṃ carann anyatamāṃ rājadhānīm anuprāptaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Candra</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, while traveling on a tour through the countryside, reached a certain royal capital.

children.text: aśrauṣīd rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣiktaḥ candraḥ samyaksaṃbuddho 'smākaṃ vijitam anuprāpta iti
children.translated_text: A consecrated kṣatriya king heard that <s>Candra</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, had arrived in our realm.

children.text: śrutvā ca punar mahatyā rājarddhyā mahatā rājānubhāvena samanvāgato yena candraḥ samyaksaṃbuddhas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ
children.translated_text: Having heard this, endowed with great royal splendor and great royal authority, he approached <s>Candra</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha.

children.text: upasaṃkramya candrasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte nyaṣīdat
children.translated_text: Having approached, he bowed with his head to the feet of <s>Candra</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, and sat down to one side.

children.text: ekāntaniṣaṇṇaṃ rājānaṃ kṣatriyaṃ mūrdhābhiṣiktaṃ candraḥ samyaksaṃbuddho bodhikarakair dharmaiḥ samādāpayati
children.translated_text: As the consecrated kṣatriya king sat to one side, <s>Candra</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, instructed him in teachings that produce awakening.

children.text: atha rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣikto labdhaprasāda utthāyāsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena candraḥ samyaksaṃbuddhas tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya candraṃ samyaksaṃbuddham idam avocat adhivāsayatu me bhagavān iha vāsaṃ traimāsyaṃ sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghena
children.translated_text: Then the consecrated kṣatriya king, having gained faith, rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, set his right knee on the ground, bowed with joined palms toward <s>Candra</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, and said this to <s>Candra</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha: "Let the Blessed One consent to a three-month residence here, together with the community of monks.

children.text: ahaṃ bhagavantaṃ upasthāsyāmi cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārair iti
children.translated_text: I will serve the Blessed One with robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicines and requisites for sickness."

children.text: adhivāsayati candraḥ samyaksaṃbuddho rājñas tūṣṇībhāvena
children.translated_text: <s>Candra</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, consented to the king by silence.

children.text: tasya ca rājño nagare tena samayena mahājanamarako babhūva ītiś ca yena sa mahājanakāyo 'tīva saṃtarpyate
children.translated_text: And in that king's city at that time there was a great mortality among the people, a calamity by which that great populace was severely afflicted.

children.text: tato rājñā vyādhipraśamanārthaṃ candraḥ samyaksaṃbuddho 'dhīṣṭaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the king entreated <s>Candra</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, for the sake of pacifying the disease.

children.text: sādhu bhagavan kriyatām asyā īter upaśamopāya iti
children.translated_text: "Good, Blessed One, let some means be made for pacifying this calamity."

children.text: tato bhagavāṃś candraḥ samyaksaṃbuddho rājānam uvāca gaccha mahārāja imāṃ saṃghāṭīṃ dhvajāgre baddhvā mahatā satkāreṇa sve vijite paryāṭaya asya ca mahāntam utsavaṃ kuru
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One <s>Candra</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, said to the king: "Go, great king. Tie this <s>saṃghāṭī</s> (outer monastic robe) to the top of a banner and, with great honor, have it carried throughout your dominion; and hold a great festival for it.

children.text: sarvaṃ ca mahājanakāyaṃ buddhānusmṛtau samādāpayeti
children.translated_text: And cause the whole great populace to undertake mindfulness of the Buddha.

children.text: te svastir bhaviṣyatīti
children.translated_text: There will be well-being for you."

children.text: tato rājñā yathānuśiṣṭaṃ sarvaṃ tathaiva ca kṛtam
children.translated_text: Then the king did everything just as he had been instructed.

children.text: taddhetutatpratyayaṃ ca sarvā ītayaḥ praśāntāḥ
children.translated_text: And with that as cause and condition, all the calamities were pacified.

children.text: tataḥ sa janakāyo labdhaprasādo rājāmātyapaurāś ca buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ dharmaṃ saṃghaṃ ca śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then that populace, having gained faith, and the king, ministers, and townspeople went for refuge to the Buddha; they went for refuge to the <s>Dharma</s> (teaching) and the <s>Saṃgha</s> (community).

children.text: bhagavān āha kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena rājā babhūva ahaṃ saḥ
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "What do you think, monks? The one who at that time, on that occasion, was the king was I.

children.text: mayāsau candrasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya mahatī pūjā kṛtā
children.translated_text: I made that great worship for <s>Candra</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha.

children.text: tasya me karmaṇo vipākena devamanuṣyasaṃprāpakaṃ saṃsāre mahatsukham anubhūtam
children.translated_text: By the ripening of that karma I experienced in <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth) great happiness leading to birth among gods and humans.

children.text: idānīm api taddhaituky eva vibhūtiḥ yena yaccintayāmi yat prārthaye tat tathaiva sarvaṃ samṛdhyati
children.translated_text: Even now there is prosperity precisely because of that, so that whatever I think of and whatever I wish for, all of it succeeds just so.

children.text: tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam yacchāstāraṃ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, monks, you should train yourselves thus: 'We will honor the Teacher, revere him, esteem him, and worship him.

children.text: śāstāraṃ satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvopaniśritya vihariṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Having honored the Teacher, revered him, esteemed him, worshiped him, and relied upon him, we will dwell.'

children.text: ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, should you train yourselves."

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasas te ca bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: Those monks, pleased in mind, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.

children.text: Chapter 14

buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho rājagṛham upaniśritya viharati sma veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe
children.translated_text: The Buddha, the Blessed One, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshiped by kings, royal ministers, wealthy men, townspeople, guild leaders, caravan merchants, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, thus worshiped by gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, known as the Buddha, the Blessed One, of great merit and recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicines and requisites for sickness, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling near <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in <s>Veṇuvana</s>, at <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s>.

children.text: yadā rājñā ajātaśatruṇā devadattavigrāhitena pitā dhārmiko dharmarājo jīvitād vyaparopitaḥ svayam eva ca rājye pratiṣṭhitaḥ tadā ye aśrāddhās te balavanto jātāḥ śrāddhās tu durbalāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ
children.translated_text: When King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, alienated by <s>Devadatta</s>, had deprived his father, the righteous dharma-king, of life and had established himself in the kingdom, then those without faith became powerful, while those with faith became weak.

children.text: yāvad anyatamo vṛddhāmātyo 'śrāddho bhagavacchāsanavidveṣī sa brāhmaṇebhyo yajñam ārabdho yaṣṭum
children.translated_text: At length a certain aged minister, faithless and hostile to the Blessed One's teaching, began to perform a sacrifice for the brahmins.

children.text: tatrānekāni brāhmaṇaśatasahasrāṇi saṃnipatitāni
children.translated_text: Many hundreds of thousands of brahmins assembled there.

children.text: taiḥ kriyākāraḥ kṛtaḥ na kenacicchramaṇagautamaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkramitavyam
children.translated_text: They made a formal agreement: "No one is to approach <s>Śramaṇa Gautama</s> to see him."

children.text: atha te brāhmaṇāḥ kṛtāvayaḥ samagrāḥ saṃmodamānā vīthīmadhye vedoktena vidhinā śakram āyācituṃ pravṛttāḥ ehyehi ahalyājāra ||
children.translated_text: Then those brahmins, their arrangements made, united and rejoicing, began in the middle of the street to invoke <s>Śakra</s> according to the Vedic rule: "Come, come, lover of <s>Ahalyā</s>!"

children.text: atrāntare nāsti kiṃcid buddhānāṃ bhagavatām ajñātam adṛṣṭam aviditam avijñātam
children.translated_text: Meanwhile, there is nothing that is unknown, unseen, unrecognized, or uncomprehended by the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.

children.text: dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahākāruṇikānāṃ lokānugrahapravṛttakānām ekārakṣāṇāṃ śamathavipaśyanāvihāriṇāṃ tridamathavastukuśalānāṃ caturoghottīrṇānāṃ caturṛddhipādacaraṇatalasupratiṣṭhitānāṃ caturṣu saṃgrahavastuṣu dīrgharātrakṛtaparicayānāṃ pañcāṅgaviprahīṇānāṃ pañcagatisamatikrāntānāṃ ṣaḍaṅgasamanvāgatānāṃ ṣaṭpāramitāparipūrṇānāṃ saptabodhyaṅgakusumāḍhyānām aṣṭāṅgamārgadeśikānāṃ navānupūrvavihārasamāpattikuśalānāṃ daśabalabalināṃ daśadiksamāpūrṇayaśasāṃ daśaśatavaśavartiprativiśiṣṭānāṃ trī rātres trir divasasya ca buddhacakṣuṣā lokaṃ vyavalokya jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate ko hīyate ko vardhate kaḥ kṛcchraprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃkaṭaprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃbādhaprāptaḥ kaḥ kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasaṃbādhaprāptaḥ ko 'pāyanimnaḥ ko 'pāyapravaṇaḥ ko 'pāyaprāgbhāraḥ
children.translated_text: For it is the nature of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who are greatly compassionate, intent on benefiting the world, protected by the single guard, dwelling in calm and insight, skilled in the three objects of taming, crossed beyond the four floods, with the soles of their feet firmly established on the four bases of miraculous power, long practiced in the four means of attracting beings, free of the five factors, gone beyond the five destinies, endowed with the six factors, perfected in the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), rich with the flowers of the seven factors of awakening, teachers of the eightfold path, skilled in the attainments of the nine successive abidings, strong with the strength of the ten powers, whose fame fills the ten directions, and distinguished above ten hundreds of <s>Vaśavartins</s>, that three times in the night and three times by day they survey the world with the Buddha-eye, and knowledge and vision arise: "Who is declining? Who is increasing? Who has fallen into hardship? Who has fallen into danger? Who has fallen into constraint? Who has fallen into hardship, danger, and constraint? Who slopes toward the lower realms? Who inclines toward the lower realms? Who is headed downward to the lower realms?"

children.text: kam aham apāyād uddhṛtya svarge mokṣe ca pratiṣṭhāpayeyam kasya kāmapaṅkanimagnasya hastoddhāram anupradadyām kam āryadhanavirahitam āryadhanaiśvaryādhipatye pratiṣṭhāpayeyam kasyājñānatimirapaṭalaparyavanaddhanetrasya jñānāñjanaśalākayā cakṣur viśodhayāmi
children.translated_text: Whom shall I lift up from a bad destiny and establish in heaven and in liberation? To whom, sunk in the mud of desire, shall I extend a helping hand? Whom, lacking noble wealth, shall I establish in lordship over the riches of the noble ones? Whose eye, covered over by the mass of darkness of ignorance, shall I cleanse with the collyrium-stick of knowledge?

children.text: kasyānavaropitāni kuśalamūlāny avaropayeyam kasyāvaropitāni paripācayeyam kasya paripakvāni vimocayeyam
children.translated_text: For whom shall I plant roots of good that have not been planted? Whose planted roots shall I bring to maturity? Whose matured roots shall I bring to release?

children.text: āha ca
children.translated_text: And it is said:

children.text: apy evātikramed velāṃ sāgaro makarālayaḥ
children.translated_text: The ocean, abode of sea-monsters, might perhaps overstep its shore;

children.text: na tu vaineyavatsānāṃ buddho velām atikramet ||
children.translated_text: but the Buddha does not let the proper time pass for his dear ones who are to be trained.

children.text: paśyati bhagavān ime brāhmaṇāḥ pūrvāvaropitakuśalamūlā gṛhītamokṣamārgāḥ svahitaiṣiṇo 'bhimukhā nirvāṇe bahirmukhāḥ saṃsārād akalyāṇamitrasaṃsargād idānīṃ macchāsanaṃ vidviṣanti yannvaham eṣāṃ vinayahetor autsukyam āpadyeyeti
children.translated_text: The Blessed One saw: "These brāhmaṇas have roots of good planted in the past, have taken up the path to liberation, seek their own welfare, are turned toward <s>nirvāṇa</s> and away from <s>saṃsāra</s>; but because of association with bad friends they now hate my teaching. What if I were to make an effort for the sake of training them?"

children.text: atha bhagavāñchakraveṣam abhinirmāya taṃ yajñavāṭaṃ divyenāvabhāsenāvabhāsya avataritum ārabdhaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One created the appearance of <s>Śakra</s>, illuminated that sacrificial enclosure with divine radiance, and began to descend.

children.text: tatas te brāhmaṇā hṛṣṭatuṣṭapramuditā udagraprītisaumanasyajātā ekasamūhenoktavantaḥ ehy ehi bhagavan svāgataṃ bhagavata iti
children.translated_text: Then those brāhmaṇas, thrilled, satisfied, delighted, and filled with exultant joy and gladness, said all together, "Come, come, Blessed One. Welcome to the Blessed One."

children.text: tato bhagavān śakraveṣadhārī prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, wearing the guise of <s>Śakra</s>, sat down on the seat that had been prepared.

children.text: eṣa śabdo rājagṛhe samantato visṛtaḥ yajñe śakro devendro 'vatīrṇa iti
children.translated_text: This report spread on every side in <s>Rājagṛha</s>: "At the sacrifice <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, has descended."

children.text: yaṃ śrutvānekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi saṃnipatitāni
children.translated_text: On hearing it, many hundreds of thousands of living beings assembled.

children.text: tato bhagavān āvarjitā brāhmaṇā iti viditvā śakraveṣam antardhāpya buddhaveṣeṇaiva sthitvā tādṛśīṃ caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikīṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kṛtavān yāṃ śrutvā ṣaṣṭyā brāhmaṇasahasrair viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhittvā srotaāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam anekaiś ca prāṇiśatasahasrairbhagavati śraddhā pratilabdhā ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, knowing that the brāhmaṇas had been won over, caused the guise of <s>Śakra</s> to disappear and, remaining in his very Buddha-form, gave such a <s>Dharma</s> teaching leading to penetration of the four noble truths that, after hearing it, sixty thousand brāhmaṇas split apart with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of satkāyadṛṣṭi (identity-view), risen with twenty peaks, and directly realized the fruit of stream-entry; and many hundreds of thousands of living beings gained faith in the Blessed One.

children.text: tato bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ āścaryaṃ bhadanta yāvad ebhir brāhmaṇair bhagavantam āgatya satyadarśanaṃ kṛtam anekaiś ca prāṇiśatasahasrair mahān prasādo 'dhigata iti
children.translated_text: Then the monks, filled with doubt, asked the Buddha, the Blessed One, the cutter-off of all doubts, "It is marvelous, venerable sir, how these brāhmaṇas came to the Blessed One and saw the truth, and how many hundreds of thousands of living beings attained great faith."

children.text: bhagavān āha tathāgatenaitāni bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "Monks, these deeds were formerly done by the <s>Tathāgata</s> in other births: they were accumulated, had acquired their requisites, had matured conditions, had come to hand like a flood, and were inevitable.

children.text: mayaitāni karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni
children.translated_text: These deeds were done and accumulated by me.

children.text: ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante nābdhātau na tejodhātau na vāyudhātau api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca
children.translated_text: Who else will experience them? No, monks: deeds done and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element. Rather, deeds done ripen, both wholesome and unwholesome, precisely in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases.

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api
children.translated_text: Karmic actions do not perish even through hundreds of crores of eons;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām ||
children.translated_text: having reached the proper conjunction and time, they indeed bear fruit for embodied beings.

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani indradamano nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān
children.translated_text: Once, monks, in the past, in a former age, a perfectly awakened Buddha named <s>Indradamana</s> arose in the world: a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an arhat, a perfectly awakened Buddha, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, knower of the world, unsurpassed guide of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One.

children.text: sa janapadacārikāṃ carann anyatamāṃ rājadhānīm anuprāptaḥ
children.translated_text: While wandering on a tour through the countryside, he arrived at a certain royal capital.

children.text: sā rājadhānī tīrthikāvaṣṭabdhā
children.translated_text: That royal capital was dominated by non-Buddhist ascetics.

children.text: aśrauṣīd anyatamo rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣiktaḥ indradamanaḥ samyaksaṃbuddho 'smākaṃ vijitam anuprāpta iti
children.translated_text: A certain consecrated kṣatriya king heard, "<s>Indradamana</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, has arrived in our realm."

children.text: śrutvā ca punar mahatyā rājarddhyā mahatā rājānubhāvena samanvāgato yenendradamanaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ
children.translated_text: Having heard this, endowed with great royal magnificence and great royal power, he approached <s>Indradamana</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavata indradamanasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte niṣaṇṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Having approached, he bowed with his head at the feet of the Blessed One <s>Indradamana</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, and sat to one side.

children.text: ekānte niṣaṇṇaṃ rājānaṃ kṣatriyaṃ mūrdhābhiṣiktam indradamanaḥ samyaksaṃbuddho bodhikarakair dharmaiḥ samādāpayati
children.translated_text: As the consecrated kṣatriya king sat to one side, <s>Indradamana</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, instructed him in teachings that bring about awakening.

children.text: atha sa rājā labdhaprasāda utthāyāsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yenendradamanaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhas tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya indradamanaṃ samyaksaṃbuddham idam avocat adhivāsayatu me bhagavāṃstraimāsyavāsāya
children.translated_text: Then that king, having gained faith, rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, set his right knee on the ground, bowed with joined palms toward <s>Indradamana</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, and said this to <s>Indradamana</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha: "May the Blessed One accept from me a three-month residence.

children.text: ahaṃ bhagavantaṃ upasthāsyāmi cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārair iti
children.translated_text: I will attend upon the Blessed One with robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicines and requisites for sickness."

children.text: bhagavān āha asti te mahārāja vijite kaścid vihāro yatrāgantukā gamikāś ca bhikṣavo vāsaṃ kalpayiṣyantīti rājovāca nāsti bhagavan kiṃ tarhi tiṣṭhatu bhagavān ahaṃ vihāraṃ kārayiṣyāmi yatrāgantukā gamikāś ca bhikṣavo vāsaṃ kalpayiṣyantīti
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "Great king, is there in your realm any monastery where incoming and traveling monks may make their dwelling?" The king said, "There is none, Blessed One. In that case, let the Blessed One remain; I will have a monastery built where incoming and traveling monks may make their dwelling."

children.text: tato rājñā tathāgatasyārthe vihāraḥ kāritaḥ aviddhaprākāratoraṇo gavākṣaniryūhajālārdhacandravedikāpratimaṇḍita āstaraṇopeto jalādhārasampūrṇas tarugaṇaparivṛto nānāpuṣpaphalopetaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the king had a monastery built for the sake of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, furnished with an enclosing wall and gateways, adorned with windows, projecting balconies, lattices, half-moon railings, provided with coverings, filled with water reservoirs, surrounded by groups of trees, and supplied with various flowers and fruits.

children.text: kṛtvā ca bhagavataḥ saśrāvakasaṃghasya niryātitaḥ
children.translated_text: And having made it, he presented it to the Blessed One together with the community of disciples.

children.text: adhīṣṭaś ca bhagavān mahāprātihāryaṃ prati
children.translated_text: And the Blessed One was entreated with regard to a great miracle.

children.text: tato bhagavatā indradamanena samyaksaṃbuddhena rājño 'dhyeṣayā mahāprātihāryaṃ vidarśitaṃ buddhāvataṃsakavikrīḍitam yaddarśanād rājā sāmātyanaigamajānapadaḥ sarve ca nāgarāḥ suprasannāḥ śāsane saṃraktatarāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, at the king's request, the Blessed One, <s>Indradamana</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, displayed a great miracle, the sport of the Buddha-garland; at the sight of it the king, together with his ministers, townsmen, and country people, and all the citizens became deeply pleased and more strongly attached to the teaching.

children.text: bhagavān āha kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena rājā babhūva ahaṃ saḥ
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "What do you think, monks? He who at that time and on that occasion was the king was I myself.

children.text: mayā sā indradamanasya samyaksaṃbuddhasyaivaṃvidhā pūjā kṛtā
children.translated_text: By me such worship was performed for <s>Indradamana</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha.

children.text: tasya me karmaṇo vipākena saṃsāre 'nantaṃ sukham anubhūtam
children.translated_text: As the result of that deed, I experienced endless happiness in saṃsāra.

children.text: idānīṃ me tathāgatasya sata iyaṃ śāsanaśobhā
children.translated_text: Now, when I am a <s>Tathāgata</s>, this splendor of the teaching is mine.

children.text: tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam yacchāstāraṃ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, monks, you should train yourselves thus: 'We will honor the Teacher, highly revere him, esteem him, and worship him.

children.text: śāstāraṃ satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvopaniśritya vihariṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Having honored the Teacher, highly revered him, esteemed him, worshiped him, and relied upon him, we will dwell.'

children.text: ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, should you train yourselves."

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasas te ca bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: Those monks, pleased in mind, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.

children.text: Chapter 15

buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho rājagṛham upaniśritya viharati sma veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe
children.translated_text: The Buddha, the Blessed One, honored, highly revered, esteemed, and worshiped by kings, royal ministers, wealthy men, townspeople, guild leaders, caravan merchants, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, thus worshiped by gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, known as a Buddha, the Blessed One, of great merit and recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicines and requisites for sickness, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling near <s>Rājagṛha</s> in <s>Veṇuvana</s>, at <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s>.

children.text: yadā devadattena mohapuruṣeṇa bhagavacchāsane 'narthasahasrāṇi kṛtāni na ca śakitaṃ bhagavato romeñjanam api kartum tadā rājānam ajātaśatrum āmantritavān kriyatāṃ rājagṛhe kriyākāro na kenacicchramaṇasya gautamasyopasaṃkramitavyam piṇḍakena vā pratipādayitavyaḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Devadatta</s>, that deluded man, had done thousands of injuries to the Blessed One's teaching and yet had not been able to make even a hair of the Blessed One stir, he then addressed King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>: "Let an order be made in <s>Rājagṛha</s>: no one is to approach the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>, nor is he to be supplied even with a morsel of alms.

children.text: evam ayam alabdhalābho 'labdhasaṃmāno niyatam anyadeśaṃ saṃkrāntiṃ kariṣyatīti
children.translated_text: In this way, deprived of gain and deprived of honor, he will certainly move to another country."

children.text: rājñā tathā kāritam
children.translated_text: The king had it done in that way.

children.text: tatra ye upāsakā dṛṣṭasatyās te rodituṃ pravṛttāḥ hā kaṣṭam anāthībhūtaṃ rājagṛhanagaraṃ yatra hi nāmodumbarapuṣpadurlabhaprādurbhāvaṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantam āsādya tasya na śakyate saṃgrahaḥ kartum iti
children.translated_text: There those lay followers who had seen the truth began to weep: "Alas, misery! The city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> has become without a protector, where, having encountered the Buddha, the Blessed One, whose appearance is as rare as the udumbara flower, it is not possible to give him support."

children.text: eṣa śabdaḥ śrutiparaṃparayā bhikṣubhiḥ śrutaḥ
children.translated_text: This report, through a chain of hearing, was heard by the monks.

children.text: tata āyuṣmatānandena yathāśrutaṃ bhagavato niveditaḥ
children.translated_text: Then venerable <s>Ānanda</s> reported to the Blessed One what he had heard.

children.text: bhagavān āha alpotsukastvam ānanda bhava tathāgatā evātra kālajñāḥ
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "Be unconcerned, <s>Ānanda</s>; the <s>Tathāgatas</s> themselves know the proper time in this matter.

children.text: api tu yāvacchāsanaṃ me tāvacchrāvakāṇām upakaraṇavaikalyaṃ na bhaviṣyati prāg evedānīm iti ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, as long as my teaching lasts, there will be no lack of requisites for my disciples, all the more so now."

children.text: atrāntare śakrasya devānām indrasyādhastāj jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate
children.translated_text: Meanwhile, the knowledge and vision of <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, turned downward.

children.text: sa paśyati bhagavacchāsanasyaivaṃvidhāṃ vikṛtim
children.translated_text: He saw this kind of disturbance in the Blessed One's teaching.

children.text: sahadarśanād eva dāyakadānapatīnāṃ utsāhasaṃjananārthaṃ buddhotpādasya māhātmyasaṃjananārtham ajātaśatror devadattasya ca madadarpacchittyartham ātmanaś ca prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ sakalaṃ rājagṛham udāreṇāvabhāsenāvabhāsyoccaiḥśabdam udāharitavān eṣo 'ham adyāgreṇa bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaṃ divyaiś cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārair upasthāsyāmi
children.translated_text: As soon as he saw it, in order to arouse enthusiasm among donors and patrons, to produce an appreciation of the greatness of a Buddha's arising, to cut off the pride and arrogance of <s>Ajātaśatru</s> and <s>Devadatta</s>, and to generate faith in himself, he illuminated all <s>Rājagṛha</s> with a lofty radiance and proclaimed in a loud voice: "From this day forward I myself will attend the Blessed One together with the community of disciples with divine robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicines and requisites for sickness."

children.text: ity uktvā yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ
children.translated_text: Having said this, he approached the Blessed One.

children.text: upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Having approached, he bowed with his head to the Blessed One's feet and stood to one side.

children.text: atha śakro devendro bhagavantam idam avocat adhivāsayatu me bhagavān asminn eva rājagṛhe nagare
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One: "May the Blessed One accept my invitation here in this very city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>.

children.text: ahaṃ bhagavantam upasthāsyāmi cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārair iti
children.translated_text: I will attend the Blessed One with robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicines and requisites for sickness."

children.text: bhagavān āha alaṃ kauśika kṛtam etad yāvad eva cittam abhiprasannam
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "Enough, <s>Kauśika</s>; this is accomplished insofar as your mind is fully serene.

children.text: bahavo hi loke puṇyakāmā iti
children.translated_text: For there are many in the world who desire merit."

children.text: śakraḥ prāha adhivāsayatu me bhagavān pañca varṣāṇi
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said, "May the Blessed One accept from me for five years.

children.text: tathāgatasyārthe pañcavārṣikaṃ kariṣyāmīti
children.translated_text: I will perform a five-year offering for the sake of the <s>Tathāgata</s>."

children.text: bhagavān āha alaṃ kauśika kṛtam etad yāvaccittam abhiprasannam
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "Enough, <s>Kauśika</s>; this is accomplished insofar as your mind is fully serene.

children.text: bahavo hi loke puṇyakāmā iti
children.translated_text: For there are many in the world who desire merit."

children.text: śakraḥ prāha adhivāsayatu me bhagavān pañca divasān iti
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said, "May the Blessed One accept from me for five days."

children.text: tato bhagavān svapuṇyabalapratyakṣīkaraṇārthaṃ śakrasya ca devendrasyānugrahārtham anāgatapañcavārṣikaprabandhahetoś cādhivāsitavāṃstūṣṇībhāvena ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, in order to make manifest the power of his own merit, to show favor to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, and to establish the future continuation of five-year offerings, accepted by silence.

children.text: atha śakro devendro bhagavatas tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā tad veṇuvanaṃ vaijayantaṃ prāsādaṃ pradarśitavān divyāni cāsanāni divyāḥ puṣkariṇīr divyaṃ ca bhojanam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, knowing from the Blessed One's silence that he had accepted, displayed that <s>Veṇuvana</s> as the <s>Vaijayanta</s> palace, and displayed divine seats, divine lotus ponds, and divine food.

children.text: atha bhagavān prajñapta eva āsane niṣaṇṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One sat down on the very seat that had been prepared.

children.text: tataḥ śakro devendraḥ sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ viditvā anekadevatāsahasraparivṛtaḥ svahastaṃ saṃtarpayati saṃpravārayati
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, knowing that the community of monks headed by the Buddha was comfortably seated, surrounded by many thousands of deities, satisfied them and invited them to take more with his own hand.

children.text: anekaparyāyeṇa svahastaṃ saṃtarpya saṃpravārya bhagavantaṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastam apanītapātraṃ nīcataram āsanaṃ gṛhītvā bhagavataḥ purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya
children.translated_text: Having satisfied them and invited them to take more in many ways with his own hand, and knowing that the Blessed One had eaten, had washed his hands, and that the bowl had been taken away, he took a lower seat and sat down before the Blessed One to hear the <s>Dharma</s> (teaching).

children.text: tato bhagavān śakraṃ devendraṃ saparivāraṃ dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, with a discourse on <s>Dharma</s> (teaching), instructed, moved, encouraged, and delighted <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, together with his retinue.

children.text: paśyati ca rājā ajātaśatrur upariprāsādatalagataḥ san bhagavato veṇuvane evaṃvidhāṃ pūjāṃ
children.translated_text: And King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, being on the upper terrace of the palace, saw such worship of the Blessed One there in <s>Veṇuvana</s>.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punar vipratisārajāto mahāntaṃ prasādaṃ praveditavān
children.translated_text: Having seen it, he became remorseful and produced great faith.

children.text: rājagṛhanivāsinaś ca paurā dharmavegaprāptā rājānam upasaṃkramyaivam ūcuḥ muṣyante deva mahārāja rājagṛhanivāsinaḥ paurāḥ yatra nāma devāḥ pramattāḥ santaḥ pramādavihāriṇo divyān viṣayān apahāya bhagavantaṃ pūjayanti
children.translated_text: And the townspeople living in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, seized with urgency for the <s>Dharma</s> (teaching), approached the king and said this: "Your Majesty, great king, the townspeople living in <s>Rājagṛha</s> are being deprived, when even the gods, though heedless and living in heedlessness, abandon divine pleasures and worship the Blessed One.

children.text: sādhu deva udghāṭyatāṃ kriyākāra iti ||
children.translated_text: It would be good, Your Majesty, if the formal restriction were lifted."

children.text: tato rājñā ajātaśatruṇā kriyākāram udghāṭya rājagṛhe nagare ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kāritam kriyatāṃ bhagavataḥ satkāro yathāsukham iti
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, having lifted the formal restriction, caused a bell proclamation to be made in the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>: "Let honor be done to the Blessed One as each one wishes."

children.text: tato rājagṛhanivāsinaḥ paurāḥ saparivārā hṛṣṭatuṣṭapramuditā udagraprītisaumanasyajātāḥ puṣpagandhamālyāny ādāya bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāntāḥ
children.translated_text: Then the townspeople living in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, together with their retinues, thrilled, satisfied, glad, and filled with uplifted joy and gladness of mind, took flowers, perfumes, and garlands and approached to see the Blessed One.

children.text: tato devair manuṣyaiś ca bhagavato mahān satkāraḥ kṛtaḥ bhagavatā ca tad adhiṣṭhānaṃ devamanuṣyāṇāṃ tādṛśī caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā yāṃ śrutvā anekair devamanuṣyaiḥ satyadarśanaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Then by gods and humans great honor was done to the Blessed One. And the Blessed One, taking that assembly of gods and humans as his occasion, gave such a <s>Dharma</s> teaching leading to penetration of the four noble truths that, after hearing it, many gods and humans saw the truth.

children.text: bhikṣavo bhagavataḥ pūjāṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃśayajātā buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ āścaryaṃ bhadanta yad bhagavataḥ śāsane evaṃvidha utsava iti
children.translated_text: The monks, seeing the worship of the Blessed One, became doubtful and asked the Buddha, the Blessed One, "It is marvelous, venerable sir, that there is such a festival in the Blessed One's teaching."

children.text: bhagavān āha tathāgatenaivaitāni bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "Monks, these deeds were formerly done by the <s>Tathāgata</s> (Thus-Gone One) himself in other births: they were accumulated, had obtained their requisites, had matured conditions, had come to hand like a flood, and were inevitable.

children.text: mayaitāni karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni
children.translated_text: These deeds were done and accumulated by me.

children.text: ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante nābdhātau na tejodhātau na vāyudhātau api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca
children.translated_text: Who else will experience them? No, monks, deeds done and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element. Rather, deeds done, both wholesome and unwholesome, ripen precisely in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases.

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api
children.translated_text: Karmic actions do not perish even through hundreds of crores of eons;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām ||
children.translated_text: having reached the proper conjunction and time, they indeed bear fruit for embodied beings.

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani ratnaśailo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān
children.translated_text: Formerly, monks, in the past, in a bygone age, there arose in the world a perfectly awakened Buddha named <s>Ratnaśaila</s>: a <s>Tathāgata</s> (Thus-Gone One), an arhat, a perfectly awakened Buddha, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, knower of the world, unsurpassed guide of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One.

children.text: sa janapadacārikāṃ carann anyatamāṃ rājadhānīm anuprāptaḥ
children.translated_text: Wandering on a tour through the countryside, he arrived at a certain royal capital.

children.text: tasyāṃ ca rājadhānyāṃ dharmabuddhir nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati tasyāṃ ca rājadhānyāṃ mahatī ītiḥ
children.translated_text: And in that royal capital a king named <s>Dharmabuddhi</s> was ruling, and in that royal capital there was a great calamity.

children.text: tatas tena rājñā ītipraśamanahetor bhagavān śrāvakasaṃghatraimāsye bhaktenopanimantritaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, for the sake of pacifying the calamity, that king invited the Blessed One, together with the community of disciples, for a three-month period with meals.

children.text: tato rājño nāgaraiś cāvarjitamānasaistathāgatasya saśrāvakasaṃghasya pañcavārṣikaṃ kṛtam
children.translated_text: Then, with the minds of the king and the townspeople won over, a <s>pañcavārṣika</s> (five-year festival) was held for the <s>Tathāgata</s> (Thus-Gone One) together with the community of disciples.

children.text: āha ca
children.translated_text: And he said:

children.text: rājabhūtena ānanda ratnaśailo mahādyutiḥ
children.translated_text: "When I had become a king, <s>Ānanda</s>, I invited the greatly radiant <s>Ratnaśaila</s>;

children.text: adhīṣṭaḥ śāntikāmena akārṣīt pañcavārṣikam ||
children.translated_text: desiring pacification, I held a <s>pañcavārṣika</s> (five-year festival).

children.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena rājā babhūva ahaṃ saḥ
children.translated_text: What do you think, monks? The one who at that time, on that occasion, was the king was I.

children.text: yan mayā ratnaśailasya tathāgatasya pañcavārṣikaṃ kṛtam tena me saṃsāre mahatsukham anubhūtam
children.translated_text: Because I held a <s>pañcavārṣika</s> (five-year festival) for the <s>Tathāgata</s> (Thus-Gone One) <s>Ratnaśaila</s>, through that I experienced great happiness in <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth).

children.text: taddhaitukaś cedānīṃ tathāgatasyaivaṃvidhaḥ satkāraḥ
children.translated_text: And because of that, now too there is such honor for the <s>Tathāgata</s> (Thus-Gone One).

children.text: parinirvṛtasya ca me śāsane anekāni pañcavārṣikaśatāni bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: And after I have passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final nirvāṇa), there will be many hundreds of <s>pañcavārṣikas</s> (five-year festivals) in my teaching.

children.text: tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam yacchāstāraṃ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, monks, you should train yourselves thus: 'We will honor the Teacher, revere him, esteem him, and worship him.

children.text: śāstāraṃ satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvopaniśritya vihariṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Having honored the Teacher, revered him, esteemed him, worshiped him, and relied upon him, we will dwell.'

children.text: ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, should you train yourselves."

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasas te ca bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: Those monks, pleased in mind, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.

children.text: Chapter 16

buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme
children.translated_text: The Buddha, the Blessed One, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshiped by kings, royal ministers, wealthy men, townspeople, guild leaders, caravan merchants, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, thus worshiped by gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, known as the Buddha, the Blessed One, of great merit and recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicines and requisites for sickness, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, in the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.

children.text: tena khalu samayena śrāvastyāṃ pañcamātrāṇi gāndharvikaśatāni goṣṭhikānāṃ prativasanti
children.translated_text: At that time in <s>Śrāvastī</s> there lived five hundred musicians belonging to guilds.

children.text: tatra ca kāle supriyo nāma gāndharvikarājo 'bhyāgataḥ
children.translated_text: And at that time a king of musicians named <s>Supriya</s> arrived.

children.text: tasyaivaṃvidhā śaktiḥ ekasyāṃ tantryāṃ sapta svarān ādarśayati ekaviṃśatiṃ mūrcchanāḥ
children.translated_text: Such was his power: on a single string he could display seven notes and twenty-one modes.

children.text: sa ṣaṇmahānagarāṇy apaṭukāny udghoṣayamāṇaḥ śrāvastīm anuprāptaḥ
children.translated_text: He reached <s>Śrāvastī</s>, proclaiming the six great cities to be unskilled.

children.text: śrāvastīnivāsibhiś ca gāndharvikai rājñe niveditam
children.translated_text: The musicians living in <s>Śrāvastī</s> reported this to the king.

children.text: rājāha alpotsukā bhavantu bhavantaḥ vayam atra kālajñā bhaviṣyāma iti ||
children.translated_text: The king said, "Gentlemen, be without much anxiety; in this matter we shall know the proper time."

children.text: atha supriyasya gāndharvikarājasyaitad abhavat evam anuśrūyate rājā prasenajid gāndharve 'tīva kuśalaḥ
children.translated_text: Then this occurred to <s>Supriya</s>, the king of musicians: "So it is reported that King <s>Prasenajit</s> is exceedingly skilled in music.

children.text: yannvaham anena saha vādam ārocayeyam iti
children.translated_text: What if I were to arrange a contest with him?"

children.text: tataḥ supriyo gāndharvikarājo yena rājā prasenajit kauśalas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Supriya</s>, the king of musicians, went to where King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s> was.

children.text: upasaṃkramya rājānaṃ prasenajitaṃ kauśalam idam avocat śrutaṃ me rājan yathā tvaṃ gāndharvakuśala iti
children.translated_text: Having approached, he said this to King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s>: "I have heard, O king, that you are skilled in music.

children.text: yadi te aguru mīmāṃsasveti
children.translated_text: If it is not burdensome to you, test me."

children.text: tato rājñā prasenajitā tasya vikṣepaḥ kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> deflected him.

children.text: uktaś ca sādho asti me gurur jetavane sthito 'nuttaro gāndharvikarājaḥ
children.translated_text: And he said, "Good sir, I have a teacher staying in <s>Jetavana</s>, an unsurpassed king of musicians.

children.text: ehi tatsamīpaṃ yāsyāma iti
children.translated_text: Come; let us go to him."

children.text: atha rājā prasenajit kauśalaḥ pañcamātrair gāndharvikaśataiḥ parivṛtaḥ supriyeṇa gāndharvikarājenānekaiś ca prāṇiśatasahasrair jetavanaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s>, surrounded by about five hundred musicians, together with <s>Supriya</s> the king of musicians and many hundreds of thousands of living beings, went to <s>Jetavana</s>.

children.text: atrāntare nāsti kiṃcid buddhānāṃ bhagavatām ajñātam adṛṣṭam aviditam avijñātam
children.translated_text: Meanwhile, there is nothing at all that is unknown, unseen, unrecognized, or uncomprehended by the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.

children.text: dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahākāruṇikānāṃ lokānugrahapravṛttakānām ekārakṣāṇāṃ śamathavipaśyanāvihāriṇāṃ tridamathavastukuśalānāṃ caturoghottīrṇānāṃ caturṛddhipādacaraṇatalasupratiṣṭhitānāṃ caturṣu saṃgrahavastuṣu dīrgharātrakṛtaparicayānāṃ pañcāṅgaviprahīṇānāṃ pañcagatisamatikrāntānāṃ ṣaḍaṅgasamanvāgatānāṃ ṣaṭpāramitāparipūrṇānāṃ saptabodhyaṅgakusumāḍhyānām aṣṭāṅgamārgadeśikānāṃ navānupūrvavihārasamāpattikuśalānāṃ daśabalabalināṃ daśadiksamāpūrṇayaśasāṃ daśaśatavaśavartiprativiśiṣṭānāṃ trī rātres trir divasasya ca buddhacakṣuṣā lokaṃ vyavalokya jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate ko hīyate ko vardhate kaḥ kṛcchraprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃkaṭaprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃbādhaprāptaḥ kaḥ kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasaṃbādhaprāptaḥ ko 'pāyanimnaḥ ko 'pāyapravaṇaḥ ko 'pāyaprāgbhāraḥ
children.translated_text: For it is the nature of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who are greatly compassionate, intent on benefiting the world, protected by the single guard, dwelling in calm and insight, skilled in the three objects of taming, crossed beyond the four floods, with the soles of their feet firmly established on the four bases of miraculous power, long practiced in the four means of attracting beings, free of the five factors, gone beyond the five destinies, endowed with the six factors, perfected in the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), rich with the flowers of the seven factors of awakening, teachers of the eightfold path, skilled in the attainments of the nine successive abidings, strong with the strength of the ten powers, whose fame fills the ten directions, and distinguished above ten hundreds of <s>Vaśavartins</s>, that three times in the night and three times by day they survey the world with the Buddha-eye, and knowledge and vision arise: "Who is declining? Who is increasing? Who has fallen into hardship? Who has fallen into danger? Who has fallen into constraint? Who has fallen into hardship, danger, and constraint? Who slopes toward the lower realms? Who inclines toward the lower realms? Who is headed downward to the lower realms?"

children.text: kam aham apāyād uddhṛtya svarge mokṣe ca pratiṣṭhāpayeyam kasya kāmapaṅkanimagnasya hastoddhāram anupradadyām kam āryadhanavirahitam āryadhanaiśvaryādhipatye pratiṣṭhāpayeyam kasyājñānatimirapaṭalaparyavanaddhanetrasya jñānāñjanaśalākayā cakṣur viśodhayāmi
children.translated_text: "Whom shall I lift up from a bad destiny and establish in heaven and in liberation? To whom, sunk in the mud of desire, shall I extend a helping hand? Whom, lacking noble wealth, shall I establish in lordship over the riches of the noble ones? Whose eye, covered over by the mass of darkness of ignorance, shall I cleanse with the collyrium-stick of knowledge?

children.text: kasyānavaropitāni kuśalamūlānyavaropayeyam kasyāvaropitāni paripācayeyam kasya paripakvāni vimocayeyam
children.translated_text: For whom shall I plant roots of good that have not been planted? Whose planted roots shall I bring to maturity? Whose matured roots shall I bring to release?"

children.text: āha ca
children.translated_text: And it is said:

children.text: apy evātikramed velāṃ sāgaro makarālayaḥ
children.translated_text: The ocean, abode of makaras, might perhaps overstep its shore;

children.text: na tu vaineyavatsānāṃ buddho velām atikramet ||
children.translated_text: but the Buddha would not let the proper time pass for his dear ones who are to be trained.

children.text: tato bhagavān vaineyajanānugrahārthaṃ laukikaṃ cittam utpāditavān
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, for the sake of benefiting the people to be trained, produced a worldly thought.

children.text: aho bata pañcaśikho gandharvaputraḥ saptagandharvasahasraparivṛto vaiḍūryadaṇḍāṃ vīṇām ādāya matsakāśam upasaṃkrāmed iti
children.translated_text: "Ah, if only <s>Pañcaśikha</s>, the gandharva youth, surrounded by seven thousand gandharvas, would take up his vīṇā with a beryl neck and approach my presence."

children.text: sahacittotpādāt pañcaśikho gandharvaputraḥ saptagandharvasahasraparivṛto bhagavantaṃ yathāvad abhyarcya bhagavato vaiḍūryadaṇḍāṃ vīṇām upanayati sma
children.translated_text: At the very arising of that thought, <s>Pañcaśikha</s>, the gandharva youth, surrounded by seven thousand gandharvas, duly worshiped the Blessed One and presented to the Blessed One the vīṇā with the beryl neck.

children.text: tataḥ supriyo gandharvarājo bhagavataḥ purastād vīṇām anuśrāvitum ārabdhaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Supriya</s>, the king of musicians, began to play the vīṇā before the Blessed One.

children.text: yata ekasyāṃ tantryāṃ sapta svarāṇi ekaviṃśatiṃ mūrcchanāś ca darśayitum ārabdhaḥ yacchravaṇād rājā prasenajid anyatamaś ca mahājanakāyaḥ paraṃ vismayam āpannaḥ
children.translated_text: On a single string he began to display seven notes and twenty-one modes; at the hearing of this, King <s>Prasenajit</s> and that great body of people were filled with supreme amazement.

children.text: tato bhagavān api vaiḍūryadaṇḍāṃ vīṇām āśrāvitavān yata ekaikasyāṃ tantryām aneke svaraviśeṣā mūrcchanāś ca bahuprakārā darśitāḥ te ca śūnyākāreṇaiva
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One too played the vīṇā with the beryl neck, so that on each single string many distinct notes and many kinds of modes were displayed; and these were precisely in the aspect of emptiness.

children.text: idaṃ ca śarīraṃ vīṇāvad ādarśitavān svarān indriyavat mūrcchanāś cittadhātuvat
children.translated_text: And he displayed this body as like a vīṇā, the tones as like the faculties, and the musical modes as like the elements of mind.

children.text: yacchravaṇād āvarjitaḥ supriyo gandharvarājo vīṇāṃ gandhakuṭyāṃ niryātya bhagavatsakāśe pravrajitaḥ
children.translated_text: On hearing that, <s>Supriya</s>, the gandharva king, was won over; he put aside his vīṇā in the perfumed chamber and went forth in the presence of the Blessed One.

children.text: tena yujyamānena ghaṭamānena vyāyacchamānena idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam
children.translated_text: As he applied himself, strove, and exerted himself, he understood this very five-knobbed wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> as moving and unstable; having overcome all courses of conditioned things as subject to shattering, falling, scattering, and destruction, he directly realized arhatship through the abandonment of all defilements.

children.text: arhan saṃvṛttaḥ traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhaḥ
children.translated_text: He became an arhat, free from passion for the three realms, regarding clods and gold alike, with a mind equal toward space and the palm of the hand, like sandalwood before the axe, his eggshell split open by knowledge, having attained knowledge, superknowledges, and analytical discernments, and turned away from existence, gain, greed, and honor.

children.text: sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He became worthy of worship, honor, and salutation by the gods, including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>.

children.text: tata āvarjitā devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragā bhagavacchāsane rakṣāvaraṇaguptiṃ kartum ārabdhāḥ
children.translated_text: Then the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, won over, began to provide protection, shelter, and guarding in the Blessed One's teaching.

children.text: pañcānām api gāndharvikaśatānāṃ prītisaumanasyajātānām etad abhavat vayaṃ nīce karmaṇi vartāmahe kṛcchravṛttayaś ca
children.translated_text: Joy and gladness arose in all five hundred gandharva musicians, and they thought, "We are engaged in low work and live with difficulty.

children.text: yannu vayaṃ rājānaṃ vijñāpya bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaṃ nagarapraveśenopanimantrayemahīti
children.translated_text: What if, after informing the king, we were to invite the Blessed One together with the community of disciples to enter the city?"

children.text: yāvat tair gāndharvikair labdhānujñair bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃgho nagarapraveśenopanimantritaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after those gandharvas had received permission, they invited the Blessed One together with the community of disciples to enter the city.

children.text: adhivāsitaṃ ca bhagavatā teṣāṃ gāndharvikāṇāṃ tūṣṇībhāvena
children.translated_text: And the Blessed One consented to those gandharvas by silence.

children.text: tatas tair gāndharvikair rājāmātyapaurajanapadasahāyaiḥ sarvā śrāvastī nagarī apagatapāṣāṇaśarkarakaṭhallā gandhodakapariṣiktā nānāpuṣpāvakīrṇā vicitradhūpadhūpitā puṣpavitānamaṇḍitā
children.translated_text: Then, with the help of the king, ministers, townspeople, and country people, those gandharvas prepared the whole city of <s>Śrāvastī</s>: its stones, gravel, and pebbles were removed, it was sprinkled with scented water, strewn with many kinds of flowers, perfumed with varied incense, and adorned with flower canopies.

children.text: te ca gāndharvikāḥ svayam eva vīṇām ādāya mṛdaṅgaveṇupaṇavādiviśeṣair upasthānaṃ cakruḥ praṇītena cāhāreṇa bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaṃ saṃtarpayāmāsuḥ ||
children.translated_text: And those gandharvas themselves, taking up vīṇās, performed attendance with special mṛdaṅga drums, flutes, paṇava drums, and the like; and with excellent food they satisfied the Blessed One together with the community of disciples.

children.text: tato bhagavān smitam akārṣīt
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One smiled.

children.text: dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhān niścārya kāścid adhastād gacchanti kāścid upariṣṭād gacchanti
children.translated_text: It is the nature of things that, at the time when Buddhas, Blessed Ones, display a smile, blue, yellow, red, and white rays issue from their mouths; some go downward and some go upward.

children.text: yā adhastād gacchanti tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanam avīcim arbudaṃ nirarbudaṃ aṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvam utpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaṃ narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakās teṣu śītībhūtā nipatanti ye śītanarakās teṣūṣṇībhūtā nipatanti
children.translated_text: Those that go downward go to the hells <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s>. In the hot hells they fall cooled; in the cold hells they fall warmed.

children.text: tena teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante
children.translated_text: By that, the special torments of those beings subside.

children.text: teṣām evaṃ bhavati kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ āhosvid anyatropapannā iti
children.translated_text: They think, "Good sirs, have we died from here, or have we been reborn somewhere else?"

children.text: teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati
children.translated_text: To generate faith in them, the Blessed One sends out an emanation.

children.text: teṣāṃ nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavati na hy eva vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ nāpy anyatropapannāḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that emanation, they think, "Surely we have not died from here, nor have we been reborn somewhere else.

children.text: api tv ayam apūrvadarśanaḥ sattvaḥ asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti
children.translated_text: Rather, by the power of this being never seen before, our special torments have subsided."

children.text: te nirmite cittam abhiprasādya tan narakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇanti yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti
children.translated_text: Having made their minds serene toward the emanation, they exhaust that karma to be experienced in hell and take rebirth among gods and humans, where they become vessels for the truths.

children.text: yā upariṣṭād gacchanti tāś cāturmahārājikāṃs trayastriṃśān yāmāṃs tuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhān apramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān abṛhān atapān sudṛśān sudarśanān akaniṣṭhān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmety udghoṣayanti gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante
children.translated_text: Those rays that go upward go to the gods of <s>Cāturmahārājika</s>, <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>, <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, <s>Parīttābha</s>, <s>Apramāṇābha</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, <s>Abṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s>; there they proclaim, "Impermanent, painful, empty, not-self," and speak two verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane
children.translated_text: "Begin! Go forth! Apply yourselves to the Buddha's teaching.

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāram iva kuñjaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Shake off the army of death as an elephant shakes off a reed hut.

children.text: yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati
children.translated_text: For whoever will live heedfully in this <s>Dharma-vinaya</s> (teaching and discipline)

children.text: prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: will abandon birth and <s>saṃsāra</s> and make an end of suffering."

children.text: atha tā arciṣas trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātum anvāhiṇḍya bhagavantam eva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti
children.translated_text: Then those rays, having traversed the three-thousand great-thousand world-system, follow the Blessed One from behind, close behind.

children.text: tad yadi bhagavān atītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If the Blessed One wishes to predict past karma, they disappear behind the Blessed One.

children.text: anāgataṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati purastād antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict future karma, they disappear in front.

children.text: narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pādatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth in hell, they disappear at the soles of his feet.

children.text: tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pārṣṇyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as an animal, they disappear at his heel.

children.text: pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as a preta, they disappear at his big toe.

children.text: manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati jānunor antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as a human, they disappear at his knees.

children.text: balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: When he wishes to predict rule as a balacakravartin king, they disappear in the palm of his left hand.

children.text: cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: When he wishes to predict rule as a wheel-turning king, they disappear in the palm of his right hand.

children.text: devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati nābhyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: When he wishes to predict rebirth among the gods, they disappear at his navel.

children.text: śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati āsye 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: When he wishes to predict awakening as a disciple, they disappear in his mouth.

children.text: pratyekāṃ bodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati ūrṇāyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: When he wishes to predict awakening as a <s>pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary Buddha), they disappear in his <s>ūrṇā</s>.

children.text: anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati uṣṇīṣe antardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: When he wishes to predict unsurpassed perfect awakening, they disappear in his <s>uṣṇīṣa</s>.

children.text: atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata ūrṇāyām antarhitāḥ
children.translated_text: Then those flames circumambulated the Blessed One three times and disappeared into the Blessed One's <s>ūrṇā</s>.

children.text: athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with hands joined, asked the Blessed One:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro vaktrāntarān niṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ
children.translated_text: "A cluster, variegated with thousands of many colors, has issued from your mouth;

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantād divākareṇodayatā yathaiva ||
children.translated_text: by it the directions all around were illuminated, just as by the sun when it rises."

children.text: gāthāś ca bhāṣate
children.translated_text: And he speaks verses:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā buddhā jagaty uttamahetubhūtāḥ
children.translated_text: "The Buddhas, free from becoming, with despondency and pride abandoned, are the supreme cause in the world;

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ smitam upadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the Jinas, conquerors of their enemies, do not display without cause a smile white as conch and lotus-fiber.

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayam adhigamya vīra buddhyā śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām
children.translated_text: Having yourself discerned at that time with heroic wisdom, O hero, O ascetic, O lord of Jinas, what the hearers desire to know,

children.text: dhīrābhir munivṛṣa vāgbhir uttamābhirutpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: O bull among sages, remove the arisen doubt with your steady, excellent, auspicious words.

children.text: nākasmāllavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ saṃbuddhāḥ smitam upadarśayanti nāthāḥ
children.translated_text: The protectors, the perfectly awakened ones, firm as the lord of the salt-water ocean, do not display a smile without reason.

children.text: yasyārthe smitam upadarśayanti dhīrāstaṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The purpose for which the steadfast ones display a smile: these crowds of people long to hear that."

children.text: bhagavān āha evam etad ānanda evam etat
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>; so it is.

children.text: nāhetvapratyayam ānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti
children.translated_text: <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Tathāgatas</s>, arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas do not reveal a smile without cause and without condition.

children.text: paśyasy ānanda ebhir gāndharvikair mamaivaṃvidhaṃ satkāraṃ kṛtam
children.translated_text: Do you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, the honor of this kind that these celestial musicians have done for me?"

children.text: evaṃ bhadanta
children.translated_text: "Yes, venerable sir."

children.text: ete ānanda gāndharvikāḥ anena kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca yathākālānugatāṃ pratyekāṃ bodhiṃ samudānīya anāgate 'dhvani varṇasvarā nāma pratyekabuddhā bhaviṣyanti hīnadīnānukampakāḥ prāntaśayanāsanabhaktā ekadakṣiṇīyā lokasya
children.translated_text: "<s>Ānanda</s>, by this root of good, by this arising of intention, and by this gift of a religious offering, these celestial musicians will in due time bring to fulfillment awakening as <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>; in a future age they will become <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> named <s>Varṇasvarā</s>, compassionate toward the low and poor, devoted to remote beds and seats, and uniquely worthy recipients of the world's offerings.

children.text: ayam eṣāṃ deyadharmo yo mamāntike cittaprasāda iti ||
children.translated_text: This is their gift of religious offering: faith of mind in my presence."

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayānāṃ chettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ kāni bhadanta bhagavatā kuśalamūlāni kṛtāni yeṣām ayam anubhāva iti
children.translated_text: The monks, having become doubtful, asked the Buddha, the Blessed One, the cutter-off of all doubts, "Venerable sir, what roots of good were made by the Blessed One, of which this is the power?"

children.text: bhagavān āha tathāgatenaitāni bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "Monks, these deeds were formerly done by the <s>Tathāgata</s> in other births; they were accumulated, had acquired their requisites, had matured conditions, had come to hand like a flood, and were inevitable.

children.text: mayaitāni karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni
children.translated_text: These deeds were done and accumulated by me.

children.text: ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante nābdhātau na tejodhātau na vāyudhātau api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca ||
children.translated_text: Who else will experience them?
