No, monks: deeds done and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element. Rather, deeds done, both wholesome and unwholesome, ripen precisely in the appropriated <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases).

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api
children.translated_text: Karmic actions do not perish even through hundreds of crores of eons;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām ||
children.translated_text: having reached the proper conjunction and time, they indeed bear fruit for embodied beings.

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani prabodhano nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān
children.translated_text: Once, monks, in the past, in a former age, a perfectly awakened Buddha named <s>Prabodhana</s> arose in the world: a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an arhat, a perfectly awakened Buddha, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, knower of the world, unsurpassed guide of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One.

children.text: sa janapadacārikāṃ carann anyatamāṃ rājadhānīm anuprāptaḥ
children.translated_text: While wandering on a tour through the countryside, he arrived at a certain royal capital.

children.text: atha rājña udyānaṃ sarvakuśalasampannaṃ babhūva
children.translated_text: Then the king's park was endowed with every good quality.

children.text: atha sa bhagavāṃs tad udyānaṃ praviśya rājānugrahārtham anyatamaṃ vṛkṣam upaniśritya niṣaṇṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Then that Blessed One entered the park and, for the sake of showing favor to the king, sat down near a certain tree.

children.text: tataḥ saṃstaraṃ prajñapya tejodhātuṃ samāpannaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, having spread out a seat, he entered absorption in the fire element.

children.text: atha rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣiktaḥ strīmayena tūryeṇa vādyamānenodyānaṃ praviṣṭaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the consecrated kṣatriya king entered the park while music was being played by a women's orchestra.

children.text: atha sa rājā tad udyānam anuvicaran dadarśa bhagavantaṃ prabodhanaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ prāsādikaṃ prasādanīyaṃ śāntamānasaṃ parameṇa cittadamavyupaśamena samanvāgataṃ suvarṇayūpam iva śriyā jvalantam
children.translated_text: Then, as that king wandered through the park, he saw the Blessed One <s>Prabodhana</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, gracious, inspiring faith, peaceful in mind, endowed with supreme taming and quieting of mind, blazing with splendor like a golden sacrificial post.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ prasādajātaḥ sa rājā sāntaḥpuro vividhena vādyena vādyamānena bhagavantaṃ tataḥ samādheḥ prabodhayāmāsa praṇītena cāhāreṇa pratipāditavān anuttarāyāṃ ca samyaksaṃbodhau kṛtavān ||
children.translated_text: Having seen him, that king, with faith arisen, together with his inner court, awakened the Blessed One from that <s>samādhi</s> with varied music being played, provided him with excellent food, and made a resolution toward unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena rājā babhūva ahaṃ saḥ
children.translated_text: What do you think, monks? The one who at that time, on that occasion, was the king was I.

children.text: yan mayā prabodhanasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya pūjā kṛtā tenaiva hetunā idānīṃ mama gāndharvikair evaṃvidhaḥ satkāraḥ kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Because I performed worship for <s>Prabodhana</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, for that very reason honor of this kind has now been done to me by the celestial musicians.

children.text: tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam yacchāstāraṃ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, monks, you should train yourselves thus: 'We will honor the Teacher, revere him, esteem him, and worship him.'

children.text: śāstāraṃ satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvopaniśritya vihariṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Having honored the Teacher, highly revered him, esteemed him, worshiped him, and relied upon him, we will dwell.

children.text: ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, should you train yourselves.

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: Those monks, pleased in mind, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.

children.text: Chapter 17

buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme
children.translated_text: The Buddha, the Blessed One, honored, highly revered, esteemed, and worshiped by kings, royal ministers, wealthy men, townspeople, guild leaders, caravan merchants, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, thus worshiped by gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, known as a Buddha, the Blessed One, of great merit and a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicines and requisites for sickness, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s> in <s>Jetavana</s>, in <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>'s park.

children.text: atha śrāvastyām anyatamaḥ pāradāriko maline karmaṇi vartate
children.translated_text: Then in <s>Śrāvastī</s> a certain adulterer was engaged in an impure act.

children.text: sa rājapuruṣair gṛhītvā rājña upanāmitaḥ
children.translated_text: He was seized by the king's officers and brought before the king.

children.text: tato rājñā aparādhika iti kṛtvā vadhya utsṛṣṭaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the king, judging him to be guilty, handed him over for execution.

children.text: sa rājapuruṣair nīlāmbaravasanair udyataśastraiḥ karavīramālābaddhakaṇṭheguṇo rathyāvīthīcatvaraśṛṅgāṭakeṣv anuśrāvyamāṇo dakṣiṇena nagaradvāreṇa apanīyate ||
children.translated_text: He was led away through the southern city gate by royal officers wearing dark-blue garments and carrying raised weapons, with a neck-cord bound with a garland of oleander, while proclamations were made through the roads, streets, squares, and crossroads.

children.text: atrāntare nāsti kiṃcid buddhānāṃ bhagavatām ajñātam adṛṣṭam aviditam avijñātam
children.translated_text: Meanwhile, there is nothing at all unknown, unseen, unfound, or uncomprehended by the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.

children.text: dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahākāruṇikānāṃ lokānugrahapravṛttakānām ekārakṣāṇāṃ śamathavipaśyanāvihāriṇāṃ tridamathavastukuśalānāṃ caturoghottīrṇānāṃ caturṛddhipādacaraṇatalasupratiṣṭhitānāṃ caturṣu saṃgrahavastuṣu dīrgharātrakṛtaparicayānāṃ pañcāṅgaviprahīṇānāṃ pañcagatisamatikrāntānāṃ ṣaḍaṅgasamanvāgatānāṃ ṣaṭpāramitāparipūrṇānāṃ saptabodhyaṅgakusumāḍhyānām aṣṭāṅgamārgadeśikānāṃ navānupūrvavihārasamāpattikuśalānāṃ daśabalabalināṃ daśadiksamāpūrṇayaśasāṃ daśaśatavaśavartiprativiśiṣṭānāṃ trī rātres trir divasasya ca buddhacakṣuṣā lokaṃ vyavalokya jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate ko hīyate ko vardhate kaḥ kṛcchraprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃkaṭaprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃbādhaprāptaḥ kaḥ kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasaṃbādhaprāptaḥ ko 'pāyanimnaḥ ko 'pāyapravaṇaḥ ko 'pāyaprāgbhāraḥ
children.translated_text: For this is the nature of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones: greatly compassionate, engaged in benefiting the world, sole protectors, dwelling in tranquility and insight, skilled in the three bases of taming, crossed over the four floods, with the soles of their feet firmly planted in the four bases of miraculous power, long practiced in the four means of gathering, rid of the five factors, passed beyond the five destinies, endowed with the six constituents, complete in the six perfections, rich with the flowers of the seven limbs of awakening, teachers of the eightfold path, skilled in attaining the nine successive dwellings, mighty with the ten powers, with fame filling the ten directions, and surpassing a thousand Vaśavartins. Three times by night and three times by day, having surveyed the world with the Buddha-eye, their knowledge and vision arises: who is declining, who is increasing; who has fallen into hardship, danger, distress, or all three; who slopes toward the lower realms, inclines toward the lower realms, is headed toward the lower realms.

children.text: kam aham apāyād uddhṛtya svarge mokṣe ca pratiṣṭhāpayeyam kasya kāmapaṅkanimagnasya hastoddhāram anupradadyām kam āryadhanavirahitam āryadhanaiśvaryādhipatye pratiṣṭhāpayeyam kasyājñānatimirapaṭalaparyavanaddhanetrasya jñānāñjanaśalākayā cakṣur viśodhayāmi
children.translated_text: Whom shall I lift out of a lower realm and establish in heaven and liberation? To whom, sunk in the mud of desire, shall I extend a helping hand? Whom, destitute of noble wealth, shall I establish in sovereignty over noble wealth? Whose eye, covered by the veil of the darkness of ignorance, shall I cleanse with the collyrium-stick of knowledge?

children.text: kasyānavaropitāni kuśalamūlānyavaropayeyam kasyāvaropitāni paripācayeyam kasya paripakvāni vimocayeyam
children.translated_text: Whose unplanted roots of goodness shall I plant? Whose planted ones shall I ripen? Whose ripened ones shall I release?

children.text: āha ca
children.translated_text: And it is said:

children.text: apyevātikramed velāṃ sāgaro makarālayaḥ
children.translated_text: The ocean, abode of makaras, might even overstep its shore;

children.text: na tu vaineyavatsānāṃ buddho velām atikramet ||
children.translated_text: but the Buddha does not overstep the proper time for the calf-like beings who are to be trained.

children.text: atha bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya śrāvastīṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat
children.translated_text: Then, in the forenoon, the Blessed One dressed, took his bowl and robe, and entered <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms.

children.text: dadarśa sa puruṣo buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam
children.translated_text: That man saw the Buddha, the Blessed One, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great person, his body radiant with the eighty secondary marks, adorned with a fathom-wide aura, with a brilliance surpassing a thousand suns, like a moving mountain of jewels, auspicious on every side.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punar bhagavataḥ pādayor nipatya bhagavantam idam avocat varāho 'smi bhagavan iṣṭaṃ me jīvitaṃ prayaccheti
children.translated_text: After seeing him, he fell at the Blessed One's feet and said this to the Blessed One: "I am wretched, Blessed One; my life is dear to me. Grant it to me."

children.text: tato bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate gaccha ānanda rājānaṃ prasenajitam
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, to King <s>Prasenajit</s>,

children.text: vada anuprayaccha me etaṃ puruṣam pravrājayāmīti
children.translated_text: and say, 'Hand this man over to me; I will ordain him.'"

children.text: athāyuṣmān ānando yena rājā prasenajit kauśalas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ
children.translated_text: Then venerable <s>Ānanda</s> approached King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kauśala</s>.

children.text: upasaṃkramya rājānaṃ prasenajitaṃ kauśalaṃ bhagavadvacanenovāca anujānīhi bhagavān etaṃ puruṣaṃ pravrājayatīti
children.translated_text: Having approached, he said to King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kauśala</s> on the Blessed One's behalf: "Permit the Blessed One to ordain this man."

children.text: bhavyarūpa iti viditvā rājñā prasenajitkauśalenānujñātaḥ
children.translated_text: Knowing that he was of a fit nature, King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kauśala</s> gave permission.

children.text: sa bhagavatā pravrājita upasaṃpāditaś ca
children.translated_text: The Blessed One ordained him and gave him full ordination.

children.text: tena yujyamānena ghaṭamānena vyāyacchamānena idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam
children.translated_text: As he applied himself, strove, and exerted himself, he understood this very fivefold wheel of saṃsāra to be wavering and unstable. Seeing all conditioned states as by nature subject to breaking, falling, scattering, and destruction, he abandoned all afflictions and realized arhatship.

children.text: arhan saṃvṛttaḥ traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhaḥ
children.translated_text: He became an arhat, free from passion for the three realms, regarding clods and gold alike, with a mind equal toward the sky and the palm of the hand, the same toward axe and sandalwood, the shell of the egg split open by knowledge, having attained knowledge, higher faculties, and discriminating insights, turned away from existence, gain, greed, and honor.

children.text: sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He became worthy to be worshiped, honored, and saluted by the gods together with <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayānāṃ chettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ āścaryaṃ bhadanta yad bhagavatā sarvaṃ cintitamātraṃ samṛdhyatīti
children.translated_text: The monks, filled with doubt, asked the Buddha, the Blessed One, the cutter-off of all doubts, "It is wondrous, venerable sir, that everything merely thought by the Blessed One is fulfilled."

children.text: bhagavān āha tathāgatenaivaitāni bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "Monks, these deeds were formerly done and accumulated by the <s>Tathāgata</s> in other births; they had acquired their requisites, had matured conditions, had come to hand like a flood, and were inevitable.

children.text: mayaitāni karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni
children.translated_text: These deeds were done and accumulated by me.

children.text: ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante nābdhātau na tejodhātau na vāyudhātau api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca
children.translated_text: Who else will experience them? No, monks: deeds done and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element. Rather, deeds done, both wholesome and unwholesome, ripen precisely in the appropriated <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases).

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api
children.translated_text: Karmic actions do not perish even through hundreds of crores of eons;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām ||
children.translated_text: having reached the proper conjunction and time, they indeed bear fruit for embodied beings.

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani indradhvajo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān
children.translated_text: Once, monks, in the past, in a former age, a perfectly awakened Buddha named <s>Indradhvaja</s> arose in the world: a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an arhat, a perfectly awakened Buddha, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed guide of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One.

children.text: sa janapadacārikāṃ carann anyatamāṃ rājadhānīm anuprāptaḥ
children.translated_text: Wandering on a tour through the countryside, he arrived at a certain royal capital.

children.text: tasyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ brāhmaṇo vedavedāṅgapārago rājño 'grāsanikaḥ
children.translated_text: In that royal capital there was a Brahmin, master of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, holder of the king's chief seat.

children.text: athendradhvajaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya tāṃ rājadhānīṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat
children.translated_text: Then <s>Indradhvaja</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, dressed in the morning, took his bowl and robe, and entered that royal capital for alms.

children.text: adrākṣīt sa brāhmaṇa indradhvajaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam
children.translated_text: That Brahmin saw <s>Indradhvaja</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man, his body resplendent with the eighty secondary marks, adorned with an arm-span halo, brighter than a thousand suns, like a moving mountain of jewels, auspicious on every side.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punar mūlanikṛtta iva drumo bhagavataḥ pādayor nipatyovāca varāho 'smi sugata niṣīdatu bhagavān agrāsana iti
children.translated_text: Having seen him, like a tree cut off at the root he fell at the Blessed One's feet and said, "You are worthy of the best, O <s>Sugata</s>; may the Blessed One sit on the chief seat."

children.text: atha bhagavān indradhvajaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhas tasyānugrahārtham agrāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One <s>Indradhvaja</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, sat on the chief seat in order to show favor to him.

children.text: agrāsane niṣaṇṇaś cendradhvajaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhas tena brāhmaṇena padaśatena stutaḥ praṇītena cāhāreṇa pratipāditaḥ anuttarāyāṃ ca samyaksaṃbodhau praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam
children.translated_text: And while <s>Indradhvaja</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, sat on the chief seat, that Brahmin praised him with a hundred verses, served him with excellent food, and made a resolution toward unsurpassed perfect awakening.

children.text: taddhaitukaṃ yāvad āvarjitā rājāmātyapaurāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For that reason, the king, the ministers, and the townspeople were drawn in as well.

children.text: tat kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena brāhmaṇo babhūva ahaṃ saḥ
children.translated_text: What do you think, monks? I was the Brahmin who existed at that time, on that occasion.

children.text: yan me indradhvajasya tathāgatasya pūjā kṛtā taddhaitukaṃ ca me saṃsāre anantaṃ sukham anubhūtam
children.translated_text: Because I performed worship for <s>Indradhvaja</s> the <s>Tathāgata</s>, for that very reason I experienced endless happiness in <s>saṃsāra</s>.

children.text: api yac cintayāmi yat prārthaye tat sarvaṃ samṛdhyati
children.translated_text: Moreover, whatever I think and whatever I wish for, all of it is fulfilled.

children.text: tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam yacchāstāraṃ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, monks, you should train yourselves thus: 'We will honor the Teacher, revere him, esteem him, and worship him.'

children.text: śāstāraṃ satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvopaniśritya vihariṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Having honored, revered, esteemed, worshiped, and relied upon the Teacher, we will dwell.

children.text: ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, you should train yourselves.

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the Blessed One's speech.

children.text: Chapter 18

buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho rājagṛham upaniśritya viharati sma veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe
children.translated_text: The Buddha, the Blessed One, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshiped by kings, royal officers, wealthy men, citizens, merchants, caravan leaders, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas; thus worshiped by gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, famous and greatly meritorious, receiving robes, almsfood, bedding and seats, and medicines as requisites for illness, was dwelling with the community of his disciples near <s>Rājagṛha</s> in the <s>Veṇuvana</s>, at <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s>.

children.text: yadā rājñā bimbisāreṇānekaprāṇiśatasahasraparivāreṇa satyāni dṛṣṭāni tadā tena kṛtapratyupakārasaṃdarśanārthaṃ buddhapūjāsaṃvartanārthaṃ gṛhavistarasaṃdarśanārthaṃ buddhotpādabahumānasaṃjananārthaṃ ca bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃgho rājakule bhaktenopanimantritaḥ māgadhakānāṃ ca paurāṇām ājñā dattā bhagavato nagarapraveśe puṣpagandhamālyavilepanaiḥ pūjā kartavyā sarvaṃ ca rājagṛhaṃ nagaram apagatapāṣāṇaśarkarakaṭhallaṃ vyavasthāpayitavyam nānāpuṣpāvakīrṇam ucchritadhvajapatākaṃ yāvac ca veṇuvanaṃ yāvac ca rājagṛham atrāntarā sarvo mārgo vicitrair vastrair ācchādayitavya iti
children.translated_text: When the truths had been seen by King <s>Bimbisāra</s>, surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of living beings, then, in order to demonstrate repayment for what had been done for him, to promote worship of the Buddha, to display the magnificence of his household, and to generate great respect for the arising of a Buddha, the Blessed One, together with the community of his disciples, was invited by him to a meal in the royal household. And an order was given to the citizens of <s>Magadha</s>: 'At the Blessed One's entrance into the city, worship is to be performed with flowers, perfumes, garlands, and ointments; the whole city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> is to be put in order, with stones, gravel, and potsherds removed, strewn with various flowers, with banners and flags raised. And from the <s>Veṇuvana</s> as far as <s>Rājagṛha</s>, along the whole road in between, it is to be covered with variegated cloths.'

children.text: amātyaiś ca sarvam anuṣṭhitam
children.translated_text: And everything was carried out by the ministers.

children.text: tato rājā bimbisāraḥ svayam eva bhagavato mūrdhni śataśalākaṃ chatraṃ dhārayati pariśeṣāḥ paurāḥ bhikṣusahasrasya ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Bimbisāra</s> himself held a parasol with a hundred ribs over the Blessed One's head, while the remaining citizens did so for the thousand monks.

children.text: atha bhagavān dānto dāntaparivāraḥ śāntaḥ śāntaparivāro mukto muktaparivāra āśvasta āśvastaparivāro vinīto vinītaparivāro 'rhann arhatparivāro vītarāgo vītarāgaparivāraḥ prāsādikaḥ prāsādikaparivāro vṛṣabha iva gogaṇaparivṛto gaja iva kalabhagaṇaparivṛtaḥ siṃha iva daṃṣṭrigaṇaparivṛto haṃsa iva haṃsagaṇaparivṛtaḥ suparṇīva pakṣigaṇaparivṛto vipra iva śiṣyagaṇaparivṛtaḥ svaśva iva turagagaṇaparivṛtaḥ śūra iva yodhagaṇaparivṛto deśika ivādhvagagaṇaparivṛtaḥ sārthavāha iva vaṇiggaṇaparivṛtaḥ śreṣṭhīva paurajanaparivṛtaḥ koṭṭarāja iva mantrigaṇaparivṛtaś cakravartīva putrasahasraparivṛtaś candra iva nakṣatragaṇaparivṛtaḥ sūrya iva raśmisahasraparivṛto dhṛtarāṣṭra iva gandharvagaṇaparivṛto virūḍha iva kumbhāṇḍagaṇaparivṛto virūpākṣa iva nāgagaṇaparivṛto dhanada iva yakṣagaṇaparivṛto vemacitrīvāsuragaṇaparivṛtaḥ śakra iva tridaśagaṇaparivṛto brahmā iva brahmakāyikaparivṛtaḥ stimita iva jalanidhiḥ sajala iva jaladharo vimada iva gajapatiḥ sudāntair indriyair asaṃkṣobhiteryāpathapracāro 'nekair āveṇikair buddhadharmaiḥ parivṛto bhagavāṃs tat puraṃ praviśati ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, tamed and with a retinue of the tamed, peaceful and with a retinue of the peaceful, liberated and with a retinue of the liberated, confident and with a retinue of the confident, disciplined and with a retinue of the disciplined, an arhat with a retinue of arhats, free from passion and with a retinue free from passion, inspiring faith and with a retinue inspiring faith; like a bull surrounded by a herd of cattle, like an elephant surrounded by a herd of young elephants, like a lion surrounded by fanged beasts, like a goose surrounded by a flock of geese, like <s>Suparṇin</s> surrounded by birds, like a brahmin surrounded by pupils, like a fine horse surrounded by steeds, like a hero surrounded by warriors, like a guide surrounded by travelers, like a caravan leader surrounded by merchants, like a guild-master surrounded by townspeople, like a fortress-king surrounded by ministers, like a wheel-turning king surrounded by a thousand sons, like the moon surrounded by the hosts of stars, like the sun surrounded by a thousand rays, like <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> surrounded by hosts of gandharvas, like <s>Virūḍha</s> surrounded by hosts of kumbhāṇḍas, like <s>Virūpākṣa</s> surrounded by hosts of nāgas, like <s>Dhanada</s> surrounded by hosts of yakṣas, like <s>Vemacitrin</s> surrounded by hosts of asuras, like <s>Śakra</s> surrounded by the hosts of the Thirty-three, like <s>Brahmā</s> surrounded by the Brahmā-body gods, still as the ocean, like a water-bearing cloud, like a lordly elephant free from rut, with well-tamed faculties and undisturbed movement in his postures, surrounded by many unique qualities of a Buddha, entered that city.

children.text: yadā ca bhagavatā indrakīle pādo nyastaḥ tadeyaṃ mahāpṛthivī ṣaḍvikāraṃ prakampitā
children.translated_text: And when the Blessed One set his foot at the city gate-post, this great earth shook in six ways.

children.text: bhagavataḥ purapraveśe evaṃrūpāṇy adbhutāni bhavantyanyāni ca
children.translated_text: At the Blessed One's entry into a city, such wonders as these occur, and others too.

children.text: tadyathā saṃkṣiptāni viśālībhavanti hastinaḥ krośanti aśvāś ca heṣante ṛṣabhā nardante gṛhagatāni vividhavādyabhāṇḍāni svayaṃ nadanti andhāś cakṣūṃṣi pratilabhante badhirāḥ śrotraṃ mūkāḥ pravyāharaṇasamarthā bhavanti pariśiṣṭendriyavikalā indriyāṇi paripūrṇāni pratilabhante madyamadākṣiptā vimadībhavanti viṣapītā nirviṣībhavanti anyonyavairiṇo maitrīṃ pratilabhante gurviṇyaḥ svastinā prajāyante bandhanabaddhā vimucyante adhanā dhanāni pratilabhante āntarikṣāś ca devāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragā divyaṃ puṣpam utsṛjanti ||
children.translated_text: That is, constricted places become spacious; elephants trumpet, horses neigh, and bulls bellow; the various musical instruments kept in houses sound by themselves; the blind regain their eyes, the deaf regain hearing, and the mute become able to speak; others with impaired faculties regain complete faculties; those overcome by the intoxication of liquor become sober; those who have drunk poison become free of poison; mutual enemies gain friendliness toward one another; pregnant women give birth safely; those bound in fetters are released; the poor obtain wealth; and gods, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and great serpents in the sky scatter divine flowers.

children.text: atha bhagavān evaṃvidhayā vibhūtyā rājakulaṃ praveṣṭum ārabdhaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, with splendor of this kind, began to enter the royal residence.

children.text: rājā ca bimbisāraḥ svayam eva bahirdvāraśālastho gośīrṣacandanodakena pādyaṃ gṛhītvā bhagavataḥ pādau bhikṣusaṃghasya ca prakṣālayati
children.translated_text: And King <s>Bimbisāra</s> himself, standing at the outer doorway hall, took foot-water made with gośīrṣa sandalwood water and washed the feet of the Blessed One and of the community of monks.

children.text: sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ viditvā śatarasenāhāreṇa pratipādayāmāsa
children.translated_text: Knowing that the community of monks headed by the Buddha was comfortably seated, he served them food of a hundred flavors.

children.text: bhuktavantaṃ kāśikavastrair ācchāditavān
children.translated_text: When the Blessed One had eaten, he covered him with Kāśī garments.

children.text: taddhaitukaṃ ca āvarjitā māgadhakāḥ paurāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And because of that, the Magadhan townspeople were won over.

children.text: tato bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ kutremāni bhagavatā kuśalamūlāni kṛtāni yato bhagavata evaṃvidhā pūjā bhikṣusaṃghasya ceti
children.translated_text: Then the monks, filled with doubt, asked the Buddha, the Blessed One, the cutter-off of all doubts: "Where were these roots of good made by the Blessed One, such that such honor is now given to the Blessed One and to the community of monks?"

children.text: bhagavān āha tathāgatenaivaitāni bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "Monks, these deeds were formerly done by the <s>Tathāgata</s> in other births; they were accumulated, had acquired their requisites, had matured conditions, had come to hand like a flood, and were inevitable.

children.text: mayaitāni karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni
children.translated_text: These deeds were done and accumulated by me.

children.text: ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante nābdhātau na tejodhātau na vāyudhātau api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhānyaśubhāni ca
children.translated_text: Who else will experience them? No, monks: deeds done and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element. Rather, deeds done, both wholesome and unwholesome, ripen precisely in the appropriated <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases).

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api
children.translated_text: Karmic actions do not perish even through hundreds of crores of eons;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām ||
children.translated_text: having reached the proper conjunction and time, they indeed bear fruit for embodied beings."

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani kṣemaṃkaro nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān
children.translated_text: "Once, monks, in the past, in a former age, a perfectly awakened Buddha named <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s> arose in the world: a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an arhat, a perfectly awakened Buddha, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, knower of the world, unsurpassed guide of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One.

children.text: sa janapadacārikāṃ carann anyatamāṃ rājadhānīm anuprāptaḥ
children.translated_text: While wandering on a tour through the countryside, he arrived at a certain royal capital.

children.text: aśrauṣīd rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣiktaḥ kṣemaṃkaraḥ samyaksaṃbuddho janapadacārikāṃ carann asmākaṃ rājadhānīm anuprāpta iti
children.translated_text: A king, a consecrated kṣatriya, heard: '<s>Kṣemaṃkara</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, while wandering on a tour through the countryside, has arrived at our royal capital.'

children.text: śrutvā ca mahatyā rājarddhyā mahatā rājānubhāvena samanvāgataḥ
children.translated_text: Having heard this, endowed with great royal splendor and great royal authority,

children.text: yena bhagavān kṣemaṃkaraḥ samyaksaṃbuddhas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ
children.translated_text: he approached the place where the Blessed One <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, was.

children.text: upasaṃkramya kṣemaṃkarasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte niṣaṇṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Having approached, he bowed with his head at the feet of <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, and sat down to one side.

children.text: ekānte niṣaṇṇaṃ rājānaṃ kṣatriyaṃ mūrdhābhiṣiktam kṣemaṃkaraḥ samyaksaṃbuddho bodhikarakair dharmaiḥ samādāpayati
children.translated_text: As the king, the consecrated kṣatriya, was seated to one side, <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, caused him to undertake qualities that bring about awakening.

children.text: atha sa rājā labdhaprasādaḥ kṣemaṃkaraṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ rājakule nimantrya śatarasenāhāreṇa pratipādayāmāsa
children.translated_text: Then that king, having gained faith, invited <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, to the royal residence and served him with food of a hundred flavors.

children.text: śatasāhasreṇa ca vastreṇāchādayāmāsa
children.translated_text: And he clothed him with a garment worth a hundred thousand.

children.text: parinirvṛtasya ca samantayojanaṃ stūpaṃ kāritavān krośam uccatvena ||
children.translated_text: When he had passed into final nirvāṇa, the king had a <s>stūpa</s> (reliquary mound) built, a yojana in circumference and a krośa in height.

children.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena rājā babhūva ahaṃ saḥ
children.translated_text: What do you think, monks? The one who at that time, on that occasion, was the king was I.

children.text: yan mayā kṣemaṃkarasya samyaksaṃbuddhasyaivaṃvidhā pūjā kṛtā tena mayā saṃsāre 'nantaṃ sukham anubhūtam
children.translated_text: Because I performed such worship for <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, through that I experienced endless happiness in <s>saṃsāra</s>.

children.text: idānīṃ tenaiva hetunā rājñā bimbisāreṇāpi tathāgatasya me evaṃvidhā pūjā kṛtā
children.translated_text: Now, through that very cause, King <s>Bimbisāra</s> too has performed such worship for me, the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text: tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam yacchāstāraṃ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, monks, you should train yourselves thus: We will honor the Teacher, revere him, esteem him, and worship him.

children.text: śāstāraṃ satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvopaniśritya vihariṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Having honored, revered, esteemed, and worshiped the Teacher, we will dwell in dependence upon him.

children.text: ityevaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, should you train yourselves.

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.

children.text: Chapter 19

buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho rājagṛhe viharati veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe
children.translated_text: The Buddha, the Blessed One, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshiped by kings, royal ministers, wealthy men, townsmen, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s>, thus venerated by gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s>, known, greatly meritorious, a receiver of robes, alms-food, beds and seats, and medicines as requisites for the sick, was dwelling together with the community of disciples at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in <s>Veṇuvana</s>, at <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s>.

children.text: tatra anyataraḥ śreṣṭhī āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī tīrthyābhiprasannaś ca
children.translated_text: There a certain guild-master was rich, possessing great wealth and great resources, with broad and extensive possessions, endowed with wealth like that of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, rivaling the wealth of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, and devoted to the <s>tīrthyas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers).

children.text: sa āyuṣmatā mahāmaudgalyāyanenāvarjitaḥ śāsane ca avatārito bhagavatyatyartham abhiprasannaḥ
children.translated_text: He was won over by the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, brought into the teaching, and became exceedingly faithful toward the Blessed One.

children.text: sa ca gṛhapatir udārādhimuktaḥ
children.translated_text: That householder was of generous disposition.

children.text: tenāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyana uktaḥ sahāyo me bhava icchāmi bhagavataḥ pūjāṃ kartum iti
children.translated_text: He said to the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, Be my helper; I wish to perform worship for the Blessed One.

children.text: adhivāsayaty āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanas tasya gṛhapates tūṣṇībhāvena athāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanas taṃ gṛhapatim ādāya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte niṣaṇṇaḥ
children.translated_text: The venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> accepted that householder's request by silence. Then the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, taking that householder with him, approached the place where the Blessed One was. Having approached, he bowed with his head at the Blessed One's feet and sat to one side.

children.text: ekāntaniṣaṇṇa āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyano bhagavantam idam avocat ayaṃ bhadanta gṛhapatir ākāṅkṣati bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaṃ bhojayitum
children.translated_text: Sitting to one side, the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> said this to the Blessed One: Venerable sir, this householder wishes to feed the Blessed One together with the community of disciples.

children.text: tad asya bhagavān adhivāsayed anukampām upādāyeti
children.translated_text: Therefore may the Blessed One accept from him, out of compassion.

children.text: adhivāsayati bhagavāṃs tasya gṛhapates tūṣṇībhāvena
children.translated_text: The Blessed One accepted that householder's request by silence.

children.text: atha sa gṛhapatir bhagavatas tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā śatarasam āhāraṃ samudānayati puṣpagandhamālyavilepanāni ca
children.translated_text: Then that householder, knowing the Blessed One's acceptance by silence, prepared food of a hundred flavors, along with flowers, fragrances, garlands, and ointments.

children.text: āyuṣmatāpi mahāmaudgalyāyanena śakro devendro 'dhīṣṭaḥ kriyatām asya gṛhapater upasaṃhāra iti
children.translated_text: The venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> also enjoined <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: Make an additional provision for this householder.

children.text: tataḥ śakreṇa devendreṇa veṇuvanaṃ nandavanam abhinirmitam airāvaṇasupratiṣṭhitasadṛśāni ca nāgasahasrāṇi vālavyajanena vījayanti
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, transformed <s>Veṇuvana</s> into <s>Nandavana</s>, and thousands of <s>nāgas</s> resembling <s>Airāvaṇa</s> and <s>Supratiṣṭhita</s> fanned them with yak-tail fans.

children.text: supriyapañcaśikhatumbaruprabhṛtīni cānekāni gandharvasahasrāṇy upanītāni ye vicitrair vādyaviśeṣair vādyaṃ kurvanti divyaṃ ca sudhābhojanam
children.translated_text: And many thousands of <s>gandharvas</s>, beginning with <s>Supriya</s>, <s>Pañcaśikha</s>, and <s>Tumburu</s>, were brought there; they played music with various special instruments, and divine ambrosial food was provided.

children.text: tataḥ sa gṛhapatir divyamānuṣair upakaraṇair bhagavantam upasthāya sarvāṅgeṇa bhagavataḥ pādayor nipatya praṇīdhānaṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca andhe loke anāyake apariṇāyake buddho bhūyāsam atīrṇānāṃ sattvānāṃ tārayitā amuktānāṃ mocayitā anāśvastānām āśvāsayitā aparinirvṛtānāṃ parinirvāpayiteti ||
children.translated_text: Then that householder, having attended upon the Blessed One with divine and human requisites, fell with his whole body at the Blessed One's feet and began to make a vow: By this root of good, by this arising of intention, and by this giving up of a religious gift, may I become a Buddha in the blind world, without leader and without guide; may I be the carrier across of beings not crossed, the liberator of those not liberated, the comforter of those not comforted, and the one who brings to final nirvāṇa those not yet finally extinguished.

children.text: atha bhagavāṃs tasya gṛhapater hetuparaṃparāṃ karmaparaṃparāṃ ca jñātvā smitaṃ prāvirakārṣīt
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, knowing the sequence of causes and the sequence of karma for that householder, revealed a smile.

children.text: dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhān niścārya kāścid adhastād gacchanti kāścid upariṣṭād gacchanti
children.translated_text: It is the nature of things that when the blessed Buddhas reveal a smile, at that time blue, yellow, red, and white rays issue from their mouths; some go downward and some go upward.

children.text: yā adhastād gacchanti tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanam avīcim arbudaṃ nirarbudaṃ aṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvam utpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaṃ narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakāsteṣu śītībhūtā nipatanti ye śītanarakās teṣūṣṇībhūtā nipatanti
children.translated_text: Those that go downward, having gone to the hells <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s>, fall cool into the hot hells and fall warm into the cold hells.

children.text: tena teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante
children.translated_text: By that, the special torments of those beings are allayed.

children.text: teṣām evaṃ bhavati kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ āhosvid anyatropapannā iti
children.translated_text: It occurs to them: Have we, friends, passed away from here, or have we been reborn somewhere else?

children.text: teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati
children.translated_text: For the sake of generating faith in them, the Blessed One sends forth a created apparition.

children.text: teṣāṃ nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavati na hy eva vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutā nāpy anyatropapannāḥ
children.translated_text: When they see the magically created form, it occurs to them, "Surely, sirs, we have neither fallen from here nor been reborn elsewhere.

children.text: api tv ayam apūrvadarśanaḥ sattvaḥ asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti
children.translated_text: Rather, this is a being whose sight has never been seen before; by his power our particular torments have subsided."

children.text: te nirmite cittam abhiprasādya tan narakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇanti yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti
children.translated_text: Having made their minds clear and faithful toward the magical form, they exhaust that karma to be experienced in hell and take rebirth among gods and humans, where they become fit vessels for the truths.

children.text: yā upariṣṭād gacchanti tāś cāturmahārājikāṃstrayastriṃśān yāmāṃs tuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhān apramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān abṛhān atapān sudṛśān sudarśanān akaniṣṭhān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmety udghoṣayanti gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante
children.translated_text: Those rays that go upward, having gone to the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods, the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, the <s>Yāmas</s>, the <s>Tuṣitas</s>, the <s>Nirmāṇaratis</s>, the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartins</s>, the <s>Brahmakāyikas</s>, the <s>Brahmapurohitas</s>, the <s>Mahābrahmās</s>, the <s>Parīttābhas</s>, the <s>Apramāṇābhas</s>, the <s>Ābhāsvaras</s>, the <s>Parīttaśubhas</s>, the <s>Apramāṇaśubhas</s>, the <s>Śubhakṛtsnas</s>, the <s>Anabhrakas</s>, the <s>Puṇyaprasavas</s>, the <s>Bṛhatphalas</s>, the <s>Abṛhas</s>, the <s>Atapas</s>, the <s>Sudṛśas</s>, the <s>Sudarśanas</s>, and the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods, proclaim, "Impermanent, suffering, empty, without self," and speak two verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane
children.translated_text: "Begin; go forth; apply yourselves in the Buddha's teaching.

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāram iva kuñjaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Shake off the army of Death as an elephant shakes off a reed hut.

children.text: yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati
children.translated_text: For whoever will live heedfully in this <s>dharmavinaya</s> (teaching and discipline)

children.text: prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: will abandon birth and <s>saṃsāra</s> and make an end of suffering."

children.text: atha tā arciṣas trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātum anvāhiṇḍya bhagavantam eva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti
children.translated_text: Then those rays, having traversed the three-thousand great-thousand world-system, follow the Blessed One from behind, close behind.

children.text: tad yadi bhagavān atītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If the Blessed One wishes to predict past karma, they disappear behind the Blessed One.

children.text: anāgataṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati purastād antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict future karma, they disappear in front.

children.text: narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pādatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth in hell, they disappear at the soles of his feet.

children.text: tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pārṣṇyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as an animal, they disappear at his heel.

children.text: pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as a preta, they disappear at his big toe.

children.text: manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati jānunor antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as a human, they disappear at his knees.

children.text: balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: When he wishes to predict rule as a balacakravartin king, they disappear in the palm of his left hand.

children.text: cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: When he wishes to predict rule as a wheel-turning king, they disappear in the palm of his right hand.

children.text: devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati nābhyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: When he wishes to predict rebirth among the gods, they disappear at his navel.

children.text: śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati āsye 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: When he wishes to predict awakening as a disciple, they disappear in his mouth.

children.text: pratyekāṃ bodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati ūrṇāyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: When he wishes to predict solitary awakening, they disappear in his <s>ūrṇā</s>.

children.text: anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati uṣṇīṣe antardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: When he wishes to predict unsurpassed perfect awakening, they disappear in his <s>uṣṇīṣa</s>.

children.text: atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata uṣṇīṣe 'ntarhitāḥ
children.translated_text: Then those rays circumambulated the Blessed One three times and disappeared into the Blessed One's <s>uṣṇīṣa</s>.

children.text: athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with hands joined, asked the Blessed One:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro vaktrāntarān niṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ
children.translated_text: "A cluster, variegated with thousands of many colors, has issued from the opening of your mouth;

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantād divākareṇodayatā yathaiva ||
children.translated_text: by it the directions all around have been illuminated, just as by the sun when it rises."

children.text: gāthāś ca bhāṣate
children.translated_text: And he recites verses:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā buddhā jagaty uttamahetubhūtāḥ
children.translated_text: "The Buddhas, free from becoming, with dejection and pride abandoned, are the supreme cause in the world;

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ smitam upadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Jinas</s>, conquerors of their enemies, do not display without cause a smile white as conch and lotus fiber.

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayam adhigamya vīra buddhyā śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām
children.translated_text: Having yourself discerned at that moment with heroic wisdom, O hero, O ascetic, O lord of <s>Jinas</s>, what the hearers long to know,

children.text: dhīrābhir munivṛṣa vāgbhir uttamābhir utpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: O bull among sages, remove the arisen doubt with your steady, excellent, auspicious words.

children.text: nākasmāllavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ saṃbuddhāḥ smitam upadarśayanti nāthāḥ
children.translated_text: The protectors, the perfectly awakened ones, firm as the ocean and the king of mountains, do not display a smile without reason.

children.text: yasyārthe smitam upadarśayanti dhīrāstaṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The purpose for which the steadfast ones display a smile: these crowds of people long to hear that."

children.text: bhagavān āha evam etad ānanda evam etat
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>; so it is.

children.text: nāhetvapratyayam ānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti
children.translated_text: <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Tathāgatas</s>, arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas do not reveal a smile without cause and without condition.

children.text: paśyasy ānanda anena gṛhapatinā mamaivaṃvidhaṃ satkāraṃ kṛtam
children.translated_text: Do you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, that this householder has done honor of such a kind to me?"

children.text: evaṃ bhadanta
children.translated_text: "Yes, venerable sir."

children.text: eṣa ānanda gṛhapatir anena kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca trikalpāsaṃkhyeyasamudānītāṃ bodhiṃ samudānīya mahākaruṇāparibhāvitāḥ ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ paripūrya divyānnado nāma samyaksaṃbuddho bhaviṣyati daśabhir balaiś caturbhir vaiśāradyais tribhir āveṇikaiḥ smṛtyupasthānair mahākaruṇayā ca
children.translated_text: "<s>Ānanda</s>, by this root of good, by this arising of intention, and by the giving up of this religious gift, this householder will bring to completion the awakening accumulated through three incalculable eons, fulfill the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) suffused with great compassion, and become a perfectly awakened Buddha named <s>Divyānnada</s>, endowed with the ten powers, the four confidences, the three unique establishments of mindfulness, and great compassion.

children.text: ayam asya deyadharmo yo mamāntike cittaprasādaḥ
children.translated_text: This is his religious gift: faith of mind in my presence."

children.text: etacca prakaraṇaṃ rājā bimbisāro māgadhakāś ca paricārakāḥ śrutvā paraṃ vismayam āpannāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having heard this matter, king <s>Bimbisāra</s> and the <s>Māgadhaka</s> attendants were filled with supreme wonder.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ paśya bhagavan yāvad anena gṛhapatinā bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃgho divyamānuṣībhir ṛddhibhir abhyarcita iti ||
children.translated_text: The monks, having become doubtful, asked the Buddha, the Blessed One, the cutter-off of all doubts, "Look, Blessed One, how greatly this householder has honored the Blessed One together with the community of disciples, through divine and human miraculous powers."

children.text: bhagavān āha tathāgatenaivaitāni bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "Monks, these deeds were formerly done by the <s>Tathāgata</s> in other births; they were accumulated, had acquired their requisites, had matured conditions, had come to hand like a flood, and were inevitable.

children.text: mayaitāni karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni
children.translated_text: These deeds were done and accumulated by me.

children.text: ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante nābdhātau na tejodhātau na vāyudhātau api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca
children.translated_text: Who else will experience them? No, monks: deeds done and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element. Rather, deeds done, both wholesome and unwholesome, ripen precisely in the appropriated <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases).

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api
children.translated_text: Karmic actions do not perish even through hundreds of crores of eons;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām ||
children.translated_text: having reached the proper conjunction and time, they indeed bear fruit for embodied beings.

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani pūrṇo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān
children.translated_text: Once, monks, in the past, in a former age, a perfectly awakened Buddha named <s>Pūrṇa</s> arose in the world: a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an arhat, a perfectly awakened Buddha, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, knower of the world, unsurpassed guide of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One.

children.text: atha pūrṇaḥ samyaksaṃbuddho janapadacārikāṃ carann anyatamāṃ rājadhānīm anuprāptaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Pūrṇa</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, while wandering on a tour through the countryside, arrived at a certain royal capital.

children.text: aśrauṣīd rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣiktaḥ pūrṇaḥ samyaksaṃbuddho janapadacārikāṃ carann asmākaṃ rājadhānīm anuprāpta iti
children.translated_text: A king, a consecrated kṣatriya, heard: '<s>Pūrṇa</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, while wandering on a tour through the countryside, has arrived at our royal capital.'

children.text: śrutvā ca punar mahatyā rājarddhyā mahatā rājānubhāvena samanvāgato yena bhagavān pūrṇaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ
children.translated_text: Having heard this, endowed with great royal splendor and great royal authority, he approached the place where the Blessed One <s>Pūrṇa</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, was.

children.text: upasaṃkramya pūrṇasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte niṣaṇṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Having approached, he bowed with his head at the feet of <s>Pūrṇa</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, and sat down to one side.

children.text: ekānte niṣaṇṇaṃ rājānaṃ kṣatriyaṃ mūrdhābhiṣiktaṃ pūrṇaḥ samyaksaṃbuddho bodhikarakair dharmaiḥ samādāpayati
children.translated_text: As the king, the consecrated kṣatriya, was seated to one side, <s>Pūrṇa</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, caused him to undertake qualities that bring about awakening.

children.text: atha rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣiktaḥ pūrṇaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaṃ traimāsyaṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārair upanimantritavān
children.translated_text: Then the king, the consecrated kṣatriya, invited <s>Pūrṇa</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, together with the community of disciples, for the three-month period with robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicines and requisites for sickness.

children.text: adhivāsitaṃ ca pūrṇena samyaksaṃbuddhena rājñas tūṣṇībhāvena
children.translated_text: And the invitation of the king was accepted by <s>Pūrṇa</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, through silence.

children.text: atha rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣiktaḥ pūrṇasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā traimāsyaṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārair upasthāpya bhagavato ratnamayapratimāṃ kārayitvā buddhaharṣaṃ kāritavān yatrānekaiḥ prāṇiśatasahasrair mahāprasādo labdhaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the king, the consecrated kṣatriya, knowing from <s>Pūrṇa</s>'s silence that he had accepted, served him for the three-month period with robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicines and requisites for sickness; and, having had a jewel-made image of the Blessed One made, he caused a Buddha-festival to be held, at which many hundreds of thousands of beings obtained great faith.

children.text: taddhetu tatpratyayaṃ ca te parinirvṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: By that cause and by that condition, they attained parinirvāṇa.

children.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena rājā babhūva ahaṃ saḥ
children.translated_text: What do you think, monks? The one who at that time and on that occasion was the king was I.

children.text: yan mayā pūrṇasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya tādṛśī pūjā kṛtā tena me saṃsāre 'nantaṃ sukham anubhūtam tenaiva ca hetunā tathāgatasya ca me śreṣṭhinā śakreṇa ca īdṛśī pūjā kṛtā
children.translated_text: Because I performed such worship for <s>Pūrṇa</s>, the perfectly awakened Buddha, I experienced endless happiness in saṃsāra; and for that very reason such worship was performed for me, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, by the guild-master and by <s>Śakra</s>.

children.text: tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam yacchāstāraṃ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, monks, you should train yourselves thus: 'We shall honor the Teacher, highly revere him, esteem him, and worship him.

children.text: śāstāraṃ satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvopaniśritya vihariṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Having honored the Teacher, highly revered him, esteemed him, worshiped him, and relied upon him, we will dwell.'

children.text: ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, should you train yourselves.

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: Those monks, pleased in mind, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.

children.text: Chapter 20

buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho magadheṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ caran gaṅgātīram anuprāptaḥ
children.translated_text: The Buddha, the Blessed One, honored, highly revered, esteemed, and worshiped by kings, royal ministers, wealthy men, townspeople, guild leaders, caravan merchants, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, thus worshiped by gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, known as a Buddha, the Blessed One, of great merit and a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicines and requisites for sickness, together with the community of disciples, while wandering on tour in the lands of <s>Magadha</s>, arrived at the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>.

children.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena gaṅgātīrasya nātidūre stūpam avarugṇaṃ vātātapābhyāṃ pariśīrṇam bhikṣubhir dṛṣṭvā bhagavān pṛṣṭaḥ kasya bhagavann ayaṃ stūpa iti
children.translated_text: At that time, not far from the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, there was a <s>stūpa</s> broken down and decayed by wind and sun. Seeing it, the monks asked the Blessed One, 'Blessed One, whose <s>stūpa</s> is this?'

children.text: bhagavān āha candano nāma pratyekabuddho babhūva tasyeti
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, 'There was a pratyekabuddha named <s>Candana</s>; it is his.'

children.text: bhikṣava ūcuḥ kuto bhagavaṃś candanasya pratyekabuddhasyotpattir nāmābhinirvṛttiś ceti
children.translated_text: The monks said, 'Blessed One, what was the origin of <s>Candana</s> the pratyekabuddha, and how did his name come to be?'

children.text: bhagavān āha icchatha yūyaṃ bhikṣavaḥ śrotuṃ yathā candanasya pratyekabuddhasyotpattir nāmābhinirvṛttiś ca evaṃ bhadanta
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, 'Do you wish, monks, to hear how <s>Candana</s> the pratyekabuddha arose and how his name came to be?' 'Yes, venerable sir.'

children.text: tena hi bhikṣavaḥ śṛṇuta sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuruta bhāṣiṣye ||
children.translated_text: 'Then listen, monks, and bear it well and carefully in mind. I will speak.'

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ brahmadatto nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca praśāntakalikalahaḍimbaḍamaraṃ taskararogāpagataṃ śālīkṣugomahiṣīsampannam
children.translated_text: Once, monks, in the past, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a king named <s>Brahmadatta</s> ruled a kingdom that was prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, filled with many people, with strife, quarrels, tumults, and disturbances pacified, free from robbers and disease, and endowed with rice, sugarcane, cows, and buffaloes.

children.text: dhārmiko dharmarājo dharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayati
children.translated_text: He was righteous, a king of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), and he ruled by <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: so 'putraḥ putrābhinandī śivavaruṇakuberaśakrabrahmādīn anyāṃś ca devatāviśeṣān āyācate tadyathā ārāmadevatā vanadevatāś catvaradevatāḥ śṛṅgāṭakadevatā balipratigrāhikā devatāḥ
children.translated_text: Being sonless and longing for a son, he entreated <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and other particular deities, namely garden deities, forest deities, deities of squares, deities of crossroads, and deities who receive offerings.

children.text: sahajāḥ sahadhārmikā nityānubaddhā api devatā āyācate
children.translated_text: He also entreated the deities who were born together with him, shared his destiny, and were always attached to him.

children.text: asti caiṣa loke pravādo yadāyācanahetoḥ putrā jāyante duhitaraś ca
children.translated_text: And there is this common saying in the world, that sons and daughters are born because of entreaty.

children.text: tac ca naivam
children.translated_text: But that is not so.

children.text: yady evam abhaviṣyad ekaikasya putrasahasram abhaviṣyat tadyathā rājñaś cakravartinaḥ
children.translated_text: If this were so, each person would have had a thousand sons, just like a wheel-turning king.

children.text: api tu trayāṇāṃ sthānānāṃ saṃmukhībhāvāt putrā jāyante duhitaraś ca
children.translated_text: Rather, sons and daughters are born through the conjunction of three conditions.

children.text: katameṣāṃ trayāṇām
children.translated_text: Which three?

children.text: mātāpitarau raktau bhavataḥ saṃnipatitau mātā ca kalyā bhavati ṛtumatī gandharvaś ca pratyupasthito bhavati
children.translated_text: The mother and father are passionate and have come together, the mother is in season and fertile, and a <s>gandharva</s> (being to be reborn) is present.

children.text: eṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ sthānānāṃ saṃmukhībhāvāt putrā jāyante duhitaraś ca
children.translated_text: Through the conjunction of these three conditions, sons and daughters are born.

children.text: sa caivam āyācanaparas tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: And he remained intent upon entreaty in just this way.

children.text: tasya codyāne mahāpadmini tatra padmam atipramāṇaṃ jātam
children.translated_text: Then in his garden, in the great lotus pond, an exceptionally large lotus arose.

children.text: tad divase divase vardhate na tu phullati
children.translated_text: Day by day it grew, but it did not bloom.

children.text: tata ārāmikeṇa rājñe niveditam
children.translated_text: Then the gardener reported this to the king.

children.text: rājñā uktaḥ parīkṣyatām etat padmam iti
children.translated_text: The king said, 'Let this lotus be examined.'

children.text: yāvad apareṇa samayena sūryodaye tat padmaṃ vikasitam
children.translated_text: Then at another time, at sunrise, that lotus opened.

children.text: tasya ca padmasya karṇikāyāṃ dārakaḥ paryaṅkaṃ baddhvāvasthitaḥ abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko gauraḥ kanakavarṇaś chatrākāraśirāḥ pralambabāhur vistīrṇalalāṭaḥ uccaghoṣaḥ saṃgatabhrūs tuṅganāsaḥ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtagātro 'śītyānuvyañjanair virājitagātraḥ
children.translated_text: And in the pericarp of that lotus a boy was seated cross-legged: handsome, lovely to behold, pleasing, fair, golden-colored, with a head shaped like a parasol, long arms, a broad forehead, a deep voice, joined eyebrows, a prominent nose, his body adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man and radiant with the eighty minor marks.

children.text: tasya mukhāt padmagandho vāti śarīrācca candanagandhaḥ
children.translated_text: From his mouth came the fragrance of a lotus, and from his body the fragrance of sandalwood.

children.text: tata ārāmikeṇa rājñe niveditam
children.translated_text: Then the gardener reported this to the king.

children.text: tato rājā sāmātyaḥ sāntaḥpuraś ca tad udyānaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: Thereupon the king, together with his ministers and his inner court, went to that garden.

children.text: sahadarśanāt tena dārakeṇa rājā saṃbhāṣitaḥ ehi tāta ahaṃ te 'putrasya putra iti
children.translated_text: As soon as he saw him, that boy addressed the king: 'Come, father. I am a son to you who have no son.'

children.text: tato rājā hṛṣṭatuṣṭapramudita uvāca evam eva putra yathā vadasīti
children.translated_text: Then the king, delighted, satisfied, and overjoyed, said, 'So it is, my son, just as you say.'

children.text: tato rājā padminīm avagāhya taṃ dārakaṃ padmakarṇikāyāṃ gṛhītvā pāṇitale sthāpitavān
children.translated_text: Then the king entered the lotus pond, took that boy from the lotus pericarp, and placed him on the palm of his hand.

children.text: yatra yatra sa dārakaḥ pādau sthāpayati tatra tatra padmāni prādurbhavanti
children.translated_text: Wherever that boy set his feet, lotuses appeared there.

children.text: tatas tasya candana iti nāma kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Then he was given the name <s>Candana</s>.

children.text: yadā candano dārako 'nupūrveṇa mahān saṃvṛttaḥ tadā nāgarai rājā vijñaptaḥ ihāsmākaṃ deva nagaraparva pratyupasthitam
children.translated_text: When the boy <s>Candana</s> had gradually grown up, the townspeople petitioned the king: 'Your Majesty, our city festival has arrived here.

children.text: tad arhati devaś candanaṃ kumāram utsraṣṭum
children.translated_text: Therefore Your Majesty should release prince <s>Candana</s>.'

children.text: rājāha evam astv iti
children.translated_text: The king said, 'So be it.'

children.text: tataś candanaḥ sarvālaṃkāravibhūṣito 'mātyaputraparivṛto vividhair vādyair vādyamānai rājakulād bahir upayāti nagaraparva pratyanubhavitum
children.translated_text: Then <s>Candana</s>, adorned with all ornaments and surrounded by the sons of ministers, went out from the royal palace while various instruments were being played, in order to experience the city festival.

children.text: tatra tasya gacchataḥ padavinyāse padavinyāse padmāni prādurbhavanti darśanīyāni manoramāṇi ca
children.translated_text: As he went there, at every placement of his feet, beautiful and delightful lotuses appeared.

children.text: tāny arkaraśmibhiḥ spṛṣṭamātrāṇi mlāyanti śuṣyanti ||
children.translated_text: As soon as they were touched by the rays of the sun, they withered and dried up.

children.text: atha tasya śuddhasattvasya kalyāṇāśayasya pūrvabuddhāvaropitakuśalamūlasya taddarśanād yoniśo manasikāra utpannaḥ yathemāni padmāni utpannamātrāṇi śobhante arkaraśmiparitāpitāni mlāyanti śuṣyanti evam etad api śarīram iti
children.translated_text: Then, in that pure being of wholesome intention, whose roots of good had been planted under former Buddhas, right attention arose from seeing that: 'Just as these lotuses, as soon as they have arisen, are beautiful, but when scorched by the rays of the sun wither and dry up, so too is this body.'

children.text: tasyaivaṃ cintayatas tulayata uparīkṣamāṇasya saptatriṃśad bodhipakṣyadharmā abhimukhībhūtāḥ
children.translated_text: As he thought, weighed, and examined in this way, the thirty-seven <s>bodhipakṣya-dharmas</s> (factors conducive to awakening) became present before him.

children.text: tena tasyaiva janakāyasya madhye sthitena pratyekabodhiḥ sākṣātkṛtā
children.translated_text: Standing there in the midst of that very crowd of people, he realized pratyekabodhi.

children.text: yāvacchuddhāvāsakāyikair devais tasmai kāṣāyāṇy upanāmitāni
children.translated_text: Then gods belonging to the Pure Abodes brought him ocher robes.

children.text: tāni ca prāvṛtya gaganatalam utpatitaḥ vicitrāṇi ca prātihāryāṇi kartuṃ pravṛttaḥ yaddarśanād rājñāmātyanaigamasahāyena mahān prasādaḥ pratilabdho vicitrāṇi ca kuśalamūlāny avaropitāni
children.translated_text: Having put them on, he rose into the sky and began to perform various miracles; from seeing them, the king, together with his ministers, townspeople, and companions, obtained great faith and planted various roots of good.

children.text: bhagavān āha ataś candanasya pratyekabuddhasyotpattirnāmābhinirvṛttiś ceti ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, 'Thus was the arising of <s>Candana</s> the pratyekabuddha and the origin of his name.'

children.text: bhikṣavo bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ kāni bhadanta candanena pratyekabuddhena karmāṇi kṛtāni yenāsya śarīraṃ sugandhi tīkṣṇendriyaś ceti
children.translated_text: The monks asked the Blessed One, 'Venerable sir, what deeds were done by <s>Candana</s> the pratyekabuddha, because of which his body was fragrant and his faculties sharp?'

children.text: bhagavān āha kāśyape bhagavati pravrajito babhūva tatrānena keśanakhastūpe gandhāvasekaḥ kṛtaḥ puṣpāṇi cāvaropitāni pratyekabodhau cānena mārgo bhāvitaḥ
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, 'He had gone forth under the Blessed One <s>Kasyapa</s>. There he poured fragrant water over a stupa of hair and nails, planted flowers, and cultivated the path to pratyekabodhi.

children.text: tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam yacchāstāraṃ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, monks, you should train yourselves thus: We shall honor the Teacher, revere him highly, esteem him, and worship him.

children.text: śāstāraṃ satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvopaniśritya vihariṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Having honored the Teacher, revered him highly, esteemed him, worshiped him, and relied upon him, we shall dwell.

children.text: ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, should you train yourselves.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: Those monks, pleased in mind, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.

children.text: Chapter 21

buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme
children.translated_text: The Buddha, the Blessed One, honored, highly revered, esteemed, and worshiped by kings, royal ministers, wealthy men, townspeople, guild leaders, caravan merchants, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, thus worshiped by gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, known as the Buddha, the Blessed One, of great merit, and a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicines and requisites for sickness, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s> in <s>Jetavana</s>, in <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>'s park.

children.text: ācaritam etan madhyadeśe yadārāmikāḥ padmāny ādāya vīthīṃ gatvā vikrīṇate
children.translated_text: This is the custom in <s>Madhyadeśa</s>: monastery attendants take lotuses, go into the street, and sell them.

children.text: atha bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya śrāvastīṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, having dressed in the morning and taken his bowl and robe, entered <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms.

children.text: anyatamā ca strī dārakaṃ svabhujābhyām ādāya vīthīm avatīrṇā
children.translated_text: And a certain woman, carrying a boy in her two arms, had gone down into the street.

children.text: dadarśa ca sa dārako buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam
children.translated_text: That boy saw the Buddha, the Blessed One, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great person, his body shining with the eighty secondary signs, adorned with a fathom-wide aura, with a radiance surpassing a thousand suns, like a moving mountain of jewels, altogether auspicious.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ prasādajātaḥ sahasā bāhum abhiprasārya ārāmikasakāśāt padmaṃ gṛhītvā bhagavato mūrdhni prakṣiptavān
children.translated_text: Having seen him, and with faith arisen in him, he suddenly stretched out his arm, took a lotus from the monastery attendant, and threw it onto the Blessed One's head.

children.text: tatas tat padmaṃ śakaṭacakramātraṃ bhūtvopari vihāyasi sthitam
children.translated_text: Thereupon that lotus became as large as a cartwheel and stood above him in the sky.

children.text: bhagavantaṃ ca gacchantam anugacchati tiṣṭhantaṃ tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: When the Blessed One went, it followed him; when he stood still, it stood still.

children.text: tato bhagavatā padmarāgasadṛśā prabhā utsṛṣṭā sakalā śrāvastī avabhāsitā taddhaitukaṃ ca rājāmātyapaurāḥ āvarjitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then a radiance like padmarāga was emitted by the Blessed One, and all <s>Śrāvastī</s> was illuminated; because of that, the king, ministers, and townspeople were drawn there.

children.text: tato bhagavatā smitam upadarśitam
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One displayed a smile.

children.text: dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhān niścārya kāścid adhastād gacchanti kāścid upariṣṭād gacchanti
children.translated_text: It is indeed the nature of things that, at the time when Blessed Ones reveal a smile, blue, yellow, red, and white rays issue from their mouths; some go downward, and some go upward.

children.text: yā adhastād gacchanti tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanam avīcim arbudaṃ nirarbudaṃ aṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvam utpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaṃ narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakās teṣu śītībhūtā nipatanti ye śītanarakās teṣūṣṇībhūtā nipatanti
children.translated_text: Those that go downward, having gone to the hells <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s>, fall as cool in the hot hells and as warm in the cold hells.

children.text: tena teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante
children.translated_text: Through that, the particular torments of those beings are pacified.

children.text: teṣām evaṃ bhavati kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ āhosvid anyatropapannā iti
children.translated_text: They think, 'Have we, sirs, died from here, or have we been reborn somewhere else?'

children.text: teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati
children.translated_text: In order to produce faith in them, the Blessed One sends forth a created apparition.

children.text: teṣāṃ nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavati na hy eva vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ nāpy anyatropapannāḥ
children.translated_text: When they see the apparition, they think, 'Surely we have not died from here, nor have we been reborn somewhere else.

children.text: api tv ayam apūrvadarśanaḥ sattvaḥ asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti
children.translated_text: Rather, this being, never seen before, has by his power pacified our particular torments.'

children.text: te nirmite cittam abhiprasādya tan narakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇanti yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti
children.translated_text: Having made their minds faithful toward the apparition, they exhaust the karma to be experienced in hell and take rebirth among gods and humans, where they become vessels for the truths.

children.text: yā upariṣṭād gacchanti tāś cāturmahārājikāṃs trayastriṃśān yāmāṃs tuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhān apramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān abṛhān atapān sudṛśān sudarśanān akaniṣṭhān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmety udghoṣayanti gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante
children.translated_text: Those that go upward, having gone to the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s>, <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>, <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, <s>Parīttābha</s>, <s>Apramāṇābha</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, <s>Abṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods, proclaim, 'Impermanent, painful, empty, without self,' and speak two verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane
children.translated_text: 'Begin! Go forth! Apply yourselves in the Buddha's teaching.

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāram iva kuñjaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Shake off the army of Death, as an elephant shakes off a reed hut.

children.text: yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati
children.translated_text: For whoever will live diligently in this Dharma and Vinaya

children.text: prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: will abandon the cycle of birth and make an end of suffering.'

children.text: atha tā arciṣas trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātum anvāhiṇḍya bhagavantam eva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti
children.translated_text: Then those rays, having wandered through the three-thousand-great-thousand world system, follow along behind the Blessed One, just behind him.

children.text: tad yadi bhagavān atītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante
