children.translated_text: If the Blessed One wishes to predict past karma, they disappear behind the Blessed One.

children.text: anāgataṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati purastād antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the future, they disappear in front of him.

children.text: narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pādatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth in hell, they disappear at the soles of his feet.

children.text: tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pārṣṇyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as an animal, they disappear at his heels.

children.text: pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as a preta, they disappear at his big toe.

children.text: manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati jānunor antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as a human, they disappear at his knees.

children.text: balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict kingship as a <s>balacakravartin</s> (mighty wheel-turning monarch), they disappear in his left palm.

children.text: cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict wheel-turning kingship, they disappear in his right palm.

children.text: devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati nābhyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth among the gods, they disappear at his navel.

children.text: śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati āsye 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict <s>śrāvakabodhi</s> (disciple-awakening), they disappear at his mouth.

children.text: pratyekabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati ūrṇāyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: When he wishes to predict pratyekabodhi, they disappear into the <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft of hair between the eyebrows).

children.text: anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati uṣṇīṣe antardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: When he wishes to predict unsurpassed perfect awakening, they disappear into the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (cranial protuberance).

children.text: atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata ūrṇāyām antarhitāḥ
children.translated_text: Then those rays of flame circumambulated the Blessed One three times and vanished into the Blessed One's <s>ūrṇā</s>.

children.text: athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with hands joined, asked the Blessed One:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro vaktrāntarān niṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ
children.translated_text: "A cluster, variegated with thousands of many colors, has issued from the opening of your mouth;

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantād divākareṇodayatā yathaiva ||
children.translated_text: by it the directions all around have been illuminated, just as by the sun when it rises."

children.text: gāthāś ca bhāṣate
children.translated_text: And he recites verses:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā buddhā jagaty uttamahetubhūtāḥ
children.translated_text: "The Buddhas, free from becoming, with dejection and pride abandoned, are the supreme cause in the world;

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ smitam upadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Jinas</s>, conquerors of their enemies, do not display without cause a smile white as conch and lotus fiber.

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayam adhigamya vīra buddhyā śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām
children.translated_text: Having yourself discerned at that moment, with heroic wisdom, O hero, O ascetic, O lord of <s>Jinas</s>, what the hearers long to know,

children.text: dhīrābhir munivṛṣa vāgbhir uttamābhirutpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: O bull among sages, remove the arisen doubt with your steady, excellent, auspicious words.

children.text: nākasmāllavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ saṃbuddhāḥ smitam upadarśayanti nāthāḥ
children.translated_text: The protectors, the perfectly awakened ones, firm as the salty ocean and the king of mountains, do not display a smile without reason.

children.text: yasyārthe smitam upadarśayanti dhīrāstaṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The purpose for which the steadfast ones display a smile: these crowds of people long to hear that."

children.text: bhagavān āha evam etad ānanda evam etat
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>; so it is.

children.text: nāhetvapratyayam ānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti
children.translated_text: <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Tathāgatas</s>, arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas do not reveal a smile without cause and without condition.

children.text: paśyasy ānanda anena dārakeṇa prasādajātena tathāgatasya padmaṃ kṣiptam
children.translated_text: Do you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, that this boy, being filled with faith, has thrown a lotus to the <s>Tathāgata</s>?"

children.text: evaṃ bhadanta
children.translated_text: "Yes, venerable sir."

children.text: eṣa ānanda dārako 'nena kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca pañcadaśa kalpān vinipātaṃ na gamiṣyati
children.translated_text: "<s>Ānanda</s>, by this root of good, by this arising of intention, and by the giving up of this <s>deyadharma</s> (religious gift), this boy will not go to a state of ruin for fifteen eons.

children.text: divyamānuṣasukham anubhūya padmottaro nāma pratyekabuddho bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: After experiencing divine and human happiness, he will become a pratyekabuddha named <s>Padmottara</s>.

children.text: ayam asya deyadharmo yo mamāntike cittaprasādaḥ
children.translated_text: This is his <s>deyadharma</s>: the faith of mind that he has in my presence.

children.text: tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam yad buddhapratyekabuddhaśrāvakeṣu kārān kariṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, monks, you should train yourselves thus: 'We shall perform acts of honor toward Buddhas, pratyekabuddhas, and disciples.'

children.text: ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, should you train yourselves."

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: Those monks, pleased in mind, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.

children.text: Chapter 22

buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho rājagṛhe viharati veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe
children.translated_text: The Buddha, the Blessed One, honored, highly revered, esteemed, and worshiped by kings, royal ministers, wealthy men, townspeople, guild leaders, caravan merchants, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, thus worshiped by gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, known as a Buddha, the Blessed One, of great merit and a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicines and requisites for sickness, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in <s>Veṇuvana</s>, at <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s>.

children.text: rājagṛhe 'nyatamaḥ sārthavāho mahāsamudram avatīrṇaḥ
children.translated_text: In <s>Rājagṛha</s>, a certain caravan merchant had set out upon the great ocean.

children.text: tasya bhāryā yauvanavatī
children.translated_text: His wife was youthful.

children.text: sā svāmino 'rthe utkaṇṭhati paritapyati na cāsyā bhartā āgacchati
children.translated_text: She longed for her husband and was tormented on his account, but her husband did not come.

children.text: tayā nārāyaṇasya praṇipatya pratijñātam yadi me śīghram āgacchati ahaṃ te sauvarṇacakraṃ pradāsyāmīti
children.translated_text: Having bowed down to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, she made a vow: "If he comes back to me quickly, I will give you a golden discus."

children.text: tatas tasyāḥ svāmī svastikṣemābhyāṃ mahāsamudrād āśu pratyāgataḥ
children.translated_text: Then her husband soon returned from the great ocean safe and sound.

children.text: tayā sauvarṇacakraṃ kāritam
children.translated_text: She had a golden discus made.

children.text: sā dāsīgaṇaparivṛtā cakram ādāya gandhadhūpapuṣpaṃ ca devakulaṃ sampratiṣṭhitā ||
children.translated_text: Surrounded by a group of maidservants, she took the discus, together with perfume, incense, and flowers, and set out for the temple.

children.text: atrāntare nāsti kiṃcid buddhānāṃ bhagavatām ajñātam adṛṣṭam aviditam avijñātam
children.translated_text: Meanwhile there is nothing at all unknown, unseen, unrecognized, or uncomprehended by the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.

children.text: dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahākāruṇikānāṃ lokānugrahapravṛttakānām ekārakṣāṇāṃ śamathavipaśyanāvihāriṇāṃ tridamathavastukuśalānāṃ caturoghottīrṇānāṃ caturṛddhipādacaraṇatalasupratiṣṭhitānāṃ caturṣu saṃgrahavastuṣu dīrgharātrakṛtaparicayānāṃ pañcāṅgaviprahīṇānāṃ pañcagatisamatikrāntānāṃ ṣaḍaṅgasamanvāgatānāṃ ṣaṭpāramitāparipūrṇānāṃ saptabodhyaṅgakusumāḍhyānām aṣṭāṅgamārgadeśikānāṃ navānupūrvavihārasamāpattikuśalānāṃ daśabalabalināṃ daśadiksamāpūrṇayaśasāṃ daśaśatavaśavartiprativiśiṣṭānāṃ trī rātres trir divasasya ca buddhacakṣuṣā lokaṃ vyavalokya jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate ko hīyate ko vardhate kaḥ kṛcchraprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃkaṭaprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃbādhaprāptaḥ kaḥ kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasaṃbādhaprāptaḥ ko 'pāyanimnaḥ ko 'pāyapravaṇaḥ ko 'pāyaprāgbhāraḥ
children.translated_text: For this is the nature of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones: they are greatly compassionate, active for the benefit of the world, sole protectors, dwelling in calm and insight, skilled in the three bases of taming, crossed beyond the four floods, their feet well established on the four bases of miraculous power, long practiced in the four means of gathering, free from the five components, beyond the five destinies, endowed with six factors, fulfilled in the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), rich with the flowers of the seven factors of awakening, teachers of the eightfold path, skilled in attaining the nine successive abidings, strong with the strength of the ten powers, their fame filling the ten directions, surpassing ten hundreds of <s>Vaśavartin</s> gods; three times by night and three times by day, after surveying the world with the Buddha-eye, their knowledge and vision arise: who is declining, who is increasing, who has fallen into hardship, who has fallen into danger, who has fallen into confinement, who has fallen into hardship, danger, and confinement, who slopes toward the lower realms, who inclines toward the lower realms, who is turned toward the lower realms?

children.text: kam aham apāyād uddhṛtya svarge mokṣe ca pratiṣṭhāpayeyam kasya kāmapaṅkanimagnasya hastoddhāram anupradadyām kam āryadhanavirahitam āryadhanaiśvaryādhipatye pratiṣṭhāpayeyaṃ kasyājñānatimirapaṭalaparyavanaddhanetrasya jñānāñjanaśalākayā cakṣur viśodhayāmi
children.translated_text: Whom shall I lift up from the lower realms and establish in heaven and liberation? To whom, sunk in the mire of desire, shall I extend a helping hand? Whom, deprived of noble wealth, shall I establish in lordship over the sovereignty of noble wealth? Whose eyes, covered by the mass of the darkness of ignorance, shall I cleanse with the collyrium-stick of knowledge?

children.text: kasyānavaropitāni kuśalamūlāny avaropayeyam kasyāvaropitāni paripācayeyam kasya paripakvāni vimocayeyam
children.translated_text: For whom shall I plant roots of good that have not been planted? For whom shall I ripen those that have been planted? Whom shall I liberate when they have ripened?

children.text: āha ca
children.translated_text: And he says:

children.text: apy evātikramed velāṃ sāgaro makarālayaḥ
children.translated_text: Even the ocean, abode of makaras, might overstep its shore,

children.text: na tu vaineyavatsānāṃ buddho velām atikramet ||
children.translated_text: But a Buddha does not miss the proper occasion for beings, his calves, who are to be trained.

children.text: paśyati bhagavān iyaṃ dārikā maddarśanāt pratyekabodheḥ kuśalamūlāny avaropayiṣyatīti
children.translated_text: The Blessed One saw, "Through seeing me, this girl will plant roots of good for <s>pratyekabodhi</s> (solitary awakening)."

children.text: tataḥ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto rājagṛhaṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat
children.translated_text: Then in the forenoon, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, surrounded by a group of monks and preceded by the community of monks, he entered <s>Rājagṛha</s> for alms.

children.text: athāsau dārikā dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam
children.translated_text: Then that girl saw the Buddha, the Blessed One, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great person, his limbs shining with the eighty secondary marks, adorned with a fathom-wide radiance, brighter than a thousand suns, like a moving mountain of jewels, auspicious from every side.

children.text: sahadarśanācca labdhaprasādā bhavati sauvarṇacakraṃ kṣeptum ārabdhaḥ
children.translated_text: At the very sight she gained faith and began to throw a golden discus.

children.text: tataś ceṭikayā vāryate nāyaṃ nārāyaṇa iti sā vāryamāṇāpi tīvraprasādā āvarjitamānasā buddhasya bhagavata upari sauvarṇacakraṃ nikṣipya gandhamālyaṃ ca dattavatī ||
children.translated_text: Then a maidservant restrained her, saying, "This is not <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>." But though she was being restrained, with intense faith and her mind drawn toward him, she cast the golden discus above the Buddha, the Blessed One, and gave perfume and garlands.

children.text: tato bhagavatā smitaṃ vidarśitam
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One displayed a smile.

children.text: dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhān niścārya kāścid adhastād gacchanti kāścid upariṣṭād gacchanti
children.translated_text: Now it is the nature of things that when Buddhas, Blessed Ones, reveal a smile, then blue, yellow, red, and white rays issue from their mouth; some go downward and some go upward.

children.text: yā adhastād gacchanti tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanam avīcim arbudaṃ nirarbudaṃ aṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvam utpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaṃ narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakās teṣu śītībhūtā nipatanti ye śītanarakās teṣūṣṇībhūtā nipatanti
children.translated_text: Those that go downward go to the hells <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s>; in the hot hells they fall cool, and in the cold hells they fall warm.

children.text: tena teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante
children.translated_text: By that, the special torments of those beings subside.

children.text: teṣām evaṃ bhavati kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ āhosvid anyatropapannā iti
children.translated_text: They think, "Have we, friends, died from here, or have we been reborn somewhere else?"

children.text: teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati
children.translated_text: In order to generate faith in them, the Blessed One sends forth an emanation.

children.text: teṣāṃ taṃ nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavati na hy eva vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ nāpy anyatropapannāḥ
children.translated_text: When they see that emanation, they think, "No, friends, we have not died from here, nor have we been reborn somewhere else.

children.text: api tv ayam apūrvadarśanaḥ sattvaḥ asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti
children.translated_text: Rather, this is a being never seen before; through his power our special torments have subsided."

children.text: te nirmite cittam abhiprasādya tan narakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇanti yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti
children.translated_text: Having made their minds clear with faith in the emanation, they exhaust the karma to be experienced in hell and take rebirth among gods and humans, where they become fit vessels for the truths.

children.text: yā upariṣṭād gacchanti tāś cāturmahārājikāṃs trayastriṃśān yāmāṃs tuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhān apramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān abṛhān atapān sudṛśān sudarśanān akaniṣṭhān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmety udghoṣayanti gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante
children.translated_text: Those that go upward go to the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s>, <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>, <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, <s>Parīttābha</s>, <s>Apramāṇābha</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, <s>Abṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> realms; having gone there, they proclaim, "Impermanent, suffering, empty, without self," and speak two verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane
children.translated_text: "Strive, go forth, apply yourselves in the teaching of the Buddha.

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāram iva kuñjaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Shake off the army of Death as an elephant shakes a reed hut.

children.text: yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati
children.translated_text: For whoever will live heedfully in this <s>dharmavinaya</s> (doctrine and discipline),

children.text: prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: having abandoned the cycle of birth, will make an end of suffering."

children.text: atha tā arciṣas trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātum anvāhiṇḍya bhagavantam eva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti
children.translated_text: Then those rays, after roaming through the three-thousand great-thousand world-system, follow the Blessed One from behind, close behind.

children.text: tad yadi bhagavān atītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If the Blessed One wishes to predict past karma, they disappear behind the Blessed One.

children.text: anāgataṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati purastād antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict future karma, they disappear in front.

children.text: narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pādatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth in hell, they disappear into the soles of his feet.

children.text: tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pārṣṇyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as an animal, they disappear into his heels.

children.text: pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as a <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost), they disappear into his big toe.

children.text: manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati jānunor antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth as a human, they disappear into his knees.

children.text: balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rule as a powerful <s>cakravartin</s> (wheel-turning monarch), they disappear into his left palm.

children.text: cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rule as a <s>cakravartin</s> (wheel-turning monarch), they disappear into his right palm.

children.text: devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati nābhyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict rebirth among the gods, they disappear into his navel.

children.text: śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati āsye 'ntardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict the awakening of a <s>śrāvaka</s> (disciple), they disappear into his mouth.

children.text: pratyekabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati ūrṇāyām antardhīyante
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict <s>pratyekabodhi</s> (solitary awakening), they disappear into the <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft between the eyebrows).

children.text: anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati uṣṇīṣe antardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: If he wishes to predict unsurpassed perfect awakening, they disappear into the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (cranial crest).

children.text: atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata ūrṇāyām antarhitāḥ
children.translated_text: Then those rays circumambulated the Blessed One three times clockwise and disappeared into the Blessed One's <s>ūrṇā</s>.

children.text: athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with hands joined, asked the Blessed One:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro vaktrāntarān niṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ
children.translated_text: "A cluster, variegated with thousands of many colors, has issued from the opening of your mouth;

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantād divākareṇodayatā yathaiva ||
children.translated_text: by it the directions all around have been illuminated, just as by the sun when it rises."

children.text: gāthāś ca bhāṣate
children.translated_text: And he recites verses:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā buddhā jagaty uttamahetubhūtāḥ
children.translated_text: "The Buddhas, free from becoming, with dejection and pride abandoned, are the supreme cause in the world;

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ smitam upadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Jinas</s>, conquerors of their enemies, do not display without cause a smile white as a conch and lotus fiber.

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayam adhigamya vīra buddhyā śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām
children.translated_text: Having yourself discerned at that moment with heroic wisdom, O hero, O ascetic, O lord of <s>Jinas</s>, what the expectant hearers desire,

children.text: dhīrābhir munivṛṣa vāgbhir uttamābhirutpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: O bull among sages, remove with your steady, excellent, auspicious words the doubt that has arisen.

children.text: nākasmāllavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ saṃbuddhāḥ smitam upadarśayanti nāthāḥ
children.translated_text: The protectors, perfectly awakened ones, firm as the salt-water ocean and the king of mountains, do not display a smile for no reason.

children.text: yasyārthe smitam upadarśayanti dhīrāstaṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The crowds of people long to hear the purpose for which the steadfast ones display a smile.

children.text: bhagavān āha evam etad ānanda evam etat
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said, "So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>; so it is.

children.text: nāhetvapratyayam ānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti
children.translated_text: <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Tathāgatas</s>, arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas do not reveal a smile without cause and without condition.

children.text: paśyasy ānanda anayā dārikayā tathāgatasya sauvarṇacakraṃ kṣiptam
children.translated_text: Do you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, that this girl has thrown a golden wheel toward the <s>Tathāgata</s>?"

children.text: evaṃ bhadanta
children.translated_text: "Yes, venerable sir."

children.text: eṣā ānanda dārikā anena kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca pañcadaśa kalpān vinipātaṃ na gamiṣyati divyaṃ mānuṣaṃ sukham anubhūya ca cakrāntaro nāma pratyekabuddho bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: "<s>Ānanda</s>, through this root of good, this arising of intention, and this relinquishing of a religious gift, this girl will not go to a state of downfall for fifteen kalpas; after experiencing divine and human happiness, she will become a <s>pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary Buddha) named <s>Cakrāntara</s>.

children.text: ayam asya deyadharmo yo mamāntike cittaprasādaḥ iti
children.translated_text: This is her religious gift, namely, faith of mind in my presence."

children.text: tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam yad buddhapratyekabuddhaśrāvakeṣu kārān kariṣyāmaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, monks, you should train yourselves thus: 'We shall perform acts of honor toward Buddhas, pratyekabuddhas, and disciples.'

children.text: ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, monks, should you train yourselves."

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said this.

children.text: āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan ||
children.translated_text: Those monks, pleased in mind, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.
